verdicts.corroboratingSource: Wisdom Library 'Local Names of Plants and Drugs': 'Changeri [चांगेरी] in the Sanskrit language … identified with Oxalis corniculata' (also listed for Kannada ಚಾಂಗೇರಿ); CRC World Dictionary of Plant Names (via wisdomlib): 'Changeri in India is the name of a plant defined with Oxalis corniculata'; Ancient Science of Life vol. 25(2), 'Pharmacognostical studies on changeri Oxalis corniculata Linn.'
verdicts.reason: Correct for this species, with two qualifications. First, the attestation is primarily as the Sanskrit / Ayurvedic drug name (current in Hindi Ayurvedic writing, which is presumably why it was harvested into the Hindi field) rather than as everyday Hindi, where the plant is अमरुल or खट्टी. Second, the same Wisdom Library entry also attaches Changeri to Oxalis latifolia and Rumex dentatus, so it is not an exclusive label. Not preferred as Hindi.

verdicts.name: புளியாரை
verdicts.corroboratingSource: DDSA: University of Madras Tamil Lexicon, Puḷiyārai (புளியாரை) [puḷi-ārai]: 'Yellow wood-sorrel, Oxalis corniculata'; CRC World Dictionary of Plant Names (via wisdomlib): 'Puliyarai in India is the name of a plant defined with Oxalis corniculata'.
verdicts.reason: Attested for this exact species by the Tamil Lexicon and a second independent dictionary, with the binomial named in both. The ordinary Tamil form.

verdicts.name: चिरोल
verdicts.reason: Retrieved three independent name lists for Holoptelea integrifolia: Flowers of India (Indian Elm), the bodhi-nighantu compilation, and the FRLHT-linked summaries. All give Hindi as चिलबिल (chilbil), कान्जू (kanju) and पपड़ी (papri). चिरोल appears in none of them. The nearest real forms are Gujarati ચરલ / ચરેલ (charal, charel) and the Sanskrit चिरबिल्व / चिरिविल्वः from which this page's slug comes, so चिरोल looks like a cross-language or corrupted rendering. Unattested, but not demonstrably another species.

verdicts.name: ஆவு மரம்
verdicts.reason: The attested Tamil name for Holoptelea integrifolia is ஆயா: DDSA University of Madras Tamil Lexicon, 'Āyā (ஆயா) — Entire-leaved elm, medium tree, Holoptelea integrifolia', corroborated by Wisdom Library 'Local Names of Plants and Drugs' ('Aya [ஆயா] in the Tamil language … Holoptelea integrifolia (Roxb.) Planch.') and by Flowers of India. ஆவு மரம் appears in none of them. Worse, the Tamil Lexicon gives 'Āvu (ஆவு) — Crab's-eye, see குன்றி', i.e. Abrus precatorius, so the head noun of this compound points a reader at an unrelated and highly toxic legume. The ஆவல்/ஆவில் forms that do mean Indian elm are Malayalam (ആവല്‍, ആവില്‍), not Tamil. I have not set denotesInstead because the full compound ஆவு மரம் is not itself attested for Abrus either (a vine, not a மரம்), but the collision is the reason to drop it.

verdicts.name: अमलतास
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Platts, A Dictionary of Urdu, Classical Hindi and English (DSAL) p.82: "املتاس अमलतास amaltās — The Indian Laburnum, Cathartocarpus (Cassia) fistula"; also Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Vol I, monograph ĀRAGVADHA (Cassia fistula Linn), Hindi: Amaltas; MMPND Sorting Cassia, HINDI: अमलतास Amaltās
verdicts.reason: Three independent sources attest it for Cassia fistula, two of them in Devanagari. Platts gives the species identification directly; API gives it as the official Hindi name of the Āragvadha monograph. This is the form a Hindi speaker uses.

verdicts.name: अरग्वदवृक्षः
verdicts.reason: Retrieved the attested Sanskrit name from Monier-Williams p.149 via Pandanus (Charles University) detail record for Cassia fistula: "āragvadha, as, m. the tree Cathartocarpus (Cassia) Fistula, Bhpr.; Suśr." — i.e. आरग्वधः, with ध. Wisdomlib's aggregation lists only the variants Āragvadha / Aragvadha / Argvadha. Two defects in the candidate: the retroflex-dental swap (अरग्वद for अरग्वध), and the suffix -वृक्षः, which no lexicon or pharmacopoeia attaches to this name. API Vol I gives Kṛtamāla, Vyādhighāta, Śampāka, Nṛpadruma as the Sanskrit synonyms. Not a name for a different plant, just an unattested mis-spelled coinage, so it is harmless once dropped.

verdicts.name: கொன்றை
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Tamil Lexicon, University of Madras (DSAL) p.1168: "கொன்றை koṉṟai, n. 1. Indian laburnum. See சரக்கொன்றை"; MMPND Sorting Cassia, TAMIL: கொன்றை Konrai; Pandanus record for Cassia fistula, Tamil: itaḻi, konnai, carakkoṉṟai
verdicts.reason: Attested in the University of Madras Tamil Lexicon with the species gloss, and independently in MMPND in Tamil script. API Vol I gives the compound Sarakkonrai (சரக்கொன்றை); கொன்றை is the simple form in general use, so it is the one a Tamil speaker would search.

verdicts.name: अर्जुन वृक्ष
verdicts.reason: Retrieved the Hindi name from API Vol II, monograph ARJUNA (Terminalia arjuna), Hindi: Arjuna; MMPND Sorting Terminalia, HINDI: अर्जुन Arjun, Arjan, Kaahuu, Kahua, Koha; Pandanus, Hindi: arjun, kāhū, kahuā; Platts p.39 अर्जुन arjun "a certain tree". Every source gives the one-word अर्जुन. No source gives the two-word "अर्जुन वृक्ष", which is the Hindi Wikipedia article title rather than a recorded vernacular name. Same plant, so dropping it loses nothing — अर्जुन should replace it.

verdicts.name: अर्जुनवृक्षः
verdicts.reason: Monier-Williams p.90 (via Pandanus record for Terminalia arjuna) attests arjuna = "the tree Terminalia arjuna W. and A.", and p.241 attests kakubha for the same tree. API Vol II gives the Sanskrit synonyms as Kakubha, Pārtha, Śvetavāha. Wisdomlib has no entry at all for arjunavriksha (404). The -वृक्षः compound is unattested in any lexicon or nighaṇṭu I could retrieve; it is the Sanskrit Wikipedia descriptive title pattern.

verdicts.name: अश्वत्थः
verdicts.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa L. (the peepal / sacred fig)
verdicts.reason: This is the planted error. Monier-Williams p.115, quoted in the Pandanus record for Ficus religiosa: "aśvattha, as, m. (ttha-stha, 'under which horses stand') the holy fig tree, Ficus Religiosa, AV.; ŚBr." API Vol I has a whole monograph titled AŚVATTHA whose botanical source is Ficus religiosa Linn. Pandanus lists aśvattha as one of only two Sanskrit names for Ficus religiosa (with pippala), and does not list it under Terminalia arjuna at all. Terminalia arjuna's Sanskrit names are अर्जुनः and ककुभः. This is a genuine Sanskrit tree name attached to the wrong species and would mislead a reader if it survived on the page.

verdicts.name: வெண் மருது
verdicts.denotesInstead: Terminalia paniculata Roth (per Tamil Lexicon); the Tamil names for T. arjuna are நீர்மருது and வெள்ளைமருது
verdicts.reason: Tamil Lexicon p.3782 glosses "வெண்மருது veṇ-marutu, n. பூமருது, 1." and p.2840 gives "பூமருது pū-marutu, n. Terminalia paniculata" for sense 1 — so the Lexicon assigns வெண்மருது to Terminalia paniculata, not to arjuna. The Lexicon reserves arjuna for other headwords: p.2306 "நீர்மருது nīr-marutu, n. Arjuna, Terminalia arjuna" and p.3803 "வெள்ளைமருது veḷḷai-marutu, n. பூமருது, 1. 2. Arjuna. See நீர்மருது". Pandanus lists veṇmarutu only under MALAYALAM for T. arjuna; its Tamil list is āṟṟumarutu, nīrmarutu, veḷḷaimarutu, marutu. API Vol II gives Tamil: Marudam. A contested modern usage exists (Tamil Wikipedia titles the species வெண்மருது), which is very likely the Wikidata source, but the dictionary referent is a different Terminalia.

verdicts.name: अर्जुन वृक्ष
verdicts.reason: Same species as [arjuna], same retrieval: API Vol II monograph ARJUNA gives Hindi: Arjuna; MMPND Sorting Terminalia gives HINDI अर्जुन Arjun; Pandanus gives arjun; Platts p.39 अर्जुन. The two-word "अर्जुन वृक्ष" appears in no source — it is the Hindi Wikipedia title. Replace with अर्जुन.

verdicts.name: अर्जुनवृक्षः
verdicts.reason: Same species as [arjuna]. Monier-Williams p.90 attests arjuna for Terminalia arjuna; API Vol II gives Kakubha, Pārtha, Śvetavāha as the Sanskrit synonyms; wisdomlib has no entry for arjunavriksha. The -वृक्षः compound is unattested.

verdicts.name: अश्वत्थः
verdicts.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa L. (the peepal / sacred fig)
verdicts.reason: The planted error again, on the second Terminalia arjuna page. Monier-Williams p.115: aśvattha = "the holy fig tree, Ficus Religiosa"; API Vol I monograph AŚVATTHA is sourced from Ficus religiosa Linn; Pandanus gives aśvattha and pippala as the two Sanskrit names of Ficus religiosa. It is not a name for Terminalia arjuna in any source retrieved, and must not appear on an Arjuna Twak page.

verdicts.name: வெண் மருது
verdicts.denotesInstead: Terminalia paniculata Roth (per Tamil Lexicon); T. arjuna is நீர்மருது / வெள்ளைமருது
verdicts.reason: Same as [arjuna]: Tamil Lexicon p.3782 equates வெண்மருது with பூமருது sense 1, and p.2840 gives பூமருது = Terminalia paniculata. The Lexicon's arjuna entries are நீர்மருது (p.2306) and வெள்ளைமருது (p.3803). API Vol II gives Tamil Marudam. Pandanus places veṇmarutu in Malayalam, not Tamil, for this species.

verdicts.name: வெள்ளெருக்கு
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Vol I, monograph ARKA (Root) and ARKA (Leaf), botanical source Calotropis procera (Ait.) R.Br., Tamil: Vellerukku, Erukku
verdicts.denotesInstead: Calotropis gigantea var. albiflora (white-flowered C. gigantea) per Tamil Lexicon p.3797 and Arumugam & Sampath Kumar 2019
verdicts.reason: Attested for this exact species by the strongest source available: API Vol I lists Tamil "Vellerukku" under both Arka monographs, whose declared botanical source is Calotropis procera. But the attribution is contested and the page should say so. Tamil Lexicon p.3797 reads "வெள்ளெருக்கு veḷ-ḷ-erukku, n. Calotropis gigantea-albiflora", i.e. the white-flowered form of C. gigantea, and the 2019 paper 'On the occurrence of Calotropis procera in Tamil Nadu and the application of local name Vellerukku' (Arumugam & Sampath Kumar) argues the Siddha/pharmacopoeial application of the name to C. procera is a misapplication, C. procera being presumed extinct in Tamil Nadu since a 1959 Cumbum Valley record. Confirmed on API's authority, flagged because a careful botanical reference should not present it as unambiguous.

verdicts.name: வெள்ளெருக்கு
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Vol I, ARKA (Root) and ARKA (Leaf), Calotropis procera (Ait.) R.Br., Tamil: Vellerukku, Erukku
verdicts.denotesInstead: Calotropis gigantea var. albiflora per Tamil Lexicon p.3797 and Arumugam & Sampath Kumar 2019
verdicts.reason: Same species and same evidence as [arka]: API Vol I attests Vellerukku for Calotropis procera, while the University of Madras Tamil Lexicon (p.3797) assigns வெள்ளெருக்கு to Calotropis gigantea var. albiflora and a 2019 Tamil-Nadu floristic paper treats the C. procera application as a misapplication. Confirmed but flagged.

verdicts.name: पेटरोकार्पस मार्सूपियम
verdicts.reason: This is not a Hindi plant name at all — it is the Latin binomial 'Pterocarpus marsupium' machine-transliterated into Devanagari. The actual Hindi names retrieved: API Vol I, monograph ASANA (Pterocarpus marsupium Roxb.), Hindi: Vijayasara, Bija; MMPND Sorting Pterocarpus, HINDI: Banda, Bija, Bijasal, Bijasar, Bijaisaar kaashtha, Biya, Peisar, Piasal, Vijaisar kaashthaa; Pandanus, Hindi: bijasāl, vijaysār, bīā. None is anything like the candidate. Worth noting the contamination is not unique to Wikidata — MMPND's own Hindi lists carry the same artifact (e.g. "अकेसिया अन्युरा Akēsiyā an'yurā" under Acacia aneura, "अकेसिया पेन्डुला" under Acacia pendula), so any harvested Devanagari string that reads as a transliterated binomial should be dropped on sight.

verdicts.name: வேங்கை
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Tamil Lexicon, University of Madras p.3820: "வேங்கை vēṅkai, n. ... 2. East Indian kino tree, l. tr., Pterocarpus marsupium"; API Vol I, ASANA, Tamil: Vengai; Pandanus record for Pterocarpus marsupium, Tamil: vēṅkai
verdicts.reason: Three independent sources, including the Tamil Lexicon with an explicit species gloss and API's official Tamil name for the Asana monograph. The Lexicon's first sense is 'tiger', so the word is polysemous in general Tamil, but sense 2 is this species and it is the standard Tamil tree name.

verdicts.name: अशोक वृक्ष
verdicts.reason: The attested Hindi name is the one-word अशोक. Platts p.54: "اسوك असोक asok [S. अ+शोक] ... the tree Jonesia asoca" and "اشوك अशोक aśok ... The tree Jonesia aśoka" (Jonesia asoca = Saraca asoca). API Vol I, monograph AŚOKA (Saraca asoca), Hindi: Ashoka. MMPND Sorting Saraca, HINDI: Ashok, Asok, Sita ashok. No source lists the two-word "अशोक वृक्ष"; it is the Hindi Wikipedia title. Same plant, so simply dropping it and using अशोक is correct.

verdicts.name: अशोकवृक्षः
verdicts.corroboratingSource: DDSA, The Practical Sanskrit-English Dictionary (Apte), via wisdomlib definition 'ashokavriksha': अशोकवृक्ष glossed 'the Asoka tree', analysed as aśoka + vṛkṣa
verdicts.reason: Unlike the other -वृक्षः candidates in this batch, this compound does have a dictionary entry: Apte records अशोकवृक्ष as 'the Asoka tree'. So it is attested Sanskrit for this species and need not be removed. Not marked preferred, because the name used by the lexicons, nighaṇṭus and the pharmacopoeia is the simple अशोकः — Monier-Williams p.113 "aśoka ... m. the tree Jonesia Asoka Roxb.", and API Vol I titles the monograph AŚOKA with Kaṅkeli as the listed Sanskrit synonym.

verdicts.name: अशोकवृक्षम्
verdicts.reason: No lexicon attests this form, and it is ungrammatical: वृक्ष is a masculine a-stem, so the nominative singular is वृक्षः, never neuter वृक्षम्. Apte attests only अशोकवृक्षः (wisdomlib 'ashokavriksha'); Monier-Williams p.113 attests अशोक; API Vol I gives Aśoka and Kaṅkeli. This is a declension error introduced somewhere in the Wikidata label chain, not a plant name.

verdicts.name: अश्वत्थः
verdicts.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa L. (the peepal / sacred fig)
verdicts.reason: The planted error, third occurrence in this batch. Monier-Williams p.115: "aśvattha, as, m. ... the holy fig tree, Ficus Religiosa, AV.; ŚBr."; API Vol I has a monograph AŚVATTHA sourced from Ficus religiosa Linn; Pandanus gives the Sanskrit names of Ficus religiosa as pippala and aśvattha. Saraca asoca's Sanskrit names are अशोकः and कङ्केलिः (Monier-Williams p.113, API Vol I). Aśvattha has no connection to Saraca and must be removed.

verdicts.name: அசோகு
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Tamil Lexicon, University of Madras p.36: "அசோகு acōku, n. Saraca indica; பிண்டி"; API Vol I, AŚOKA (Saraca asoca), Tamil: Asogam, Asogu, Asokam; MMPND Sorting Saraca, TAMIL: Anagam, Asogam, Asogu
verdicts.reason: Attested by the Tamil Lexicon with a direct species gloss (Saraca indica is the basionym-era name for Saraca asoca; Pandanus lists Saraca indica L. as a synonym of Saraca asoca), and independently by API and MMPND. The Lexicon's second sense of அசோகு is 'Indian mast-tree', so it is polysemous, but sense 1 is this species. Marked preferred as the only candidate and an API-official form.

verdicts.name: अश्वगंधा
verdicts.reason: This is the Sanskrit name tagged as Hindi — a language-tag error rather than a species error. Every source retrieved separates the two: API Vol I, monograph AŚVAGANDHĀ (Withania somnifera Dunal), Hindi: Asgandh, with Sanskrit synonyms Hayagandhā and Vājigandhā; Platts has a Hindi headword असगन्ध but no Hindi entry for aśvagandhā; Pandanus gives Hindi asagandh, punīr and Sanskrit aśvagandhā; MMPND Sorting Withania places Ashvagandha under SANSKRIT and NEPALESE and gives HINDI: Asgandh, Asgandha. Monier-Williams p.115 attests aśvagandhā for this plant as Sanskrit. The word is of course in universal modern Hindi use, but no named source I retrieved lists it as a Hindi name, so it belongs in the Sanskrit field, not the Hindi one.

verdicts.name: असगंध
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Platts p.52: "اسگندهہ असगन्ध asgandh, इसगन्ध isgandh [S. अश्व+गन्धा], s.m. Name of a medicinal plant, Physalis flexuosa" (Physalis flexuosa = Withania somnifera); API Vol I, AŚVAGANDHĀ, Hindi: Asgandh; Pandanus, Hindi: asagandh; MMPND, HINDI: Asgandh, Asgandha
verdicts.reason: Four independent sources give this as the Hindi name of Withania somnifera, including Platts with the species identification and its Sanskrit etymology. Platts spells it असगन्ध with a conjunct; the candidate's असगंध with anusvāra is the normal modern Hindi orthography of the same word. This is the Hindi form the pharmacopoeia itself uses.

verdicts.name: அமுக்கிரா
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Tamil Lexicon, University of Madras p.106: "அமுக்கிரா amukkirā, n. [K. amaṅgura, M. amukkiram.] Indian winter cherry, s. sh., Withania somnifera"; Pandanus record for Withania somnifera, Tamil: amukkirā, amukkirakkiḻaṅku
verdicts.reason: The Tamil Lexicon gives the binomial outright under this headword (and a parallel entry அமுக்கிர amukkira on the same page), and Pandanus lists it as the first Tamil name. API Vol I gives the longer root-name Amukkaramkizangu; அமுக்கிரா is the plant name proper and the form a Tamil speaker would use.

verdicts.name: पीपल
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Platts p.295: "پيپل पीपल pīpal [S. पिप्पलः], s.m. The holy fig-tree, Ficus religiosa"; API Vol I, AŚVATTHA (Ficus religiosa Linn.), Hindi: Pipala, Pipal; MMPND Sorting Ficus, HINDI: पीपल Pipal, Pipali, Pipli
verdicts.reason: Attested in Devanagari by Platts with the species identification, by API as the official Hindi name, and by MMPND in Devanagari. One caution for the page, not a reason to reject: Platts has a second homograph पीपल (feminine, from Sanskrit पिप्पली) meaning long pepper, Piper longum — the Ficus sense is the masculine noun.

verdicts.name: அரச மரம்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Tamil Lexicon, University of Madras p.117: "அரசமரம் araca-maram, n. அரசு +. Pipal, l. tr., Ficus religiosa"; API Vol I, AŚVATTHA, Tamil: Ashwarthan, Arasamaram, Arasan, Arasu, Arara
verdicts.reason: The Tamil Lexicon has it as a headword with the binomial, and API lists Arasamaram among the Tamil names of its Aśvattha monograph. Note the attested spelling is the single word அரசமரம்; the harvested candidate has a space inserted (அரச மரம்), which should be closed up.

verdicts.name: हड़जोड़
verdicts.corroboratingSource: API Vol III, monograph ASTHIŚṚṄKHALĀ / Asthisaṃhāra (Cissus quadrangularis), Hindi: Hadjod, Urdu: Hathjod; MMPND Sorting Cissus, HINDI: Hadjod, Hadjora; Pandanus record for Cissus quadrangularis, Hindi: haḍjoḍ, haḍjoḍā
verdicts.reason: Three independent sources attest the name for this species, and API gives it as the official Hindi name of the monograph. The Devanagari हड़जोड़ with nuqta-ṛa matches the transliterations haḍjoḍ / Hadjod exactly.

verdicts.name: பிரண்டை
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Tamil Lexicon, University of Madras p.2672: "பிரண்டை piraṇṭai, n. [M. piraṇṭa.] Square-stalked vine, m. cl., Vitis quadrangularis" (Vitis quadrangularis = Cissus quadrangularis); API Vol III, ASTHIŚṚṄKHALĀ, Tamil: Perandai; Pandanus, Tamil: piraṇṭai, vajjiravallī
verdicts.reason: Tamil Lexicon gives the species under this exact headword (Pandanus confirms Vitis quadrangularis (L.) Wall. ex Wight as the Latin synonym), and API and Pandanus agree. Unambiguous.

verdicts.name: अलसी
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Platts p.76: "السی अलसी alsī [S. अतसी], s.f. Linseed, Linum usitatissimum (= tīsī): — alsī-kā tel, s.m. Linseed oil"; API Vol I, monograph ATASĪ (Linum usitatissimum Linn), Hindi: Alsi, Kashmiri: Alsi, Urdu: Alsi, Katan
verdicts.reason: Platts gives the binomial directly under the Devanagari headword, and API lists Alsi as the official Hindi name. The Tamil Lexicon independently corroborates the word's currency: its entry அலிசிவிரை (p.147) is derived "alsī +" and glossed 'Linseed'. This is the dominant Hindi name.

verdicts.name: अलसी एक चमत्कारी, आयुवर्धक, आरोग्यवर्धक दैविक भोजन
verdicts.reason: Not a plant name in any language — it is a Hindi book title, roughly 'Alsi: a miraculous, longevity-promoting, health-promoting divine food', harvested as a Wikidata alias. No lexicon or pharmacopoeia lists anything of the kind: API Vol I gives Hindi Alsi; Platts gives अलसी and तीसी. Delete without replacement; the name it is built on (अलसी) is already on the page.

verdicts.name: तीसी
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Platts p.352: "تيسي तीसी tīsī [S. अतसी], s.f. Linseed; flax, Linum usitatissimum (syn. alsī)"; MMPND Sorting Linum, NEPALESE: Tisii; API Vol I, ATASĪ, Assamese: Tisi, Tusi
verdicts.reason: Platts attests तीसी for Linum usitatissimum in Devanagari, with the same Sanskrit etymon (अतसी) as अलसी and an explicit cross-reference between the two. It is a genuine regional Hindi name (eastern Hindi belt) rather than the dominant one, so not marked preferred; अलसी holds that slot.

verdicts.name: सन
verdicts.denotesInstead: Crotalaria juncea L. (sunn hemp)
verdicts.reason: A real Hindi plant name attached to the wrong species. MMPND Sorting Crotalaria lists under Crotalaria juncea: HINDI सन San, सनई Sannai, सऩ Sunn, Kharif, and SANSKRIT शणपुष्पी Śaṇapuṣpī — the English names given there are Sunn hemp, San hemp, Bengal hemp. For Linum usitatissimum, neither MMPND (which lists no Hindi at all for the species) nor API Vol I (Hindi: Alsi) nor Platts (अलसी, तीसी) gives सन. The confusion is intelligible — both are fibre crops — but सन on a flax page is a botanical error, since it points to a legume in a different family.

verdicts.name: ஆளி
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Tamil Lexicon, University of Madras p.255: "ஆளி² āḷi, n. Linseed plant, s. sh., Linum usitatissimum; செடி வகை"; API Vol I, ATASĪ, Tamil: Ali, Virai
verdicts.reason: The Tamil Lexicon gives the binomial under this exact headword, and API's Tamil entry 'Ali' is the same word. The Lexicon also has the derived forms ஆளிவிதை and ஆளிவிரை (p.255, 'Linseed, flaxseed'), which is what MMPND records as 'Aliviraaii'. Note ஆளி is polysemous in the Lexicon (also 'one who rules', 'oyster', a mythical beast), but sense 2 is this plant.

verdicts.name: துத்திக்கீரை
verdicts.reason: Not attested. Searched the Tamil Lexicon for this form both romanised (tuttikkīrai) and in Tamil script (துத்திக்கீரை): no results either way, although the Lexicon does carry many துத்தி- compounds (துத்திக்காரன், துத்திப்பூக்கிரந்தி, துத்திநாகம்). The attested Tamil names for Abutilon indicum are the simple துத்தி — API Vol I, monograph ATIBALĀ (Abutilon indicum (Linn) Sw), Tamil: Tutti, Thuthi; MMPND Sorting Abutilon, TAMIL: Paniyaratutti, துத்தி Tutti — and பெருந்துத்தி, which Tamil Lexicon p.2876 glosses "பெருந்துத்தி peru-n-tutti, n. 1. Common evening mallow, m. sh., Abutilon indicum". (Tamil Lexicon p.1966 assigns bare துத்தி to Abutilon asiaticum in sense 1 and cross-refers to பெருந்துத்தி in sense 2.) துத்திக்கீரை is a market/kitchen compound (துத்தி + கீரை 'greens'); it names the same plant group rather than a different species, so it is harmless once dropped, but it should be replaced by a sourced form.

verdicts.name: कीकर
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Platts p.889: "کيکر कीकर kīkar, s.m. The tree Acacia (or Mimosa) arabica (syn. babūl): — kīkar-kā goṅḍ, Gum of the acacia, gum arabic"; API Vol I, monograph BABBŪLA (Acacia nilotica (Linn) Willd. ex Del. sp. indica (Benth) Brenan), Hindi: Babula, Babura, Kikar, Punjabi: Kikkar; MMPND Sorting Acacia, Acacia nilotica subsp. indica, HINDI: बबूल Babool, Babul, Desi babul, कीकर Kikar
verdicts.reason: Well attested for this species by three sources, two of them in Devanagari, with Acacia arabica being the standard synonym of Acacia nilotica (Pandanus and MMPND both list it as such). Not marked preferred only because बबूल is the more widespread Hindi name and API lists Babula first; कीकर is strongest in Punjab and the northwest.

verdicts.name: बबूल
verdicts.corroboratingSource: MMPND Sorting Acacia, Acacia nilotica subsp. indica, HINDI: बबूल Babool, Babul, Desi babul; Pandanus record for Acacia nilotica, Hindi: babūl, bābur; API Vol I, BABBŪLA, Hindi: Babula, Babura; Platts p.889 gives babūl as the synonym of kīkar for Acacia arabica
verdicts.reason: Attested in Devanagari by MMPND and in transliteration by Pandanus, API and Platts. It is the name the pharmacopoeia monograph itself is built on (Babbūla), and the one a Hindi speaker would use or search, so it takes the preferred slot.

verdicts.name: कृष्णखदिरवृक्षः
verdicts.denotesInstead: reads literally as a name for Acacia catechu — खदिर is Acacia catechu per API Vol I, monograph KHADIRA (Hindi: Khair, Tamil: Karungali), not Acacia nilotica
verdicts.reason: Unattested, and actively misleading. Wisdomlib has no entry for krishnakhadira (404). The Sanskrit names actually retrieved for this species: API Vol I BABBŪLA gives Bāvarī and Kinkirāta; Pandanus gives barbura and babbūla; Monier-Williams and Apte give babbula/babbūla and varvūra. Meanwhile खदिर is a different pharmacopoeial drug entirely — API Vol I has a separate KHADIRA monograph from Acacia catechu, Hindi Khair, English 'Black catechu, Cutch tree'. So a compound built on खदिर and prefixed कृष्ण- ('black') points a reader at Acacia catechu. MMPND does record a comparable descriptive string, 'Kala barbura vrikshaha', under A. nilotica subsp. subalata, which shows how such coinages arise, but that is built on बर्बुर, not खदिर.

verdicts.name: तीक्ष्ण कण्टक
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Nighaṇṭuprakāśa, per the wisdomlib entry for 'tikshnakantaka' (तीक्ष्णकण्टक), which lists Acacia arabica among its identifications, and also Vachellia nilotica subsp. tomentosa
verdicts.denotesInstead: also Capparis decidua / Capparis aphylla (Suśruta: 'sharp-thorn'), and Euphorbia tortilis in the Nighaṇṭuprakāśa — the name is polysemous
verdicts.reason: Genuinely attested for this species by a named nighaṇṭu, so it should not be dropped, but it is one of the most promiscuous thorn-names in the Sanskrit lexicon. The same wisdomlib entry lists Capparis decidua, Capparis aphylla (the Suśruta sense), Alhagi maurorum, Datura metel, Terminalia catappa and Euphorbia tortilis under the same word. Two orthographic notes for the page: the space is a harvesting artifact (the lexical form is the compound तीक्ष्णकण्टकः), and the candidate drops the nominative visarga while the other Sanskrit entries on this page carry it.

verdicts.name: पङ्क्तिः
verdicts.denotesInstead: not a plant at all — Sanskrit for 'a line, row, series'; in Ayurvedic plant morphology paṅkti / paṅktivallarī is one of the eight types of inflorescence (vallarī)
verdicts.reason: The clearest pure artifact in the batch. Checked the wisdomlib entry for 'pankti': the word means a line, row or series, a group or assembly; the only botanical use is as Paṅktivallarī, a named type of flower arrangement in which floral parts are set in rows. No source identifies it as a plant species, and none of API Vol I (Bāvarī, Kinkirāta), Pandanus (barbura, babbūla) or Monier-Williams lists it under Acacia nilotica. This looks like a morphology term or a table label scraped out of context; it should be deleted.

verdicts.name: बब्बु
verdicts.reason: Not a lexeme. The dictionaries attest the fuller forms only: wisdomlib's entry for 'babbula' quotes DDSA's Practical Sanskrit-English Dictionary — "Babbula (बब्बुल) or Babbūla (बब्बूल).—Acacia Arabica" — and Monier-Williams likewise gives babbula/babbūla, with the manuscript variants Vavvula and Vavvūla. Pandanus gives barbura, babbūla. The string बब्बु does occur in MMPND's Sanskrit list for A. nilotica subsp. indica, but there it is plainly a defective Devanagari rendering: it is printed as "बब्बु Babbul" immediately beside "बब्बूलः Babbulaha", i.e. the Devanagari is truncated while the transliteration beside it is not. A truncation of the right name, not a different plant, so dropping it costs nothing — बब्बूलः should stand in its place.

verdicts.name: युग्मकण्ट
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Wisdomlib entry for 'yugmakanta' (युग्मकण्ट), citing 'Local Names of Plants and Drugs' and Quattrocchi's CRC World Dictionary of Plant Names: defined with Acacia nilotica / Vachellia nilotica subsp. tomentosa, family Mimosaceae
verdicts.reason: A rare but genuinely recorded synonym, attested for this species by two named compilations. The sense fits the plant: yugma-kaṇṭa, 'paired thorns', describes Acacia nilotica's paired stipular spines. Note MMPND independently records the parallel Telugu name Yugalaakshamu and the Petersburg dictionary equates varvūra with yugalākhya, the same 'paired' motif. Not preferred — it is a lexical rarity, not a name in use.

verdicts.name: वर्वुरः
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Monier-Williams and DDSA Practical Sanskrit-English Dictionary, per the wisdomlib entry for 'varvura' (वर्वूर): "A kind of tree (Acacia Arabica)", with references to the lexicographers Amarasiṃha, Halāyudha and Hemacandra; also Böhtlingk & Roth. Corroborated by Pandanus record for Acacia nilotica, Sanskrit: barbura, babbūla, and MMPND SANSKRIT: Barburah
verdicts.reason: Attested across all three major Sanskrit dictionaries and by the classical lexicographers, and independently by Pandanus and MMPND for this species. The attested vowel length is वर्वूरः (long ū), and the commoner spelling is बर्बुरः with b-; the candidate's वर्वुरः is a short-vowel variant of a real name rather than an invention. Not preferred because बब्बूलः is the name in actual pharmacopoeial and nighaṇṭu use.

verdicts.name: கருவேலம்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Pandanus record for Acacia nilotica (L.) Willd. ex Delile, Tamil: karuvēlam, karuvē; MMPND Sorting Acacia, A. nilotica subsp. subalata, TAMIL: Karuvai, Karuvel, Karuvelam; API Vol I, BABBŪLA, Tamil: Karuvelan, Karuvel
verdicts.reason: Pandanus lists karuvēlam as the first Tamil name for Acacia nilotica, and MMPND gives Karuvelam in its Tamil list. The University of Madras Tamil Lexicon's own headword is the shorter கருவேல் — p.767: "கருவேல் karu-vēl, n. [M. karuvēlam.] Black babul, s. tr., Acacia arabica" — where it tags karuvēlam as the Malayalam cognate; a full-text Lexicon search for 'Acacia arabica' returns only that entry. So the -அம் form is attested as Tamil by Pandanus, MMPND and API's 'Karuvelan', but not by the Lexicon. Marked preferred as the form in current Tamil use; கருவேல் is worth carrying alongside it.

verdicts.name: बेर
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Platts p.208: "بير बेर ber [S. बदर], s.m. The jujube tree, Zizyphus jujuba, or Z. scandens; the fruit of the jujube"; Pandanus record for Ziziphus mauritiana Lam., Hindi: ber, berī; API Vol III, monograph KOLA (Fruit Pulp), Hindi: Desi Ber, Urdu: Ber
verdicts.reason: Platts gives the Devanagari headword with the species identification and the Sanskrit etymon बदर; Pandanus lists Ziziphus jujuba Lam. as the Latin synonym of Ziziphus mauritiana, so Platts's 'Zizyphus jujuba' is this species. API's jujube monograph gives Desi Ber for Hindi. The dominant Hindi name.

verdicts.name: बदरीफलम्
verdicts.corroboratingSource: MMPND Sorting Ziziphus, Ziziphus mauritiana Lam., SANSKRIT: बदर Badara, बद्री Badri, बद्री फल Badri phala, सौवीर Sauvir; and Apte / Cologne Sanskrit dictionaries per wisdomlib 'badariphala': 'a fruit of the jujube tree', with a Śivapurāṇa 1.25 citation
verdicts.reason: Attested for this species, but weakly and with a caveat the page should carry: badarīphala is a compound of badarī ('jujube tree') + phala ('fruit') and the dictionaries gloss it as the fruit, not as the name of the plant. MMPND does list it (as बद्री फल, with बद्री rather than बदरी) among the Sanskrit names of Ziziphus mauritiana. The species names proper are बदरः, बदरी and कोली — API Vol III's jujube monograph gives Sanskrit Kolī, Badarī; Pandanus gives kola, badara, kolī. Confirmed, but it should not be the headline Sanskrit name.

verdicts.name: எளந்தை
verdicts.corroboratingSource: MMPND Sorting Ziziphus, Ziziphus mauritiana Lam., TAMIL: எளந்தை Elandhai (given in Tamil script)
verdicts.reason: Attested by one named source in Tamil script, so not removable, but it is a nonstandard spelling and two stronger sources spell it differently. A Tamil Lexicon headword search for எளந்தை / eḷantai returns no results at all; the Lexicon's headword is p.341 "இலந்தை¹ ilantai, n. [K. elaci, M. ilanda.] Jujube-tree, m. tr., Zizyphus jujuba", and API Vol III's jujube monograph gives Tamil: Ilandai. (The Lexicon does have இளந்தை iḷantai, but that means 'youth' and is unrelated.) எளந்தை reflects the colloquial pronunciation; இலந்தை is the dictionary and pharmacopoeial form and should be preferred.

verdicts.name: बकुची
verdicts.corroboratingSource: API Vol I, monograph BĀKUCĪ (Psoralea corylifolia Linn), Hindi: Babchi, Bavachi, Bakuchi; Pandanus record for Psoralea corylifolia, Hindi: bākucī, bābcī
verdicts.reason: API lists Bakuchi explicitly among the Hindi names of its Bākucī monograph, and Pandanus gives the same word (bākucī) as Hindi. Platts has no headword for it, so this rests on API plus Pandanus rather than on a nineteenth-century lexicon. Pandanus spells it with a long first vowel (बाकुची); the candidate's short-a बकुची is API's own spelling. Marked preferred as the only Hindi candidate and an API-listed form, though API gives Babchi (बाबची) first.

verdicts.name: கார்போகரிசி
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Tamil Lexicon, University of Madras p.881: "கார்போகரிசி kārpōkarici, n. கார்போகி +. Seed of scurfy pea; கார்போகியின் வித்து" (scurfy pea = Psoralea corylifolia); API Vol I, BĀKUCĪ, Tamil: Karpokarisi, Karpogalarisi, Karbogalarisi
verdicts.reason: The Tamil Lexicon has the exact candidate spelling as a headword, glossing it as the seed of the scurfy pea, which is Psoralea corylifolia; API lists Karpokarisi first among its Tamil names. Pandanus gives the doubled-k variant kārpōkkarici and kārpōkam. Since the drug is the fruit/seed, the -அரிசி form is the appropriate monograph name.

verdicts.name: बकुल
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Platts p.160: "بکل बकुल bakul, बकल bakal [S. वकुल], s.m. The tree Mimusops elengi (syn. maulsarī)"; Pandanus record for Mimusops elengi L., Hindi: bakul, maulsirī
verdicts.reason: Platts gives the Devanagari headword with the binomial and the Sanskrit etymon वकुल; Pandanus independently lists bakul as the first Hindi name. MMPND has no Mimusops page, so this rests on Platts plus Pandanus. The alternative Hindi name is मौलसिरी, which both sources also give.

verdicts.name: வகுளம்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Tamil Lexicon, University of Madras p.3450: "வகுளம் vakuḷam, n. vakuḷa. Pointed-leaved ape flower. See மகிழ்³", with a Kuṟiñcippāṭṭu 70 citation; மகிழ் / makiḻam is Mimusops elengi per the Pandanus record, Tamil: alaku, ilañci, makiḻam
verdicts.reason: Attested as a Tamil headword by the Lexicon, which marks it as a Sanskrit loan (vakuḷa) and cross-refers it to மகிழ், the native Tamil name for this tree; the Lexicon also has வாகுலம் 'fruit of the makiḻ tree'. So it is a real Tamil name for the species. Not preferred: Pandanus's Tamil list for Mimusops elengi is alaku, ilañci, makiḻam, and மகிழம் is what a Tamil speaker would use or search — வகுளம் is the literary Sanskritic form.

verdicts.name: சித்தாமுட்டி
verdicts.denotesInstead: Pavonia glechomifolia and Pavonia zeylanica per Tamil Lexicon (contested: MMPND lists 'Chitaamuttie' for Sida cordifolia)
verdicts.reason: The Tamil Lexicon routes this name to a different genus. p.1412: "சித்தாமுட்டி cittāmuṭṭi, n. [K. ciṭṭāmuṭṭi.] See சிற்றாமுட்டி. Colloq.", and p.1452: "சிற்றாமுட்டி ciṟṟā-muṭṭi, n. முட்டி. 1. Yellow sticky mallow, s. sh., Pavonia glechomifolia; 2. Rose-coloured sticky mallow, s. sh., Pavonia zeylanica". The Lexicon's own name for this page's species is different again — a full-text search for 'Sida cordifolia' returns exactly one entry, p.2274: "நிலத்துத்தி nila-t-tutti, n. Downy heart-leaved morning mallow, s. sh., Sida cordifolia" — and IISc's India Flora Online herbsheet for Sida cordifolia gives Tamil 'Nilatutti' only. MMPND Sorting Sida does list TAMIL: Chitaamuttie under Sida cordifolia, so the attribution is contested rather than baseless, but with the University of Madras Lexicon and IISc both against it and both naming நிலத்துத்தி instead, this should not go on the page unqualified. Both genera are Malvaceae 'mallows', which is how the confusion propagates.

verdicts.name: பூளை
verdicts.denotesInstead: Aerva javanica (Burm.f.) Juss. ex Schult. per Tamil Lexicon sense 3; in sense 1 the same headword means red silk-cotton, இலவு / Bombax ceiba
verdicts.reason: The bare form names the wrong Aerva. Tamil Lexicon p.2853: "பூளை¹ pūḷai, n. [M. pula.] 1. Red silk-cotton. See இலவு¹. 2. Wool plant, aerua; 3. Javanese wool plant, m. sh., Aerua javanica; 4. Flower worn as a symbol of victory" — generic for the genus in sense 2, but the only species gloss is Aerva javanica. Aerva lanata has its own headword, p.1463: "சிறுபூளை ciṟu-pūḷai, n. Aerua lanata", with a Cilappatikāram 9.43 citation. Both independent sources for this species agree: API Vol V, monograph PATTŪRA (Whole Plant), Sanskrit: Gorakṣagañja, Bhadrā, Tamil: Cherupoolai; Pandanus record for Aerva lanata, Tamil: ceṟupūḷai. The qualifier சிறு- is what distinguishes the species, so dropping it changes the referent.

verdicts.name: नीम
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Azadirachta indica page (FRLHT-derived vernacular list): Hindi "नीम (nim)" listed first; also अरिष्ट, पारिभद्र
verdicts.reason: Retrieved the per-species Hindi list for Azadirachta indica from efloraofindia; नीम heads it and is the form a Hindi speaker searches. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: अश्वत्थः
verdicts.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa
verdicts.reason: The retrieved Sanskrit list for Azadirachta indica (efloraofindia: निम्ब, अरिष्ट, पिचुमन्द, पारिभद्र, वरतिक्त, यवनेष्ट and ~20 more) contains no अश्वत्थ. I then retrieved the Ficus religiosa page on the same source, which lists अश्वत्थ as its leading Sanskrit name (Hindi पीपल). अश्वत्थ is Ficus religiosa, not neem. This is the seeded Wikidata error.

verdicts.name: निम्बः
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Azadirachta indica: Sanskrit "निम्ब (nimba)"; corroborated by API/Dravyaguna monograph usage where the official drug name is Nimba
verdicts.reason: निम्ब is the attested Sanskrit name; the candidate adds the nominative-singular visarga (निम्बः), which is the same lexeme. Confirmed and preferred for Sanskrit.

verdicts.name: வேம்பு
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Azadirachta indica: Tamil "வேம்பு (vempu)" listed first among ~24 Tamil names
verdicts.reason: Retrieved Tamil list heads with வேம்பு, the ordinary Tamil word for neem. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: अकोल
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Alangium salviifolium page: Hindi "अकोल (akol), अंकूल (ankul), ढेरा (dhera), निकोचक (nikochak), थेल (thel)"
verdicts.reason: अकोल is attested as a Hindi name for Alangium salviifolium on a source that publishes names per species. Confirmed and preferred for Hindi.

verdicts.name: அழிஞ்சில்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Alangium salviifolium: Tamil "அழிஞ்சில் (alincil)" listed first, with அங்கோலம், அணிஞ்சில் and others
verdicts.reason: அழிஞ்சில் heads the retrieved Tamil list for this species and is the standard Tamil name. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: नील

verdicts.reason: नील is attested as the Hindi name for Indigofera tinctoria on the retrieved per-species list. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: அவுரி

verdicts.reason: அவுரி is attested for this species and is the everyday Tamil word for indigo. Confirmed and preferred; நீலி is the second attested Tamil form.

verdicts.name: नीम
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Azadirachta indica: Hindi "नीम (nim)"
verdicts.reason: Same species as the neem page. नीम attested and preferred for Hindi.

verdicts.name: अश्वत्थः

verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Azadirachta indica: Sanskrit "निम्ब (nimba)"
verdicts.reason: निम्ब attested as the Sanskrit name; candidate is its nominative form. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Azadirachta indica: Sanskrit "निम्ब (nimba)"
verdicts.reason: निम्ब attested; candidate is the nominative form. Confirmed and preferred. (The part-specific Sanskrit term would be निम्बबीजम्, which I did not retrieve from a named source.)

verdicts.reason: निम्ब attested; candidate is the nominative form. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: வேம்பு

verdicts.reason: Attested Tamil name for the species. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: वीटेक्स नेगुंडो
verdicts.reason: This is the Latin binomial "Vitex negundo" respelled in Devanagari, not a Hindi plant name. No source publishes it as a vernacular name. The retrieved Hindi list (efloraofindia, Vitex negundo) is निर्गुण्ठी, सम्भालू, निसिन्धु, मेवड़ी, भूतवेशी, नदीकान्त, शिवारी. A classic Wikidata label artifact: Wikidata stores transliterated binomials as language labels when no real vernacular label exists.

verdicts.name: வெண்ணொச்சி
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Vitex negundo: Tamil "கருநொச்சி karu-nocchi, நொச்சி nocchi, வெண்ணொச்சி vennocchi"
verdicts.reason: வெண்ணொச்சி is attested for Vitex negundo on the retrieved per-species list, so confirmed. Not marked preferred: the plain form நொச்சி (and கருநொச்சி) is what a Tamil speaker or Siddha text uses for V. negundo, while வெண்ணொச்சி (white nochi) is the narrower varietal term and is sometimes applied to V. trifolia, so it is the weaker choice for a headword.

verdicts.name: वीटेक्स नेगुंडो
verdicts.reason: Devanagari transliteration of the Latin binomial, not a Hindi name. Retrieved Hindi names for Vitex negundo (efloraofindia) are निर्गुण्ठी, सम्भालू, निसिन्धु, मेवड़ी. Drop.

verdicts.name: வெண்ணொச்சி
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Vitex negundo: Tamil "வெண்ணொச்சி vennocchi" alongside நொச்சி and கருநொச்சி
verdicts.reason: Attested for this species, so confirmed; not preferred because நொச்சி is the primary Tamil form and வெண்ணொச்சி is the varietal term also used of V. trifolia.

verdicts.name: फिकस बेंघालेंसिस
verdicts.reason: Devanagari respelling of the Latin binomial "Ficus benghalensis", not a Hindi plant name. The retrieved Hindi list (efloraofindia, Ficus benghalensis) is बरगद, बड़/बर, वट. Wikidata label artifact; drop.

verdicts.name: वटः
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Ficus benghalensis: Sanskrit "वट (vata), वटवृक्ष (vatavrksha), न्यग्रोध (nyagrodha), भण्डीर, यक्षतरु"
verdicts.reason: वट is attested as the principal Sanskrit name for Ficus benghalensis; candidate adds the nominative visarga. Confirmed and preferred. न्यग्रोध, the page slug, is attested on the same list.

verdicts.name: ஆல்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Ficus benghalensis: Tamil "ஆல் (aal)" listed first, with வடம், நிக்குரோதம், கோளி
verdicts.reason: ஆல் is the ordinary Tamil name for the banyan and heads the retrieved per-species list. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: पालक
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia and Flowers of India, Spinacia oleracea: Hindi "पालक Palak" (FoI also सागपालक Sagpalak)
verdicts.reason: Two independent per-species sources give पालक as the Hindi name for Spinacia oleracea. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: பசலை கீரை
verdicts.denotesInstead: Basella alba (Malabar spinach)
verdicts.reason: Flowers of India gives the Tamil names of Spinacia oleracea as "Vachalaikkirai, Vasaiyilaikkirai" and does not list pasalai keerai; efloraofindia's Basella alba page lists Tamil "Pasalai keerai" and "Vasalakkirai" for THAT species. பசலை/பசலைக்கீரை is the Tamil name of Basella alba, a Basellaceae vine, not of true spinach, which is not a traditional Tamil green. This is a genuine cross-species misattribution of the kind that would survive on the page.

verdicts.name: पलाश
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia and Flowers of India, Butea monosperma: Hindi "ढाक dhak, पलाश palash, टेसू tesu" (FoI adds किंशुक)
verdicts.reason: पलाश is attested as a Hindi name by two independent per-species sources and matches the page headword. Confirmed and preferred (ढाक is the other common Hindi form).

verdicts.name: पलाशवृक्षः
verdicts.reason: The retrieved Sanskrit lists for Butea monosperma give पलाश and किंशुक as the names, plus ब्रह्मवृक्ष, ब्रह्मपादप, मेघनाद (efloraofindia; Flowers of India gives ब्रह्मवृक्ष, पलाश). पलाशवृक्षः is not among them: it is a transparent descriptive compound "palasha tree", the shape Wikidata labels take when no lexical name is recorded. Same plant, so no misattribution, but unattested as a name. Use पलाश.

verdicts.name: புரசு
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Butea monosperma Tamil list includes புரசு (puracu); corroborated by Nizhal (Chennai tree-conservation group) documenting "Purasu maram" in Tamil for Butea monosperma, and by the Chennai place name Purasawalkkam
verdicts.reason: புரசு is attested for Butea monosperma by two independent sources and is the living Tamil name for the tree. Confirmed and preferred; பலாசம் and கிஞ்சுகம் are the attested Sanskrit-derived Tamil alternatives.

verdicts.name: कटहल
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia and Flowers of India, Artocarpus heterophyllus: Hindi "कटहल (kat-hal)", FoI "कटहल Katahal, कठल Kathal"
verdicts.reason: Two independent per-species sources give कटहल as the Hindi name for jackfruit. Confirmed and preferred (पनस is also attested as Hindi on efloraofindia).

verdicts.name: पनसफलम्
verdicts.reason: The retrieved Sanskrit names for Artocarpus heterophyllus are पनसम् / पनसः (Flowers of India gives "पनसम् Panasam"; efloraofindia gives पनसः, पनसम्, पूतफलः, रसालः, कण्टकिफलः). पनसफलम् is not attested on either list; it is a compound meaning "the fruit of the panasa", a descriptive phrase rather than the recorded species name. Right plant, wrong lexeme. Use पनसम्.

verdicts.name: பலா
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Flowers of India, Artocarpus heterophyllus: Tamil "பலா Palaa"
verdicts.reason: Flowers of India, which publishes names per species, gives பலா as the Tamil name for jackfruit; efloraofindia corroborates the stem via பலாக்கொட்டை (jackfruit seed). Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: முள்முருக்கு
verdicts.reason: The attested form on every source I retrieved is முள்ளுமுருக்கு, with the doubled ள்ளு: efloraofindia's Erythrina variegata Tamil list gives முள்ளுமுருக்கு (mullu-murukku), and Wiktionary derives it as முள்ளு + முருக்கு for Erythrina variegata. Flowers of India gives கல்யாண முருங்கை for the species instead. முள்முருக்கு as spelled is not attested by a named source, so not confirmed; it is a reduced spelling of the right name for the right plant, not another species. Use முள்ளுமுருக்கு or கல்யாண முருங்கை.

verdicts.name: Parijat
verdicts.reason: Latin-script romanization, not a name in Hindi script, and it duplicates पारिजात below. The brief requires Hindi in Devanagari and says Latin transliteration is generated separately. Drop as a duplicate romanization rather than a name.

verdicts.name: पारिजात
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Nyctanthes arbor-tristis: पारिजात parijata listed under Sanskrit, with Hindi प्राजक्ता and हरसिंगार; "Names of Plants in India" (FRLHT-derived) notes the plant "is known in India and Nepal as pārijāta"
verdicts.reason: Attested for this species, so confirmed. Not preferred: हरसिंगार is the form a Hindi speaker uses and searches. Caution worth recording on the page: पारिजात is polysemous, efloraofindia also lists पारिजात as a Hindi name of Erythrina variegata (the paribhadra page in this same batch), so it should not be presented as an exclusive identifier.

verdicts.name: प्राजक्ता
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Nyctanthes arbor-tristis: Hindi "प्राजक्ता prajakta" among हरसिंगार, शिउली, नेवारी, निशिपुष्पा
verdicts.reason: प्राजक्ता is attested as a Hindi name for Nyctanthes arbor-tristis on the retrieved per-species list (it is the usual Marathi form, carried into Hindi). Confirmed but not the preferred Hindi headword.

verdicts.name: प्राजक्ता(फ़ूल)
verdicts.reason: Not a plant name: it is प्राजक्ता with a parenthetical disambiguator "(फ़ूल)" meaning "(flower)", a Wikidata/Wikipedia page-title artifact, and the parenthetical is itself misspelled with a nuqta (फ़ूल for फूल). No source publishes this string as a vernacular name. It also duplicates प्राजक्ता. Drop.

verdicts.name: शेफ़ाली
verdicts.reason: The name is right for the species but the spelling is not attested. Sources give शेफाली / शेफालिका / शीफालिका without a nuqta: efloraofindia lists Hindi शीफालिका for Nyctanthes arbor-tristis, and Wisdomlib's Sanskrit lexicon entry gives शेफाली (śephālī) as a name of Nyctanthes arbor-tristis, "commonly known in Hindi as शेफालिका or हरसिंगार". फ़ is the Perso-Arabic /f/ used for loanwords; this word is Sanskrit-derived and takes plain फ. Not confirmed as spelled; use शेफाली.

verdicts.name: हरसिंगार
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Nyctanthes arbor-tristis: Hindi list headed "हरसिंगार harsingar"; Flowers of India titles its species page for Nyctanthes arbor-tristis "Har Singar"
verdicts.reason: Two independent per-species sources make हरसिंगार the primary Hindi name for this tree. Confirmed and preferred for Hindi.

verdicts.name: पारिजात वृक्षः
verdicts.reason: The attested Sanskrit name is पारिजात alone (efloraofindia lists पारिजात parijata among अत्यूहा, निशिपुष्पा, शीफालिका, शीतमञ्जरी, रजनीहासा for Nyctanthes arbor-tristis). "पारिजात वृक्षः" is a two-word descriptive phrase, "the parijata tree", the shape Wikidata labels take rather than a lexical name. Right plant, not a name. Use पारिजात.

verdicts.name: பவழமல்லி
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Wisdomlib plant-name lexicon: "Pavizhamalli ... in Tamil is the name of a plant identified with Nyctanthes arbor-tristis of the Oleaceae family"; corroborated by a Siddha clinical paper in Der Pharma Chemica on "Nyctanthes arbor-tristis (Pavalamalli)"; efloraofindia gives the fuller Tamil form பவளமல்லிகை
verdicts.reason: The coral-jasmine name is attested for this species by a lexicon and a Siddha source independent of Wikidata. பவழம் and பவளம் are both standard Tamil spellings of "coral", so பவழமல்லி is the same name as the attested பவளமல்லிகை. Confirmed and preferred for Tamil; பாரிசாதம் is also attested but is shared with Erythrina variegata.

verdicts.name: பாதிரி
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Flowers of India, Stereospermum chelonoides: Tamil "ambuvagina, padiri, pathiriver, pumbadiri"; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Vol. III p.147 monograph for Patala (Stereospermum suaveolens DC., the accepted synonym of S. chelonoides) gives the Tamil name as Padari/Padiri
verdicts.reason: Retrieved the per-species list from Flowers of India, which gives padiri/pathiri for Stereospermum chelonoides, and the API monograph for Patala, which gives the same Tamil name for the drug. பாதிரி is the standard Tamil orthography of that name. Confirmed and preferred. Flowers of India also confirms the page headword by giving Sanskrit पाटल for this species.

verdicts.name: सीसालपिनिया सप्पन
verdicts.reason: Devanagari respelling of the Latin binomial "Caesalpinia sappan", not a Hindi plant name, and a poor transliteration at that. The retrieved Hindi names for the species (efloraofindia, Caesalpinia sappan) are Patang/पतंग and Bakam/बकम. Wikidata label artifact; drop.

verdicts.name: பதிமுகம்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Flowers of India, Caesalpinia sappan (Sappan Wood) gives the Tamil name பதிமுகம் (Padhimugam); corroborated by Tamil/Siddha herb suppliers and the Siddha literature, where sappan heartwood is traded as Padhimugam/Pathimukham and the Siddha names are Patangam and Anaikuntrumani; efloraofindia gives Tamil Sappangu, Patangam
verdicts.reason: பதிமுகம் is attested for Caesalpinia sappan by a per-species source and by Siddha trade nomenclature, independently of Wikidata. Confirmed and preferred for Tamil.

verdicts.name: உகாய்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia, Salvadora persica: Tamil "பெருவிளா peru-vila, பீலு pilu, உகாய் ukay"
verdicts.reason: உகாய் is attested as a Tamil name for Salvadora persica on the retrieved per-species list and is the classical Tamil name for the toothbrush tree. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: पिप्पली
verdicts.reason: Both per-species sources I retrieved give the Hindi name as पिपली, not पिप्पली, and assign पिप्पली to Sanskrit: efloraofindia lists "Hindi: पिपली Pipli / Sanskrit: पिप्पली", and Flowers of India lists "Hindi: पिपली Pipli / Sanskrit: पिप्पली Pippali, Magadhi". API-derived monograph summaries give the Hindi name as Pipli/Pipar. पिप्पली as a Hindi entry is the Sanskrit form duplicated into the Hindi slot. Right plant, so no misattribution, but not confirmed as Hindi. Use पिपली, and note that the superficially similar Hindi पीपल denotes Ficus religiosa, so it must not be substituted here.

verdicts.name: पिप्पली
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Flowers of India, Piper longum: Sanskrit "पिप्पली Pippali, Magadhi"; efloraofindia gives Sanskrit पिप्पली; the API monograph drug name for the dried unripe fruit of Piper longum Linn. is Pippali
verdicts.reason: Attested as the Sanskrit name for Piper longum by two independent per-species sources plus the pharmacopoeial drug name. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: திப்பிலி
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Flowers of India and efloraofindia, Piper longum: Tamil "திப்பிலீ Tippili"; API/Siddha monograph summaries give the Tamil name as Thippili
verdicts.reason: Two independent per-species sources give this Tamil name for Piper longum, differing only in the length of the final vowel (திப்பிலீ vs திப்பிலி); திப்பிலி is the standard modern spelling. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: महुआ
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MADHUKA (Flower) monograph (local copy /Users/jairajsharma/Projects/ayurveda-atlas/sources-private/api-all.txt), Hindi synonym "Mahuwa"; India Flora Online (IISc), Madhuca longifolia var. latifolia sheet, Hindi "महुआ (Mahua, Mohwa, Mauwa)".
verdicts.reason: API's Madhuka monograph is drawn on Madhuca indica J.F.Gmel., which POWO treats as a synonym of Madhuca longifolia var. latifolia, so the monograph attaches to this species. API gives Hindi Mahuwa; India Flora Online gives महुआ in Devanagari. महुआ is the standard orthography and the form a Hindi speaker would search.

verdicts.name: महुवा
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MADHUKA (Flower) monograph, Hindi synonym "Mahuwa" (also Assamese/Bengali/Gujarati Mahuwa).
verdicts.reason: API's romanisation "Mahuwa" corresponds to महुवा. A genuine spelling variant of the same word, not a separate name, so it is attested but not the preferred form; महुआ is.

verdicts.name: இலுப்பை
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MADHUKA monograph, Tamil synonyms "Katiluppai, Kattu Iluppai, Iluppi"; India Flora Online (IISc) Tamil "Kaattu-iluppai / Illupei".
verdicts.reason: Both sources give the iluppai stem as the Tamil name for this species. API also lists Malayalam Iluppa/Irippa, consistent with the same Dravidian root. Only Tamil candidate on the page and correctly scripted.

verdicts.name: महुआ
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MADHUKA (Flower) monograph, Hindi "Mahuwa"; India Flora Online (IISc), Hindi "महुआ".
verdicts.reason: Same species and the same API monograph, which is specifically the flower drug, so it maps cleanly onto a Madhuka Pushpa page. महुआ names the tree rather than the flower part; the flower-specific forms are Sanskrit मधूकपुष्प and Telugu Ippa Puvvu (API). Acceptable at species level.

verdicts.name: महुवा
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MADHUKA (Flower) monograph, Hindi "Mahuwa".
verdicts.reason: Spelling variant of महुआ, attested by API's romanisation but not the preferred Hindi form.

verdicts.name: இலுப்பை
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MADHUKA monograph, Tamil "Katiluppai, Kattu Iluppai, Iluppi"; India Flora Online (IISc) Tamil "Kaattu-iluppai".
verdicts.reason: Attested for Madhuca longifolia by two independent sources. Names the tree, not the flower drug specifically, which is acceptable at species level.

verdicts.name: बकायन
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MAHANIMBA (Stem Bark) monograph, Hindi "Bakain, Drek"; MMPND (Univ. of Melbourne Multilingual Multiscript Plant Name Database), Melia page, Hindi line "बकैन Bakain, बकाना नीम्ब Bakānā nīmba, बकायन Bakayan, महानीम Mahanimb".
verdicts.reason: MMPND gives बकायन in Devanagari verbatim under Hindi for Melia azedarach, and API independently gives Bakain. Correct species, correct language, correct script.

verdicts.name: महानिम्बिसस्यम्
verdicts.reason: Not attested anywhere I could retrieve. API's MAHANIMBA monograph gives Sanskrit "Ramyaka, Dreka" plus the monograph name Mahanimba; MMPND's Sanskrit line for Melia azedarach is only "महानिंब Mahanimbah". महानिम्बिसस्यम् is a malformed compound (mahānimbi- + sasyam, 'great-neem crop/grain') with no textual attestation, reading as a Wikidata coinage rather than a nighaṇṭu name. The correct Sanskrit is महानिम्बः. Reject.

verdicts.name: 12.தோழிக்குரைத்த பத்து
verdicts.reason: This is not a plant name at all. It is the heading of decad 12 of Ainkuṟunūṟu, a Sangam-era Tamil anthology in the Eṭṭuttokai, meaning 'the ten (songs) spoken to the confidante' (tamilsurangam.in literature index; Ainkurunuru). The leading '12.' is a table-of-contents number, which is the tell. It has been harvested into a vernacular-name slot by mistake. API gives Tamil "Malaivembu" and MMPND gives "மலை வேம்பு Malai vembu, காட்டு வேம்பூ Kattu vembhu" for Melia azedarach. Reject outright.
verdicts.denotesInstead: Nothing botanical. It is a Tamil literary section heading (Ainkuṟunūṟu, decad 12, 'tōḻikkuraitta pattu'), not a species name.

verdicts.name: मकोय
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KAKAMACI (Whole Plant) monograph on Solanum nigrum, Hindi "Makoya" (Punjabi "Mako", Urdu "Makoh"); India Flora Online / MMPND Tamil-Hindi indexes give Hindi "Mokoi मोकोय" for Solanum nigrum L.
verdicts.reason: API attests Makoya as the Hindi name in the Solanum nigrum monograph, and an independent flora index gives the same name in Devanagari. Correct species and script.

verdicts.name: மணத்தக்காளி
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KAKAMACI monograph, Tamil "Manarthakkali, Manaththakkali, Manitakkali, Maniththakkali"; India Flora Online, Solanum nigrum sheet, "மணத்தக்காளி Manatakkali".
verdicts.reason: API lists four romanised variants of exactly this Tamil name for Solanum nigrum, and India Flora Online gives it in Tamil script. Also matches API's Malayalam Manatakkali. Confirmed.

verdicts.name: मण्डूकपर्णी
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MANDUKAPARNI (Whole Plant) monograph on Centella asiatica (title name, Sanskrit synonyms "Manduki, Darduracchada"); MMPND Centella page, which lists "Maṇḍūkaparṇī" under SANSKRIT and "ब्रह्म मंडुकी Brahma maṇḍukī / ब्रहमामानडुकी Brahma manduki" under HINDI.
verdicts.reason: The name is correct for Centella asiatica, so it is not a botanical error, but the language tag is wrong: both API and MMPND place मण्डूकपर्णी on the Sanskrit side and give ब्रह्म मंडुकी as the Hindi name. It does circulate in Hindi Ayurvedic writing as a Sanskrit loanword, so I confirm it for the species while flagging that it should be tagged sa, not hi. Not preferred for Hindi.

verdicts.name: வல்லாரை
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MANDUKAPARNI monograph, Tamil "Vallarai"; MMPND Centella page, Tamil line "வல்லாரை Vallaarai [Siv] (Vallarai)".
verdicts.reason: Two independent sources, one of them giving the exact Tamil string. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: रुबिया  कॉर्डिफ़ोलिया
verdicts.reason: This is not a Hindi plant name. It is the Latin binomial 'Rubia cordifolia' respelled in Devanagari, double space and all, which is how Wikidata stores script-transliterated labels. API's MANJISTHA monograph gives Hindi "Manjitha, Manjit"; MMPND gives Hindi "Majith, Manjit". No Hindi source calls the plant रुबिया कॉर्डिफ़ोलिया. Reject; the real Hindi name is मंजीठ.
verdicts.denotesInstead: Nothing. It is the Latin binomial transliterated into Devanagari, not a vernacular name.

verdicts.name: रुबिअ कोर्दिफ़्ओलिअ
verdicts.reason: Same failure as the Hindi entry: a Devanagari transliteration of 'Rubia cordifolia', and a worse one (the broken cluster फ़्ओ is not valid Devanagari orthography). API's Sanskrit synonyms for Rubia cordifolia are "Yojnavalli, Vastrarajini, Rakta"; MMPND gives "Gandari, Manjishta, Manjishtha, Manjistha, Munjistha". Reject; the real Sanskrit name is मञ्जिष्ठा.
verdicts.denotesInstead: Nothing. It is the Latin binomial transliterated into Devanagari, not a Sanskrit name.

verdicts.name: रुबिया  कॉर्डिफ़ोलिया
verdicts.reason: Identical duplicate of the manjishtha candidate: the Latin binomial in Devanagari, not a Hindi name. API MANJISTHA monograph gives Hindi "Manjitha, Manjit"; MMPND gives "Majith, Manjit". Reject.
verdicts.denotesInstead: Nothing. It is the Latin binomial transliterated into Devanagari, not a vernacular name.

verdicts.name: रुबिअ कोर्दिफ़्ओलिअ
verdicts.reason: Identical duplicate of the manjishtha candidate: the Latin binomial in Devanagari with an invalid consonant cluster. Not attested as Sanskrit by API or MMPND. Reject.
verdicts.denotesInstead: Nothing. It is the Latin binomial transliterated into Devanagari, not a Sanskrit name.

verdicts.name: பொன்னாங்காணி
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MATSYAKSI (Whole Plant) monograph on Alternanthera sessilis, Tamil "Ponnangkanni" (Telugu "Ponnaganti Koora", Malayalam "Ponnankanni"); India Flora Online (IISc), Alternanthera sessilis sheet, Tamil "Ponnaankanni keerai".
verdicts.reason: API's Matsyaksi monograph is explicitly Alternanthera sessilis and gives Ponnangkanni as the Tamil name; India Flora Online agrees. Correct species, correct script, only Tamil candidate.

verdicts.name: नागरङ्गफलम्
verdicts.reason: WRONG SPECIES. नागरङ्ग is the Sanskrit name of the orange, not the citron. Wisdomlib's Sanskrit plant-name entry identifies Nāgaraṅga with Citrus aurantium L. (synonyms Citrus sinensis, Citrus vulgaris) and notes that English 'orange' derives from it via Arabic nāranj. API's BIJAPURA monograph on Citrus medica gives Sanskrit "Matulunga", and MMPND's Sanskrit line for Citrus medica is "अम्‍लकेसर, बीजाण्‍ड, जम्भीर, लुंग, महाफल, मातुलुङ्ग, पूरक, रुचक, सुमनःफल" with no नागरङ्ग anywhere. This is exactly the kind of genuine-name-wrong-plant error that would survive on the page, so flag and drop. (One 17th-c. dietetics text, Bhojanakutūhala, glosses nāgaraṅga loosely as 'citron', but that is a minority reading against API and MMPND.)
verdicts.denotesInstead: Citrus × aurantium / Citrus × sinensis, the orange. Not Citrus medica.

verdicts.name: நாரத்தம்பழம்
verdicts.reason: WRONG SPECIES. MMPND's Citrus sorting pages place "நாரந்தை Nārantai, நரந்தம்பழம் Narantampaḻam" exclusively under Citrus × aurantium (bitter orange, the narthangai pickled in Tamil cooking), and MMPND's Citrus medica Tamil line is "Campalam, Campiram, எலுமிச்சை Elumiccai, கடரநாரத்தை Kaṭāranārattai, கொம்மட்டிமாதுளை Kommatti-matulai". API's BIJAPURA monograph gives Tamil "Turunji Pazham, Kadarangai" for Citrus medica. The Citrus medica Tamil name is the qualified compound கடாரநாரத்தை or துருஞ்சிப்பழம்; bare நாரத்தம்பழம் is the bitter orange. Drop and flag.
verdicts.denotesInstead: Citrus × aurantium, the bitter/sour orange (narthangai). Not Citrus medica.

verdicts.name: அரம்பா
verdicts.reason: Only a weak corroborator attests this. Tamil Wikipedia's அரம்பா article is indeed about Litsea glutinosa (Lauraceae) and gives அரம்பாமரம், so it is at least not a different species, but Tamil Wikipedia mirrors Wikidata and cannot corroborate a Wikidata harvest. The two independent authorities disagree with it: API's MEDASAKAH (Stem Bark) monograph on Litsea chinensis syn. L. glutinosa gives Tamil "Medalakavi", and India Flora Online (IISc), fetched directly, gives Tamil "Pisinpatty" only. Not confirmed.

verdicts.name: मेथी
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, METHI (Seed) monograph on Trigonella foenum-graecum, Hindi "Methi"; MMPND Trigonella page, Hindi line "कसूरी मेथी Kasoorii methii (leaves-dried), मेंथी Methi (seeds), मेथि Methi (seeds), मोटी सौंफ़ Motee saunf".
verdicts.reason: Attested by API and by MMPND in Devanagari. मेथी is the standard spelling and the form a Hindi speaker would use or search.

verdicts.name: दीपनी
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Rājanighaṇṭu (13th c.) 6.67-69, as transcribed on wisdomlib's Methi entry, which lists 16 synonyms of Methī: "Methikā, Methinī, Dīpanī, Bahupatrikā, Vedhanī, Gandhavījā, Jyoti, Gandhaphālā, Vallarī, Candrikā, Methā, Miśrapuṣpā, Kairavī, Kuñcikā, Pītavījā and Bahuparṇī."
verdicts.reason: Dīpanī is genuinely in the Rājanighaṇṭu paryāya list for fenugreek, so it is attested for this species. But it is a nighaṇṭu epithet meaning 'the kindler' (digestive stimulant) and is applied generically to other dravyas too, and API's official Sanskrit for the monograph is Methini, not Dipani. Confirmed, not preferred, and worth a gloss on the page so a reader does not read it as a unique designation.

verdicts.name: मेथिका
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Rājanighaṇṭu 6.67-69 (via wisdomlib), where Methikā is the first of the 16 listed synonyms; MMPND Trigonella page, Sanskrit line "Chandrika, गंधबीजा Gandhabiijaa, Kairava, Medhika, Methika, Sarapunkha".
verdicts.reason: Two independent sources attest Methikā as a Sanskrit name for Trigonella foenum-graecum. It is the proper nominal synonym (as against the attributive Dīpanī), so it is the preferred Sanskrit form among the candidates. Note API's own monograph Sanskrit is Methinī (मेथिनी).

verdicts.name: வெந்தயம்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, METHI monograph, Tamil "Mendium, Ventaiyam"; MMPND Trigonella page, Tamil line "Mathai, மேதி Meti, Uluvaarisi, Vendayum, வெந்தியம் Ventayam, வெந்தய கீரை Ventaya kirai".
verdicts.reason: API gives Ventaiyam and MMPND gives வெந்தியம்/Vendayum; வெந்தயம் is the standard Tamil spelling of the seed and the form in everyday use. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: सौंफ
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MISREYA (Fruit) monograph on Foeniculum vulgare, Hindi "Saunf"; MMPND Foeniculum page, Hindi line "Badi, Badishep, Bari saunf, Bari sanuf, Sanuf, सौंफ Saunf, Sonp, Sont"; India Flora Online (IISc), Foeniculum vulgare sheet, Hindi "Saunf".
verdicts.reason: Three independent sources, with MMPND giving the exact Devanagari string सौंफ without nuqta. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: सौंफ़
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MISREYA monograph, Hindi "Saunf"; MMPND Foeniculum page Hindi line, which spells the word सौंफ (and uses the nuqta form in मोटी सौंफ़ on the Trigonella page).
verdicts.reason: The same word with a nuqta on फ. A legitimate orthographic variant, attested through the same sources, but not a distinct name and not the form MMPND prints for this species. Keep at most as an alias; सौंफ is preferred.

verdicts.name: பெருஞ்சீரகம்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: MMPND (Univ. of Melbourne), Foeniculum page, Tamil line "Perun siragum, Shombu, Sohikire" for Foeniculum vulgare.
verdicts.reason: MMPND, independent of Wikidata, lists Perun siragum (= பெருஞ்சீரகம்) as a Tamil name for Foeniculum vulgare, so the name is attested for this species. Two caveats a reader should see: API's MISREYA monograph gives Tamil "Shombu" and India Flora Online gives "Sopu, Kaattu seeragam", neither listing பெருஞ்சீரகம்; and some Tamil sources apply பெருஞ்சீரகம் to Pimpinella anisum (anise) instead, so the term is not exclusive to fennel. Confirmed, and preferred as the only Tamil candidate, but சோம்பு is the form both API and IISc print.

verdicts.name: मूली
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MULAKA (Seed) monograph on Raphanus sativus, Hindi "Muli"; MMPND Raphanus page, Hindi line "Mulla, Mooli, Muli, मूली Mūlī".
verdicts.reason: MMPND gives the exact Devanagari string मूली under Hindi for Raphanus sativus and API independently gives Muli. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: मूलकम्
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, monograph title MULAKA for Raphanus sativus (Sanskrit synonyms "Salamarkataka, Visra, Saleya, Marusambhava"); MMPND Raphanus page, Sanskrit line "मूलक Muulaka, राजालुक".
verdicts.reason: MMPND prints the stem form मूलक; the candidate मूलकम् is its nominative/accusative neuter singular, the same lexeme in the inflected form API's monograph title uses. Confirmed for the species. If the atlas prefers stem forms elsewhere, मूलक is the citation form.

verdicts.name: முள்ளங்கி
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MULAKA monograph, Tamil "Mullangi, Mulakam, Mullangu, Millangi"; MMPND Raphanus page, Tamil line "மூலம் Muulam, முள்ளங்கி Mullangki".
verdicts.reason: MMPND gives the exact Tamil string and API gives Mullangi. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: கார்டினியா கம்மிபெரா
verdicts.reason: Not a Tamil plant name. It is the Latin binomial 'Gardenia gummifera' respelled in Tamil script, the same Wikidata script-transliteration artefact as the Rubia entries. API's NADIHINGU (Exudate) monograph on Gardenia gummifera gives Tamil "Tikka malli" (Hindi "Naadihingu, Dikaamaali", Sanskrit "Hingunadika"), and flowersofindia's Gummy Gardenia entry gives Tamil kambil, sirukkambil, tikkamalli. Reject; the real Tamil name is திக்கமல்லி.
verdicts.denotesInstead: Nothing. It is the Latin binomial transliterated into Tamil script, not a vernacular name.

verdicts.name: नाग केसर
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, NAGAKESARA (Stamen) monograph on Mesua ferrea, Hindi "Nagkesara, Pila Nagkesara"; MMPND Mesua page, Hindi line "Gajapushpam, नाग केसर (Nāga kēsara) Nagakesar, नागचम्पा Nagchampa, नागेसर Nagesar, नागकेसर Nagkesar".
verdicts.reason: MMPND prints the exact candidate string नाग केसर, with the space, under Hindi for Mesua ferrea, and API independently gives Nagkesara. Confirmed and preferred (the closed form नागकेसर is an equally good alias).

verdicts.name: नागकेसरः
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, monograph title NAGAKESARA for Mesua ferrea (Sanskrit synonyms "Kesara, Nagapuspa, Naga, Hema, Gajakesara"); MMPND Mesua page, Sanskrit line including "नागकेशर Nagakesarah, Nagakesara, नागपुष्प Nagapuspah".
verdicts.reason: Both sources attest Nāgakesara as the Sanskrit name for Mesua ferrea; MMPND prints the -aḥ nominative that the candidate uses. The candidate spells the sibilant स (API's Nagakesara) where MMPND prints श; both spellings circulate and API's is the official one. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: நாகமரம்
verdicts.reason: Only Tamil Wikipedia attests it, which mirrors Wikidata and so cannot corroborate a Wikidata harvest. Both independent authorities give different Tamil names: API's NAGAKESARA monograph lists Tamil "Naugu, Naugaliral, Nagachampakam, Sirunagappu", and MMPND's Mesua Tamil line is "Charu-nagapu, சிறுநாகப்பூ Ciṟunākappū, Irul, Karunangu, நாகப்பூ Nāgappū, நாகேசுரம் Nakecuram, நாங்கு Nāṅku, Tadinangu, Veillutta champakam" with no நாகமரம். It is also a loose descriptive compound ('naga tree'), the kind of label that attaches to several trees, so I will not assert a specific other species for it. Not confirmed; use நாகப்பூ or சிறுநாகப்பூ instead.

verdicts.name: मोथा
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MUSTA (Rhizome) monograph on Cyperus rotundus, Hindi "Motha, Nagarmotha"; India Flora Online (IISc), Cyperus rotundus sheet, Hindi "Nagarmotha, Motha" (and family name "बड़ा नागर मोथा फैमिली" in Devanagari).
verdicts.reason: Both independent sources give Motha as a Hindi name for Cyperus rotundus. Confirmed. Preferred among the candidates as the only Hindi one, though नागरमोथा is the trade/market form and matches this page's own title, so it belongs on the page too.

verdicts.name: கோரை
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MUSTA monograph, Tamil "Korai, Korai-Kizhangu"; India Flora Online (IISc), Cyperus rotundus sheet, Tamil "korai, korai kilangu, muthakasu".
verdicts.reason: Two independent sources give korai for Cyperus rotundus. Confirmed and preferred; கோரைக்கிழங்கு (the rhizome, which is the drug) is the more precise form for the monograph.

verdicts.name: नारியल
verdicts.reason: REJECT ON SCRIPT, not on botany. This string is script-mixed: नारि is Devanagari but यल is written with the Tamil-block characters, so it is not the Hindi word नारियल. The name itself is correct for Cocos nucifera (API NARIKELA monograph, Hindi "Nariyal, Gola"; MMPND Cocos page, Hindi "नारियल Naariyal"), so publish the clean all-Devanagari नारियल instead and drop this encoding. I am flagging rather than silently fixing because a mixed-script label will fail search and collation on the site.

verdicts.name: नारिकेलम्
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, monograph title NARIKELA for Cocos nucifera (Sanskrit synonyms "Narikela, Trnaraja"); MMPND Cocos page, Sanskrit "नारीकेल Naarikela".
verdicts.reason: Both sources attest Nārikela as the Sanskrit name for Cocos nucifera; the candidate is its nominative neuter singular, matching API's monograph form. MMPND spells the second vowel long (नारीकेल); API's Narikela supports the short-i candidate. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: தேங்காய்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, NARIKELA (Endosperm) monograph, Tamil "Tenkai, Kopparai"; MMPND Cocos page, Tamil "தேங்காய் Tengai".
verdicts.reason: MMPND prints the exact Tamil string and API gives Tenkai. Note it denotes the nut/kernel; the palm itself is தென்னை. Since this page's drug is the dried endosperm, தேங்காய் is apt. Confirmed and preferred.

verdicts.name: नारியल
verdicts.reason: Same script-mixing defect as on the narikela page: नारि in Devanagari followed by यल in Tamil-block characters. The underlying name नारियल is correct for Cocos nucifera (API NARIKELA monograph Hindi "Nariyal"; MMPND "नारियल Naariyal") but this byte sequence is not it. Also note this page is coconut water, for which the Hindi is नारियल पानी; नारियल alone names the nut.

verdicts.name: नारिकेलम्
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, NARIKELA monograph on Cocos nucifera, Sanskrit "Narikela, Trnaraja"; MMPND Cocos page, Sanskrit "नारीकेल Naarikela".
verdicts.reason: Attested for the species by both sources. Caveat for this page specifically: नारिकेलम् names the coconut, not its water; the classical term for the water is नारिकेलजलम् / नारिकेलोदकम्, which is what the page title transliterates.

verdicts.name: தேங்காய்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, NARIKELA monograph, Tamil "Tenkai, Kopparai"; MMPND Cocos page, Tamil "தேங்காய் Tengai".
verdicts.reason: Correct for Cocos nucifera, but தேங்காய் is specifically the mature nut and its kernel, which is the opposite end of the fruit's life from coconut water. The Tamil for tender-coconut water is இளநீர். I confirm the name for the species but will not mark it preferred on a page about the water, because a Tamil reader would not use தேங்காய் for நாரிகேல ஜலம்.

verdicts.name: कासनी
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Flowers of India / "Names of Plants in India" (Chicory page) lists Hindi "कासनी Kasni" and "Hinduba"; efloraofindia's Cichorium intybus page independently lists Hindi कासनी (Kasni), Kashni, Hinduba.
verdicts.reason: Both per-species compilations give कासनी in Devanagari as the Hindi name for Cichorium intybus, and it is also the Ayurvedic drug name (Kasani/Kasani beej). It is the form a Hindi speaker would search, so preferred.

verdicts.name: சிக்கரி
verdicts.reason: No botanical source I retrieved gives any Tamil name for Cichorium intybus. Flowers of India's Chicory page lists Hindi, Marathi, Malayalam, Telugu, Kannada, Urdu and Sanskrit but NO Tamil; efloraofindia likewise lists no Tamil. What those sources do list is Malayalam "chikkari" and Kannada "ಚಿಕೋರಿ Chikory" and Gujarati "Chikori" — i.e. the English word "chicory" borrowed into other languages. சிக்கரி is that same English borrowing written in Tamil script, not an attested Tamil plant name. The actual Tamil name is காசினி / காசினிக்கீரை (see discovered). Dropping this.

verdicts.name: தேற்றா
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia's Strychnos potatorum page gives Tamil "Thethaan (தேத்தான்)" and "Thethaangkottai (தேத்தாங்கொட்டை)", noting the seeds clear drinking water; Tamil Wiktionary's entry for "strychnos potatorum" gives தேற்றா, and Tamil Siddha suppliers/Siddha writing use தேற்றான் கொட்டை for the seed.
verdicts.reason: தேற்றா (tēṟṟā) and தேத்தான்/தேற்றான் are the same Tamil name for the clearing-nut tree with the regular ற்/த் spelling variation, and efloraofindia attests the name for this exact species. Not marked preferred because the form a Tamil speaker actually uses and searches is தேற்றான்கொட்டை / தேத்தாங்கொட்டை (the seed), which is not in the candidate list.

verdicts.name: काफल
verdicts.corroboratingSource: efloraofindia's Myrica esculenta page gives Hindi "kaiphal, kaphal" and Nepali "काफल (Kafal)" in Devanagari; Sanskrit katphala, mahavalkala.
verdicts.reason: काफल is the Devanagari form of the Hindi/Nepali name kaphal/kafal that efloraofindia attests for Myrica esculenta, and it is the name used across the Kumaon-Garhwal range where the fruit is sold. Preferred for Hindi.

verdicts.name: கைதை
verdicts.corroboratingSource: MMPND (Multilingual Multiscript Plant Name Database, Univ. of Melbourne), "Sorting Pandanus names", citing the Tamil Lexicon: kaitai (கைதை) = fragrant screwpine, Pandanus odoratissimus (= P. odorifer), listed alongside kētakai (கேதகை).
verdicts.reason: கைதை is a genuine classical Tamil name for the fragrant screwpine, attested in the Tamil Lexicon via MMPND and in Sangam-literature usage, and P. odoratissimus is a synonym of P. odorifer so the species match is exact. Not preferred: Flowers of India's Kewda page gives Tamil as கேதகை and தாழை, and தாழை is the everyday Tamil name.

verdicts.name: खजूर
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Herbarium JCB / India Flora Online (IISc) Phoenix dactylifera sheet gives vernaculars "Kharjurah (Sanskrit); Kajur (Hindi); Kajura (Kannada); Khajuri (Marathi)"; MMPND "Sorting Phoenix names" gives Hindi "Khaji, Khajur, Salma, Sendhi" for P. dactylifera; efloraofindia gives Hindi "Khajur".
verdicts.reason: खजूर is attested for Phoenix dactylifera by three independent per-species sources and is the universal Hindi name for the date, so preferred. Caveat for the page: MMPND lists खजूर for Phoenix sylvestris too, so the name is shared between the two Phoenix species and does not by itself distinguish them.

verdicts.name: खर्जूरम्
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Herbarium JCB / India Flora Online (IISc) Phoenix dactylifera sheet gives Sanskrit "Kharjurah" (खर्जूरः); the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India carries monographs "Kharjura (Fresh Fruit)" and "Kharjura (Dried Fruit)" for Phoenix dactylifera Linn., with Sanskrit synonyms Pinda Kharjura and Aharjura.
verdicts.reason: API attests Kharjura as the Sanskrit/Ayurvedic drug name for Phoenix dactylifera, and Herbarium JCB gives खर्जूरः for the same species; खर्जूरम् is the regular neuter form used for the fruit. Important caveat to carry on the page: in classical Sanskrit lexicography खर्जूर alone is also applied to Phoenix sylvestris, and API itself disambiguates this species as पिण्डखर्जूर — so bare खर्जूरम् is correct but not species-exclusive.

verdicts.name: பேரீச்சை
