verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, RAKTACANDANA (Heart Wood) = Pterocarpus santalinus Linn. f., Hindi: 'Raktachandanam, Lalchandana'.
verdicts.reason: API lists Raktachandana first in the Hindi field for this species, alongside Lalchandana, and the same form in Bengali, Kannada, Malayalam and Marathi. Confirmed. Note that लाल चंदन is at least as common in spoken Hindi; it is in `discovered` and is a defensible alternative preferred form.

verdicts.name: செஞ்சந்தனம்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, RAKTACANDANA = Pterocarpus santalinus, Tamil: 'Sanchandanam' (printed with OCR loss for Senchandanam, i.e. செஞ்சந்தனம், 'red sandal').
verdicts.reason: API's Tamil entry for this exact species is the sem/sen- prefixed form of சந்தனம், which is what செஞ்சந்தனம் spells. Standard Tamil name for red sanders and distinct from plain சந்தனம் (Santalum album).

verdicts.name: एलियम सैटिवम
verdicts.reason: This is the Latin binomial Allium sativum written in Devanagari, which is the Hindi Wikipedia article title, not a vernacular name. API's Hindi for the species is 'Lahasun'; eFloraofIndia gives Lasun. No source lists एलियम सैटिवम as a Hindi plant name. It is a harvesting artifact of taking a Wikipedia/Wikidata label as a vernacular name, and it would look absurd on a monograph.

verdicts.name: लहसुन
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, LASUNA (Bulb) = Allium sativum Linn., Hindi: 'Lahasun'; Urdu 'Lahsan, Seer'.
verdicts.reason: API's official Hindi name for the Allium sativum monograph. Unambiguously the form a Hindi speaker uses and searches.

verdicts.name: लशुनम्
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, monograph title LASUNA (Bulb) = Allium sativum Linn., with Sanskrit synonyms 'Rasona, Yavanesta'.
verdicts.reason: API names the monograph by the official Sanskrit drug name Lasuna (लशुन), so लशुनम् is the attested Sanskrit for this species; रसोन, the page slug, is listed as its Sanskrit synonym. Preferred Sanskrit form on an API-aligned page.

verdicts.name: பூண்டு
verdicts.corroboratingSource: University of Madras Tamil Lexicon (via agarathi.com), பூண்டு: 'Garlic; உள்ளிப்பூடு'. Corroborated by API LASUNA, Tamil: 'Vellaipoondu' (வெள்ளைப்பூண்டு) for Allium sativum.
verdicts.reason: The Madras Lexicon glosses பூண்டு as garlic, and API's Tamil entry for this species is the வெள்ளை- compound of the same head word. The lexicon also records a generic sense ('a plant or herb in general'), but in modern Tamil பூண்டு on its own means garlic, so it is the preferred Tamil form.

verdicts.name: एलियम सैटिवम
verdicts.reason: Same as on the rasona-garlic page: this is the Latin binomial Allium sativum transliterated into Devanagari (the Hindi Wikipedia title), not a Hindi vernacular name. API's Hindi for the species is 'Lahasun'. Harvesting artifact; drop it.

verdicts.name: लहसुन
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, LASUNA (Bulb) = Allium sativum Linn., Hindi: 'Lahasun'.
verdicts.reason: API's official Hindi name for Allium sativum. Applies to this page too, which is the leaf of the same species.

verdicts.name: लशुनम्
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, monograph title LASUNA (Bulb) = Allium sativum Linn., Sanskrit synonyms 'Rasona, Yavanesta'.
verdicts.reason: API's official Sanskrit drug name for the species; रसोन (the page slug) is its recorded synonym.

verdicts.name: பூண்டு
verdicts.corroboratingSource: University of Madras Tamil Lexicon (via agarathi.com): பூண்டு 'Garlic; உள்ளிப்பூடு'; API LASUNA Tamil 'Vellaipoondu' for Allium sativum.
verdicts.reason: Lexicon-attested Tamil for garlic and the head word of API's Tamil entry for this species.

verdicts.name: खिरनी
verdicts.corroboratingSource: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Manilkara hexandra, Hindi: दृढ़ (drirh), खिरनी (khirni), क्षीरी (kshiri), रायन (rayan).
verdicts.reason: Attested in Devanagari as Hindi for Manilkara hexandra and the form in general use (khirni fruit). Separate page-level caution: the same source gives राजादन as the Sanskrit name for this species, and classical Ayurveda identifies Rishabhaka as one of the Ashtavarga orchids (usually Malaxis acuminata), with Manilkara hexandra being Rajadana/Khirni. The botanical mapping on this page, not just its names, is worth re-checking.

verdicts.name: பாலை
verdicts.denotesInstead: Manilkara kauki (Mimusops kauki); bare பாலை is also the generic Tamil tree element used for Wrightia tinctoria (வெட்பாலை), Alstonia scholaris (ஏழிலைப்பாலை) and Periploca esculenta (ஊசிப்பாலை)
verdicts.reason: Retrieved University of Madras Tamil Lexicon (via agarathi.com) for பாலை: 'Silvery-leaved ape-flower, m. tr., Mimusops kauki', and Winslow's Tamil-English Dictionary, which records பாலை only inside compounds for Periploca esculenta, Echites scholaris (= Alstonia scholaris), Gelonium bifarium, Asclepias volubilis and Nerium antidysentericum (= Wrightia). eFloraofIndia's Tamil for Manilkara hexandra is உலக்கைப்பாலை, not bare பாலை. So the harvested form resolves to a different Manilkara species in the lexicon and is otherwise a floating generic element, which on a monograph page reads as a precise name for this species when it is not.

verdicts.name: रोहेड़ा
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, ROHITAKA (Stem Bark) = Tecomella undulata (Sm.) Seem., Regional Language Names, Hindi: 'Roheda'; Gujarati 'Rohido', Marathi 'Rohida', Punjabi 'Rohira'.
verdicts.reason: API's Hindi name for exactly this species, with cognate forms across four neighbouring languages. Worth carrying onto the page as a caution: the same API monograph warns that bark of Aphanamixis polystachya (Syn. Amoora rohitaka) is also traded as 'Rohitak', so the Sanskrit page name is ambiguous even though the Hindi name is not.

verdicts.name: உருத்திராட்சம்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: University of Madras Tamil Lexicon (via agarathi.com), உருத்திராட்சம்: 'rudra-kṣa. 1. Olive-fruited linden, Eloeocarpus ... 2. Rudrāk, l. tr., Eloeocarpus ganitrus'. Corroborated by API Part I, RUDRAKSA (Seed) = Elaeocarpus sphaericus Gaertn., Tamil: 'Rudraksha'.
verdicts.reason: The Madras Lexicon ties உருத்திராட்சம் to the genus Elaeocarpus generally and to E. ganitrus specifically, which matches this page's genus-level botanical. API's monograph taxon is E. sphaericus, the older name for E. ganitrus. Standard and only Tamil form.

verdicts.name: நீலாம்பரம்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Barleria strigosa, Tamil: மஞ்சட்செம்முள்ளி (mancat-cemmulli), நீலாம்பரம் (nilamparam), நீலி (nili).
verdicts.reason: I initially suspected a language error, because API's monograph for this species (NILAJHINTI (Root) = Barleria strigosa Willd.) puts 'Nilambaramu' in the Telugu field and gives Tamil as 'Shemmuli'. Retrieval settled it: eFloraofIndia independently attests நீலாம்பரம் in Tamil script for Barleria strigosa, so it is confirmed, with the Telugu cognate alongside it. Not marking it preferred: that source lists three Tamil names and API gives a fourth, and I cannot tell which a Tamil speaker would reach for. API's Sanskrit for this species does include Saireyakah, so the page name itself checks out.

verdicts.name: साल
verdicts.corroboratingSource: eFloraofIndia, Shorea robusta, Hindi: साल (Sal), Salwa, Sakhu, Sakher. Corroborated by API Part I, SALA (Heart Wood) = Shorea robusta Gaertn., Hindi: 'Saal, Sakhuaa, Saakhu'.
verdicts.reason: Both sources give साल as the first Hindi name for Shorea robusta. The universally used Hindi form.

verdicts.name: குங்கிலியம்
verdicts.corroboratingSource: eFloraofIndia, Shorea robusta, Tamil: attam, venkungiliyam, kungiliyam (i.e. குங்கிலியம், வெண்குங்கிலியம்).
verdicts.reason: I expected this to be a species error and it survived verification: eFloraofIndia attests kungiliyam in the Tamil field for Shorea robusta. But flag the ambiguity on the page. API assigns Tamil 'Kungiliyam, Vellai Kundarakam' to its SARJA monograph = Vateria indica, and the AFI appendix maps sarja-rasa to both Shorea robusta and Vateria indica. குங்கிலியம் is a resin trade name shared by the two dammar sources, not a species-exclusive plant name, so it should not be the page's headline Tamil name. API's species-specific Tamil for Shorea robusta is 'Saalam'.

verdicts.name: सप्तपर्ण
verdicts.reason: Retrieved eFloraofIndia for Alstonia scholaris, which lists सप्तपर्ण under Sanskrit and सप्तपर्णी (plus चितवन, बहुपुत्र, देववृक्ष, शैतान का झाड़) under Hindi; API's SAPTAPARNA monograph gives Hindi 'Chhativan, Satawana', Sanskrit 'Saptacchada, Saptaparni, Saptahva', and puts 'Saptaparna' in the Gujarati field. So the exact form सप्तपर्ण is attested for this species in Sanskrit, not in Hindi. Same species, wrong language field: relabel it Sanskrit and use चितवन or सप्तपर्णी for Hindi.

verdicts.name: ஏழிலைப்பாலை
verdicts.corroboratingSource: eFloraofIndia, Alstonia scholaris, Tamil: ஏழிலைப்பாலை (el-ilai-p-paalai), இருள்பாலை. Corroborated by API Part I, SAPTAPARNA (Stem bark) = Alstonia scholaris, Tamil: 'Ezilampalai'; and by Winslow's Tamil-English Dictionary, which glosses ஏழிலைப்பாலை as 'a tree, Echites scholaris' (= Alstonia scholaris).
verdicts.reason: Three independent sources agree. A literal calque of saptaparṇa ('seven-leaved'), which is why it maps cleanly to this species and not to the other பாலை trees.

verdicts.name: अनंतमूल
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, SVETA SARIVA (Root) = Hemidesmus indicus (Linn.) R. Br., Hindi: 'Anantamul'; also Bengali 'Anantamul, Shvetashariva', Marathi 'Anantamula', Punjabi 'Anantmool'.
verdicts.reason: API's Hindi name for exactly this species, repeated across four neighbouring languages. The form in general Hindi use.

verdicts.name: क्षीरिणीसस्यम्
verdicts.denotesInstead: Manilkara hexandra (its head word क्षीरिणी is the attested Sanskrit for that species); क्षीरिणी is also a recorded Sanskrit synonym of Dugdhika/Euphorbia
verdicts.reason: Retrieved API's SVETA SARIVA monograph, whose Sanskrit synonyms for Hemidesmus indicus are Ananta, Gopasuta and Sariva. The compound क्षीरिणीसस्यम् ('kṣīriṇī-crop') appears in no pharmacopoeia or lexicon I retrieved for this species, and its shape suggests a constructed Wikidata-era coinage rather than a nighantu name. Its head word is independently attested elsewhere: eFloraofIndia gives Sanskrit क्षीरिणी for Manilkara hexandra, and API lists Ksirini among the Sanskrit synonyms of Dugdhika (Euphorbia). Hemidesmus is latex-bearing, which is probably how the confusion arose, but the name points away from it.

verdicts.name: நன்னாரி
verdicts.corroboratingSource: University of Madras Tamil Lexicon (via agarathi.com), நன்னாரி: 'Indian sarsaparilla, m. cl., Hemidesmus indicus'; Fabricius's Tamil-English Dictionary: 'a small fragrant herb, Indian sarsaparilla, Periploca indica' (an older synonym of H. indicus). Corroborated by API SVETA SARIVA, Tamil: 'Ven Nannar'.
verdicts.reason: The Madras Lexicon names this exact species, and API's Tamil entry is the வெண்- (white) compound of the same head word. நன்னாரி is also the everyday Tamil word through nannari sharbat, so it is the form a speaker would search.

verdicts.name: பயினி
verdicts.reason: Retrieved eFloraofIndia for Vateria indica: Tamil is துருளக்கம் and வெள்ளைக்குங்கிலியம், while പയിനി (payini), കുന്തിരിക്കപ്പൈൻ and വെള്ളപ്പൈൻ are listed under MALAYALAM. API's SARJA (Exudate) monograph agrees: 'Payin' sits in the Malayalam field and Tamil is 'Kungiliyam, Vellai Kundarakam'. So பயினி is the right plant but the wrong language: a Malayalam name re-scripted into Tamil by the harvest. No species error, but it must not be published as Tamil. This page is left with no confirmed candidate; see `discovered` for attested names in all three languages.

verdicts.name: सर्पगंधा
verdicts.corroboratingSource: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Rauvolfia serpentina, Hindi: चन्द्रभाग, छोटा चांद, नाकुली, सर्पगंधा. Corroborated by API Part I, SARPAGANDHA (Root) = Rauwolfia serpentina (Linn.) Benth. ex Kurz, whose Tamil is 'Sarppaganti' and Telugu 'Sarpagandhi'.
verdicts.reason: Attested in Devanagari in the Hindi field for this species, and the dominant Hindi name in trade and search (API's own monograph title). Note that API's Hindi field itself gives छोटा चांद and धवलबरुआ, which are in `discovered`.

verdicts.name: सर्पगन्धा
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Same attestation as सर्पगंधा: eFloraofIndia, Rauvolfia serpentina, Hindi सर्पगंधा; API monograph title SARPAGANDHA for this species.
verdicts.reason: Identical Hindi word, written with the conjunct न्ध instead of the anusvara form ं. The lexeme is attested; only the spelling differs, and nothing in the sources prefers the conjunct form in Hindi. Keep one spelling on the page and prefer सर्पगंधा; this entry is confirmed but redundant.

verdicts.name: अश्वत्थः
verdicts.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa
verdicts.reason: The seeded error again, on a second page. API Part I monograph 11 is ASVATTHA (Bark) = Ficus religiosa Linn., Sanskrit synonym Pippala, Hindi 'Pipala, Pipal', Tamil 'Arasamaram, Arasu'. Rauvolfia serpentina is an Apocynaceae undershrub; अश्वत्थ is the pipal fig. API's Sanskrit synonyms for this species are Nakuli, Candrika and Chandramarah. That the same wrong alias was attached to Adhatoda vasica, Aegle marmelos, Areca catechu and Rauvolfia serpentina shows it is a systematic Wikidata defect, not a one-off: every page in the dataset carrying अश्वत्थः should be swept, not just these.

verdicts.name: सर्पगन्धः
verdicts.reason: Retrieved eFloraofIndia's Sanskrit list for Rauvolfia serpentina: चन्द्रिका, नाकुली, पातालगरुड, सर्पगंधा; API's Sanskrit synonyms are Nakuli, Candrika, Chandramarah, with the monograph titled SARPAGANDHA. Every attestation is the feminine सर्पगन्धा/सर्पगंधा; the masculine stem सर्पगन्धः is in none of them. Right plant, wrong grammatical form, which on a Sanskrit monograph line matters. Use सर्पगन्धा.

verdicts.name: சர்பகந்தி
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, SARPAGANDHA (Root) = Rauwolfia serpentina, Tamil: 'Sarppaganti'.
verdicts.reason: API's Tamil entry for exactly this species transliterates to சர்பகந்தி. (eFloraofIndia's Tamil field for this species is corrupt, carrying a Malayalam-looking 'chevanamalpodi', so API is the sound source here.) Only Tamil candidate and the standard borrowing.

verdicts.name: घमोई
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Names of Plants in India compilation for Argemone mexicana (indiantreepix 'Names of Plants in India :: Argemone mexicana L.'), Hindi: भरभांड, घमोई (ghamoee), फिरंगी धतूरा, पीला धतूरा, सत्यानाशी, सियालकांटा, तिल्मखार.
verdicts.reason: Attested in Devanagari in the Hindi list for this species. A regional name, much less current than सत्यानाशी, so not preferred.

verdicts.name: भड़भाड़
verdicts.corroboratingSource: Names of Plants in India, Argemone mexicana: the Hindi list gives भरभांड (bharbhand), with भड़भाड़ recorded as an alternate spelling of the same name.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed as a spelling variant attested for this species, not an alien name. The primary spelling in the source is भरभांड, which is in `discovered` and is the form I would publish; keep only one of the two.

verdicts.name: सत्यानाशी
verdicts.corroboratingSource: eFloraofIndia and Names of Plants in India, Argemone mexicana, Hindi: सत्यानाशी (satyanashi), alongside भरभांड, फिरंगी धतूरा, पीला धतूरा, सियालकांटा.
verdicts.reason: Attested in Devanagari by the flora compilation and the name under which the plant is sold and searched in Hindi. Matches the page slug.

verdicts.name: பிரம்மத் தண்டு
verdicts.corroboratingSource: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Argemone mexicana, Tamil: எலியோட்டி, குருக்கு, குடிக்குச்சகுனி, குடியோட்டுப்பூண்டு, பிரம்மத் தண்டு (piram-mat-tantu).
verdicts.reason: Directly attested in Tamil script for this species; it is the Tamil calque of the Sanskrit ब्रह्मदण्डी, which the same source gives for Argemone mexicana. Not marking it preferred: the source lists five Tamil names and குடியோட்டி forms look at least as current, and I cannot tell which a Tamil speaker would use.

verdicts.name: நிலாவாரை
verdicts.corroboratingSource: CRC World Dictionary of Plant Names, regional names (via wisdomlib's Nilavarai entry), which identifies Nilavarai with Senna alexandrina (syn. Cassia lanceolata), Senna auriculata and Senna italica. Corroborated by IISc Flora of Peninsular India herbsheet for Senna alexandrina, Tamil: 'Ponnavari, Nilavirai', Hindi 'Sanay', Sanskrit 'Svarnapatri'; and by API Part I, SVARNAPATRI (Leaf) = Cassia angustifolia Vahl, Tamil 'Nilapponnai, Avarai', Kannada 'Nelavarike, Nelaavare'.
verdicts.reason: Attested for this species (Cassia angustifolia = Senna alexandrina, the accepted name) by a regional-names dictionary and an academic flora, with API's Tamil ஆவாரை and Kannada nelavarike as the same ground-avarai compound. Flag on the page: CRC gives the same Tamil name for Senna auriculata and Senna italica too, so it is not species-exclusive; bare ஆவாரை in particular means Senna auriculata and must not be used here.

discovered.name: கொடிவேலி
discovered.source: University of Madras Tamil Lexicon and Miron Winslow's Comprehensive Tamil and English Dictionary, via agarathi.com: 'A running plant whose root is a powerful caustic, rose coloured Lead-wort, Plumbago Zeylanica, L.'; Madras Lexicon 'Ceylon leadwort'. Independently in India Flora Online (IISc) as Tamil 'Kodivaeli'.
discovered.reason: The lexicon-attested Tamil name for Plumbago zeylanica, and the one the candidate list is missing. Caveat worth printing: the same lexicons also apply கொடிவேலி/கொடுவேலி to the rose-flowered Plumbago indica (P. rosea), so the species sense should be stated.

discovered.name: चित्रक
discovered.source: India Flora Online (IISc) herbsheet for Plumbago zeylanica, Sanskrit 'Chitraka'; the species is the official source of the API drug Citraka (dried mature root of Plumbago zeylanica Linn.).
discovered.reason: The Ayurvedic head-name and page eponym, absent from the harvested set entirely.

discovered.name: சித்திரமூலம்

discovered.name: கொடிவேலி

discovered.name: अजाजी

discovered.reason: A frequent and genuine Sanskrit name for this species, and notably the real form that the rejected candidate जीरिका seems to be a garble of.

discovered.name: श्वेतजीरक
discovered.source: Wisdom Library entry for Śvetajīraka: 'Cuminum cyminum L. (Jīraka) is also known as Śvetajīraka according to both the Ayurvedic Formulary of India and the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India.'
discovered.reason: Pharmacopoeially sanctioned Sanskrit name, explicitly sourced to the AFI and API, and the one that distinguishes cumin from कृष्णजीरक / कालाजीरा. Absent from the harvest.

discovered.name: दारुहरिद्रा

discovered.name: दार्वी

discovered.name: रसौत

discovered.reason: The Sanskrit head-name and page eponym — the harvest returned no Sanskrit candidate at all for this page.

discovered.name: धवई

discovered.name: त्रुटि

discovered.name: மா
discovered.source: Flowers of India, 'Mango' page: "Tamil: Ma (மா)" — Tamil script.
discovered.reason: The real Tamil name for the species, replacing the constructed இந்திய மா on this page as well.

discovered.name: आम हल्दी
discovered.source: Flowers of India, 'Mango Ginger' page (Curcuma amada): "Hindi: आम हल्दी Am-haldi" — Devanagari.
discovered.reason: This page had NO Hindi candidate at all. Attested in Devanagari, with the Marathi आंबेहळद, Kannada ಅಂಬೆಹಳದಿ, Bengali আমাদা and Urdu ﺁﻣﺒﺎ ﺣﻠﺪﯼ cognates on the same page.

discovered.name: आम्रगन्धा
discovered.source: Flowers of India, 'Mango Ginger' page: "Sanskrit: अम्रगंधा Amragandha".
discovered.reason: This page had no Sanskrit candidate, though it is named amra-haridra. Flagging an orthographic point honestly: Flowers of India prints it अम्रगंधा; the classical spelling of the compound (āmra-gandhā, 'mango-scented') is आम्रगन्धा, which is what I give here. Worth a second check against the API before publishing.

discovered.name: सारिवा
discovered.source: Flowers of India, 'Indian Sarsaparilla' page (Hemidesmus indicus): "Sanskrit: अनंतमूल Anantamul, Sariva"; MMPND Hemidesmus page: Sanskrit "Anantamoola, Sariva".
discovered.reason: The pharmacopoeial Sanskrit name of this drug, attested by two independent sources, and the safe replacement for the ambiguous क्षीरिणी. Both print roman only, so the Devanagari is the standard rendering rather than a direct read.

discovered.name: दूधली
discovered.source: Flowers of India, 'Indian Sarsaparilla' page: "Hindi: अनंतमूल Anantamul, दूधली Dudhli" — Devanagari.
discovered.reason: Second attested Hindi name, read directly in Devanagari, referring to the plant's latex.

discovered.name: अंकोल
discovered.source: Kerala State Medicinal Plants Board (smpbkerala.in), Alangium salviifolium: Hindi "Dhera, Ankol"; ayushvedah.com drug entry for ankola: Hindi "Dhera, Ankol"; SDACH Dravyaguna 'Ankola' monograph: Hindi "Ankol".
discovered.reason: The attested Hindi form, to replace अकोल. Three independent sources agree, all printing roman, so the Devanagari here is the standard rendering of 'Ankol' — flagging that.

discovered.name: ढेरा
discovered.source: Kerala State Medicinal Plants Board, Alangium salviifolium: Hindi "Dhera, Ankol"; ayushvedah.com: Hindi "Dhera, Ankol".
discovered.reason: A Hindi name entirely absent from the harvest, given first by both sources that list two Hindi names. Roman in both sources, so the Devanagari is the standard rendering.

discovered.name: अघाड़ा
discovered.source: Flowers of India, 'Prickly Chaff Flower' page (Achyranthes aspera): "Hindi: अघाड़ा (Aghara), अपामार्ग (Apamarga), चिरचिरा (Chirchira)" — Devanagari; the same page gives Gujarati અઘેડો Aghedo and Urdu اگهاڙا Aghara.
discovered.reason: A genuine Hindi name read directly in Devanagari, listed first by Flowers of India and corroborated across three scripts on the same page — a better-attested alternative than the harvested लटजीरा.

discovered.name: चिरचिरा
discovered.source: Flowers of India, 'Prickly Chaff Flower' page: Hindi "चिरचिरा (Chirchira)" — Devanagari; the same page gives Urdu چرچرا Chirchira.
discovered.reason: Second well-attested Hindi name read in Devanagari, again better corroborated than लटजीरा.

discovered.name: சங்கு கன்னிக்கொடி
discovered.source: Flowers of India, 'Butterfly Pea' page (Clitoria ternatea): "Tamil: சங்கு கன்னிக்கொடி (Kannikkodi)" — Tamil script.
discovered.reason: The Tamil name Flowers of India gives for the species, read directly in Tamil script. It belongs on the page alongside the literary கருவிளை, since the śaṅkha/conch naming (cf. Kannada ಶಂಖಪುಷ್ಪ, Marathi शंख पुष्प on the same page) is the one in current use.

discovered.name: कलौंजी
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, UPAKUNCIKA monograph (seeds of Nigella sativa Linn.) — Hindi slot "Kalaunji, Mangaraila" (api-all.txt line 15250 ff.)
discovered.reason: The page has no Hindi candidate at all. कलौंजी is the official Hindi name for this species and the form every Hindi speaker uses; API also gives मंगरैला. Names are romanised in the API text, so the Devanagari here is a direct transliteration of the source forms.

discovered.name: उपकुञ्चिका
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India — the monograph for Nigella sativa Linn. seeds is itself headed UPAKUNCIKA, and its Sanskrit slot reads "Sthulajiraka, Upakunci, Susavi"
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate. उपकुञ्चिका is the official Sanskrit drug name for Nigella sativa in API, which makes it the single most important missing name on this page.

discovered.name: स्थूलजीरक
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, UPAKUNCIKA monograph (Nigella sativa Linn.) — Sanskrit slot "Sthulajiraka, Upakunci, Susavi"
discovered.reason: Second official Sanskrit synonym, literally 'coarse cumin', distinguishing it from jiraka.

discovered.name: कलौंजी
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, UPAKUNCIKA monograph (seeds of Nigella sativa Linn.) — Hindi slot "Kalaunji, Mangaraila"
discovered.reason: The page slug is itself this Hindi name, yet no Hindi candidate was harvested. API attests it officially for the species.

discovered.name: उपकुञ्चिका
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India — monograph headed UPAKUNCIKA for Nigella sativa Linn. seeds; Sanskrit slot "Sthulajiraka, Upakunci, Susavi"
discovered.reason: Official Sanskrit drug name for this species; absent from the harvested set.

discovered.name: भूनिम्ब
discovered.source: Names of Plants in India :: Andrographis paniculata (Burm.f.) Nees — Sanskrit list "भूनिम्ब bhunimba, कालमेघ kalamegha, महातिक्ता mahatikta, यवतिक्ता yavatikta"; corroborated by efloraofindia's Andrographis paniculata page
discovered.reason: The other major Sanskrit name for this species, and the one classical texts use most ('ground neem'). Worth carrying because it also explains the chirata substitution: API's KIRATATIKTA monograph lists Bhunimba as a Sanskrit synonym for Swertia chirata, so the name is shared between the two drugs.

discovered.name: हरा चिरायता
discovered.source: Names of Plants in India :: Andrographis paniculata — Hindi list "हरा चिरायता hara chirayata, कालमेघ kalmegh, कल्पनाथ kalpanath, किरयित् kirayit, महातीता mahatita"
discovered.reason: Heads the attested Hindi list and is the common market name distinguishing this plant from true chirayata (Swertia chirata).

discovered.name: कल्पनाथ
discovered.source: Names of Plants in India :: Andrographis paniculata — Hindi list, "कल्पनाथ kalpanath"
discovered.reason: Widely used Hindi name for the species, absent from the harvested set.

discovered.name: पद्म
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KAMALA monograph (dried flowers of Nelumbo nucifera Gaertn.) — Sanskrit slot "Abja, Aravinda, Padma, Kalhara, Sitopala, Pankaja" (api-all.txt line 23951 ff.)
discovered.reason: The most important Sanskrit synonym for lotus after कमल, officially attested per monograph.

discovered.name: अरविन्द
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KAMALA (flowers of Nelumbo nucifera) — Sanskrit slot "Abja, Aravinda, Padma, Kalhara, Sitopala, Pankaja"; the same monograph's Tamil slot also carries 'Aravindan'
discovered.reason: Officially attested Sanskrit synonym that has also been borrowed into Tamil for this species.

discovered.name: कँवल
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KAMALA (flowers of Nelumbo nucifera) — Hindi slot "Kamal, Kanwal"
discovered.reason: Second official Hindi form alongside कमल; common in north-western Hindi usage.

discovered.name: पद्म
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KAMALA monograph (dried flowers of Nelumbo nucifera Gaertn.) — Sanskrit slot "Abja, Aravinda, Padma, Kalhara, Sitopala, Pankaja"
discovered.reason: The flower monograph is the right API monograph for a stamen drug, and पद्म is its leading Sanskrit synonym. I found no stamen-specific Sanskrit name in the sources retrieved and am not supplying one from memory.

discovered.name: कँवल
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KAMALA (flowers of Nelumbo nucifera) — Hindi slot "Kamal, Kanwal"
discovered.reason: Second official Hindi form for the species; the page carries only कमल.

discovered.name: पद्मकन्द
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KAMALA monograph (dried rhizome with roots of Nelumbo nucifera Gaertn.) — Sanskrit slot "Padnakanda, Saluka, Ambhoruha" (api-all.txt line 42286 ff.; 'Padnakanda' is an OCR slip for Padmakanda)
discovered.reason: This is the organ-specific official Sanskrit name for the rhizome drug this page is about, and it is exactly what the slug 'kamalakanda' refers to. Far more valuable than the generic कमलम् that was harvested.

discovered.name: शालूक
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KAMALA (rhizome of Nelumbo nucifera) — Sanskrit slot "Padnakanda, Saluka, Ambhoruha"
discovered.reason: Classical Sanskrit name specifically for the lotus rhizome/root-stock, officially attested for this organ.

discovered.name: कमल ककड़ी
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KAMALA (rhizome of Nelumbo nucifera) — Hindi slot "Kamal Kand, Kamal Kakdi"
discovered.reason: The actual Hindi market name for lotus rhizome, which is what this page documents; कमल alone names the plant. API also gives कमल कंद.

discovered.name: தாமரைக் கிழங்கு
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KAMALA (rhizome of Nelumbo nucifera) — Tamil slot "Tamardi Kizangu"
discovered.reason: Organ-specific Tamil name for the rhizome ('lotus tuber'), officially attested, where the harvested தாமரை names only the plant.

discovered.name: काञ्चनारः
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India — the monograph for the stem bark of Bauhinia variegata Blume is headed KANCANARA, with Sanskrit slot "Kancanaraka" (api-all.txt line 7815 ff.); Names of Plants in India :: Bauhinia variegata gives Sanskrit "काञ्चनार kanchanara"
discovered.reason: This is the correct Sanskrit name for the species and the direct replacement for the rejected मन्दारः. Two independent sources, one of them the official pharmacopoeia whose monograph title it is.

discovered.name: कञ्चनारक
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KANCANARA monograph (Bauhinia variegata Blume) — Sanskrit slot "Kancanaraka"
discovered.reason: The only Sanskrit synonym API itself lists for this species, so it carries pharmacopoeial authority the harvested Sanskrit candidate lacked.

discovered.name: செம்மந்தாரை
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KANCANARA monograph (Bauhinia variegata Blume) — Tamil slot "Sigappu mandarai, Sihappu mantarai"; Names of Plants in India :: Bauhinia variegata gives Tamil "செம்மந்தாரை cem-mantarai, சிவப்புமந்தாரை civappu-mantarai"
discovered.reason: The correct Tamil name for this species, and the replacement for the rejected மலையாத்தி. 'Red mandarai' distinguishes B. variegata from the other Bauhinias, which is precisely the distinction the harvested name got wrong.

discovered.name: कचनाल
discovered.source: Names of Plants in India :: Bauhinia variegata L. — Hindi list "कचनाल kachnal, कचनार kachnar"
discovered.reason: Second attested Hindi form alongside the confirmed कचनार.

discovered.name: कङ्कोल
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KANKOLA monograph (mature dried fruits of Piper cubeba Linn.f.) — Sanskrit slot "Kankolaka, Cinosana, Cinatiksna, Kakkola, Kankolika" (api-all.txt line 7974 ff.)
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate, and this is the official Sanskrit drug name the slug itself comes from. It is also where the mis-labelled Hindi candidate कंकोल actually belongs.

discovered.name: कक्कोल
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KANKOLA monograph (Piper cubeba Linn.f.) — Sanskrit slot "Kankolaka, Cinosana, Cinatiksna, Kakkola, Kankolika"
discovered.reason: Officially attested Sanskrit synonym for this species, absent from the harvested set.

discovered.name: रक्तिका
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, GUNJA monographs (seeds, api-all.txt line 6424; root, line 21658, of Abrus precatorius Linn.) — Sanskrit slot "Raktika, Kakananti"; MMPND Abrus page lists Sanskrit "रक्तिका Raktika"
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate. रक्तिका is the official Sanskrit synonym, attested by API and by MMPND in Devanagari, and is the name behind the seed's use as a weight unit.

discovered.name: रत्ती
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, GUNJA monographs (Abrus precatorius Linn.) — Hindi slot "Ratti, Ghungchi"; MMPND Abrus page lists "रत्ती Ratti" under Hindi
discovered.reason: API's official Hindi name for this species and the form a Hindi speaker is most likely to use or search, which the harvested गुंजा is not.

discovered.name: घुंघची
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, GUNJA monographs (Abrus precatorius Linn.) — Hindi slot "Ratti, Ghungchi"
discovered.reason: Second official Hindi name for the species, absent from the harvested set.

discovered.name: குன்றிமணி
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, GUNJA monographs (Abrus precatorius Linn.) — Tamil slots "Kuntri, Kunrimani, Kundamani" and "Kunrimani, Kundumani"; MMPND Abrus page lists Tamil "குன்றிமணி"
discovered.reason: The seed-specific Tamil form ('kunri bead'), which is how the drug is actually named in Tamil; the harvested குன்றி is the bare stem.

discovered.name: आत्मगुप्ता
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India — both monographs for Mucuna prurita Hook. syn. M. pruriens (seed, api-all.txt line 37197; root, line 56834) are headed ATMAGUPTA; Names of Plants in India :: Mucuna pruriens gives Sanskrit "आत्मगुप्ता (Atmagupta)"
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate, and आत्मगुप्ता is the official Sanskrit drug name API uses for this species. Two independent sources.

discovered.name: कपिकच्छुः
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, ATMAGUPTA monographs (Mucuna prurita Hook. syn. M. pruriens) — Sanskrit slots "Kapikacchu, Markati, Kandura" and "Kapikacchu, Markai, Kandura, Sukasimbi, Kapiprabha"
discovered.reason: This is the Sanskrit name the page slug is built from, officially attested in both organ monographs, yet it was not harvested at all.

discovered.name: मर्कटी
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, ATMAGUPTA monographs (Mucuna pruriens) — Sanskrit slots "Kapikacchu, Markati, Kandura"
discovered.reason: Officially attested Sanskrit synonym ('monkey plant'), matching the English common names monkey tamarind and cowhage.

discovered.name: कौंच
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, ATMAGUPTA monographs (Mucuna pruriens) — Hindi slots "Kewanch, Kaunch" and "Kevanch, Kaunch, Khujanee"; Names of Plants in India :: Mucuna pruriens also lists Kauncha
discovered.reason: The commonest Hindi name for this species and the one a speaker would search; the harvested किवांच is a variant of the Kevanch form.

discovered.name: कैथ
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KAPITTHA monograph (dried pulp of mature fruit of Feronia limonia (Linn.) Swingle = Limonia acidissima, api-all.txt line 24166 ff.) — Hindi slot "Kaitha"; MMPND Limonia page lists Hindi "कैट Kait, कैथ Kait, कैथा Kaitha"
discovered.reason: The official Hindi name for this species and the everyday word for wood apple, attested by API and by MMPND in Devanagari. It is the Hindi form that should be preferred over the three that were harvested.

discovered.name: दधित्थ
discovered.source: MMPND Limonia page lists under Sanskrit "Dadhi, दधिफल Dadhiphala, Dadhistha, दधित्थ Dadhittha, ..."; API's KAPITTHA monograph Sanskrit slot gives "Danta Satha, Kapipriya"
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate. दधित्थ is a major classical Sanskrit name for wood apple, attested in Devanagari by MMPND for this species.

discovered.name: दन्तशठ
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KAPITTHA monograph (Feronia limonia = Limonia acidissima) — Sanskrit slot "Danta Satha, Kapipriya"; MMPND Limonia page lists Sanskrit "दन्तशठ Danthashatha"
discovered.reason: Officially attested Sanskrit synonym for this species, corroborated in Devanagari by MMPND. Worth noting it is also used for Averrhoa carambola (which appears in this same batch), so it is a shared name.

discovered.name: விளாமரம்
discovered.source: MMPND Limonia page lists Tamil "விளா Vila (viḷā), விளா மரம் Vilamaram, விளாம்பழம் Vilam palam, ..."; API's KAPITTHA monograph Tamil slot gives "Vilamaram, Vilangai"
discovered.reason: The full tree name, which is what API actually prints; the harvested விளா is the bare stem. Both attested, so both belong on the page.

discovered.name: करञ्जकः
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KARANJA monographs (seeds, api-all.txt line 8646; root bark, line 24555, of Pongamia pinnata (Linn.) Merr. = Millettia pinnata) — Sanskrit slot "Karanjaka, Naktamala, Naktahva, Ghrtakaranja"
discovered.reason: The officially attested Sanskrit synonym, and the correct replacement for the rejected constructed compound करञ्जवृक्षः.

discovered.name: नक्तमालः
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KARANJA monographs (Pongamia pinnata = Millettia pinnata) — Sanskrit slot "Karanjaka, Naktamala, Naktahva, Ghrtakaranja"
discovered.reason: Major classical Sanskrit name for this species, attested identically in both organ monographs, and entirely missing from the harvested set.

discovered.name: घृतकरञ्जः
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KARANJA monographs (Pongamia pinnata = Millettia pinnata) — Sanskrit slot "Karanjaka, Naktamala, Naktahva, Ghrtakaranja"
discovered.reason: Officially attested Sanskrit synonym, and a useful one because it distinguishes this karanja (the oil-yielding one) from the other plants that share the karanja name.

discovered.name: कठिल्लः
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KARAVALLAKA monograph (fresh fruit of Momordica charantia Linn.) — Sanskrit slot "Karavella, Kathilla, Varivalli, Karavalli"; efloraofindia / Names of Plants in India :: Momordica charantia gives Sanskrit "कटिल्लः kathillah"
discovered.reason: Officially attested second Sanskrit name for this species, corroborated in Devanagari by an independent compilation.

discovered.name: பாகற்காய்
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KARAVALLAKA monograph (Momordica charantia Linn.) — Tamil slot "Paharkai"; efloraofindia / Names of Plants in India :: Momordica charantia gives Tamil "பாகற்காய் pagakkai"
discovered.reason: The Tamil form the authoritative sources actually print, and the replacement for the unverified bare stem பாகல். Attested by the official monograph and in Tamil script by an independent compilation.

discovered.name: कठिल्ल
discovered.source: efloraofindia / Names of Plants in India :: Momordica charantia — Hindi list "करेला karela, कठिल्ल kathilla, परारु poraru"
discovered.reason: Second attested Hindi name for this species, from the Sanskrit कठिल्ल.

discovered.name: பாகற்காய்
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KARAVALLAKA monograph (Momordica charantia Linn.) — Tamil slot "Paharkai"; efloraofindia / Names of Plants in India gives Tamil "பாகற்காய் pagakkai"
discovered.reason: The attested Tamil form, replacing the unverified பாகல் on this page too.

discovered.name: कठिल्लः
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KARAVALLAKA monograph (Momordica charantia Linn.) — Sanskrit slot "Karavella, Kathilla, Varivalli, Karavalli"; efloraofindia gives "कटिल्लः kathillah"
discovered.reason: Officially attested Sanskrit synonym for this species, missing from the harvested set.

discovered.name: करीरः
discovered.source: Names of Plants in India :: Capparis decidua (Forssk.) Edgew. — Sanskrit list "दीर्घपत्त्रक dirghapattraka, ग्रन्थिक granthika, ग्रन्थिल granthila, गूढपत्त्र gudhapattra, करीर karira, क्रकर krakara, कुरर kurara, मरुभूरुह marubhuruha, निष्पत्त्रिका nishpattrika, ताम्रपत्त्रक tamrapattraka, तीक्ष्णकण्टक tikshnakantaka, वेणुकर्कर venukarkara"
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate at all, and करीर is the Sanskrit name the slug 'karira' comes from. Attested in Devanagari for this exact species.

discovered.name: करील
discovered.source: Names of Plants in India :: Capparis decidua — Hindi list "कैर kair, कैरिया kairiya, करीर karir, करील karil, करीं kareen, पीचू pichu, टींट teent, टेंटी tenti"
discovered.reason: Attested Hindi variant alongside the confirmed कैर, and the form closest to the Sanskrit.

discovered.name: टींट
discovered.source: Names of Plants in India :: Capparis decidua — Hindi list includes "टींट teent, टेंटी tenti"
discovered.reason: The Hindi name for the fruit of this species, widely used in Rajasthan where the plant is a food source; not harvested.

discovered.name: செங்கம்
discovered.source: Names of Plants in India :: Capparis decidua — Tamil list "சிரக்கோழி cira-k-koli, குழலாதொண்டை kulal-atontai, கெந்திகம் kentikam, மருபூருகம் maru-purukam, செங்கம் senkam"
discovered.reason: The page has no Tamil candidate; this is an attested Tamil name for the species in Tamil script.

discovered.name: कर्मरङ्गः
discovered.source: Names of Plants in India / efloraofindia :: Averrhoa carambola — Sanskrit list "कर्मरंग (karmaranga), कर्मरकः (karmarakah)"
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate, yet the slug 'karmaranga' is itself this Sanskrit name. Attested in Devanagari for this exact species.

discovered.name: தமரத்தை
discovered.source: flowersofindia.net Star Fruit page lists Tamil "Tamarattai" for Averrhoa carambola; Names of Plants in India / efloraofindia gives Tamil "கந்தசட்கம் kantacatkam, தமரத்தை tamarattai, தாமரத்தம்பழம் tamarattampazam"
discovered.reason: The page has no Tamil candidate. தமரத்தை is attested for this species by two independent compilations, one in Tamil script.

discovered.name: करमल
discovered.source: flowersofindia.net Star Fruit page — Hindi "Karmal करमल" for Averrhoa carambola
discovered.reason: A second attested Hindi form. Recorded because flowersofindia gives this as the Hindi name and places कमरख under Urdu, so the two compilations disagree on the label; having both on the page is more honest than either alone.

discovered.name: பருத்தி
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KARPASA monograph (seeds devoid of lint of Gossypium herbaceum Linn., Fam. Malvaceae, api-all.txt line 9215 ff.) — Tamil slot "Parutti kkoottam"; MMPND Gossypium page gives Tamil "Nattupparutti, Talipparutti, Venparutti" and Parutti/Parutthi across the genus
discovered.reason: This is the real Tamil name for cotton and the replacement for the malformed harvested string. Attested by the official pharmacopoeia and by MMPND. API's full form பருத்திக் கொட்டை names the seed, which is what this monograph covers.

discovered.name: கற்பாசம்
discovered.source: MMPND (plantnames.unimelb.edu.au/Sorting/Gossypium.html) — Tamil names for Gossypium herbaceum "Karbasam, Karpasam, Nattupparutti, Talipparutti, Venparutti"
discovered.reason: The Tamil form of the Sanskrit कार्पास, and the Tamil name closest to the page slug; attested for this exact species.

discovered.name: कार्पासः
discovered.source: MMPND Gossypium page — Sanskrit "Karpasa, Karpasah, Karpasaha" for Gossypium herbaceum; the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India monograph for this species is itself headed KARPASA and its synonym block carries "Karpasa, Tula"
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate although the slug is this name. Attested by MMPND and by API's own monograph title.

discovered.name: कपास
discovered.source: MMPND Gossypium page — Hindi "Kapas, Rui" for Gossypium herbaceum; API's KARPASA monograph Hindi slot gives "Kapasa, Binaula"
discovered.reason: The page has no Hindi candidate. कपास is the ordinary Hindi word for cotton and is attested for this species by both sources.

discovered.name: बिनौला
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KARPASA monograph (seeds of Gossypium herbaceum Linn.) — Hindi slot "Kapasa, Binaula"
discovered.reason: The Hindi name specifically for the cotton seed, which is exactly the drug this monograph and page cover, so it is more precise than कपास here.

discovered.name: பருத்தி
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, KARPASA monograph (Gossypium herbaceum Linn.) — Tamil slot "Parutti kkoottam"; MMPND Gossypium page gives Parutti/Nattupparutti/Talipparutti/Venparutti
discovered.reason: Replacement for the malformed harvested Tamil string on the root-drug page. பருத்தி is the species name; the root would be பருத்தி வேர்.

discovered.name: कार्पासः
discovered.source: MMPND Gossypium page — Sanskrit "Karpasa, Karpasah, Karpasaha"; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India monograph headed KARPASA for Gossypium herbaceum Linn.
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate; this is the species name the slug is built from (karpasa-moola = cotton root).

discovered.name: कपास
discovered.source: MMPND Gossypium page — Hindi "Kapas, Rui"; API's KARPASA monograph Hindi slot "Kapasa, Binaula"
discovered.reason: The page has no Hindi candidate; कपास is the standard Hindi name for the species.

discovered.name: भांग
discovered.reason: The ordinary Hindi name for the plant, and the one a Hindi speaker searches.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Hindi list for Cannabis sativa (Wayback capture 2020-11-04); DDSA A Practical Hindi-English Dictionary: 'Bhāṃga (भांग): the intoxicating hemp — Cannabis sativa'.

discovered.name: गांजा
discovered.reason: Second common Hindi name, recorded across the Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Nepali and Odia entries of the same list.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Hindi list for Cannabis sativa (as गांझा; गांजा in the Nepali and Odia entries of the same page).

discovered.name: भङ्ग
discovered.reason: The Sanskrit name this page is titled after, attested for the species rather than inferred.
discovered.source: Wisdom Library 'Local Names of Plants and Drugs': 'Bhanga [भांग] in the Sanskrit language … identified with Cannabis sativa L.'; 'Names of Plants in India' Sanskrit list: भङ्ग bhanga.

discovered.name: विजया
discovered.reason: A standard classical Sanskrit synonym for the drug, absent from the harvested set.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Sanskrit list for Cannabis sativa: विजया vijaya (alongside इन्द्राशन, गञ्ज, मादिनी, शण).

discovered.name: கஞ்சா
discovered.reason: The only Tamil name the source records for this species; the harvested set had no Tamil candidate at all.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Tamil entry for Cannabis sativa: கஞ்சா kancha.

discovered.name: मार्कवः
discovered.reason: A primary classical Sanskrit synonym, attested in the oldest lexica, and missing from the harvested set.
discovered.source: Monier-Williams (via wisdomlib): 'Mārkava — m. Eclipta Prostrata', cited to Amarakośa 2.4.5.17 and Hemacandra's Abhidhānacintāmaṇi 1187; also the 15th-century Yogasārasaṅgraha, where Mārkava is given as another name for Bhṛṅgarāja.

discovered.name: केशराजः
discovered.reason: The 'king of hair' synonym that underlies this plant's entire hair-oil reputation; worth a monograph line.
discovered.source: Monier-Williams (via wisdomlib): 'Keśarāja — m. Eclipta prostrata', cited to the lexicographers (Amarasiṃha, Halāyudha, Hemacandra). Note the same entry also lists Wedelia calendulacea, so it is not exclusive.

discovered.name: भांगरा
discovered.reason: The indigenous Hindi name, as distinct from the Sanskrit भृंगराज carried into Hindi.
discovered.source: wisdomlib Ayurveda glossary for Bhṛṅgarāja: 'in the Hindi language it is known as Bhāṅgrā or Bhāṅgarā'.

discovered.name: கீழாநெல்லி
discovered.reason: The canonical single-word Tamil spelling, as the naming authorities print it, rather than the spaced harvested form.
discovered.source: DDSA: University of Madras Tamil Lexicon, Kīḻānelli (கீழாநெல்லி); Wisdom Library 'Local Names of Plants and Drugs', Kila-nelli [கீழாநெல்லி] = Phyllanthus fraternus G.L.Webster.

discovered.name: भूम्यामलकी
discovered.reason: The Sanskrit drug name this page is titled after, attested in classical sources; the harvested set had no Sanskrit candidate.
discovered.source: wisdomlib: 'Bhūmyāmalakī (भूम्यामलकी) — another name for Tāmalakī (Phyllanthus amarus)', from the 7th-century Mādhavacikitsā (Jvaracikitsā); Apte quotes Bhāvaprakāśa: स्याद् भूम्यामलकी तिक्ता कषाया मधुरा हिमा. Attested for P. amarus, the same taxonomic complex as P. fraternus.

discovered.name: भूर्जः
discovered.reason: The Sanskrit name this page is titled after, attested for Betula utilis specifically; the harvested set had no Sanskrit candidate.
discovered.source: wisdomlib Ayurveda glossary: 'Bhūrja (भूर्ज) refers to the medicinal plant known as Betula utilis D. Don', dealt with in the 15th-century Yogasārasaṅgraha of Vāsudeva; Apte quotes Rājanighaṇṭu: भूर्जः कटुः कषायोष्णो भूतरक्षाकरः परः.

discovered.name: गंधत्रिण
discovered.reason: The Hindi name the authority actually gives for this species, in place of the English-loan transliteration that was harvested.
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Lemon Grass page (Cymbopogon citratus): 'Hindi: गंधत्रिण Gandhatrina'.

discovered.name: கர்ப்பூரப்புல்
discovered.reason: The Tamil name the authority gives for this species, in place of the ambiguous நரந்தம் புல்.
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Lemon Grass page (Cymbopogon citratus): 'Tamil: கர்ப்பூரப்புல் Karppurappul'.

discovered.name: भूस्तृण
discovered.reason: The Sanskrit name attested for this species; the harvested set had no Sanskrit candidate, and the page's own title word भूतिक is attested elsewhere (see note below).
discovered.source: Wisdom Library 'Local Names of Plants and Drugs': 'Bhustrina in the Sanskrit language is the name of a plant identified with Cymbopogon citratus (DC.) Stapf'; Flowers of India gives Sanskrit Bhustrina; Śabda-Sāgara: 'Bhūstṛṇa — a fragrant grass'.

discovered.name: विभीतकः
discovered.reason: The attested Sanskrit form (with बिभीतकः), to replace the coined बिभीतकीवृक्षः.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Sanskrit list for Terminalia bellirica: अक्षः, बहुवीर्य, बिभीतकः, कर्षः, कासघ्नः, विभीतकः; wisdomlib: Bibhītaka = Terminalia bellirica (7th-century Mādhavacikitsā; Dharmaśāstra).

discovered.name: अक्षः
discovered.reason: A classical synonym recording the historical use of the seeds as gambling dice; absent from the harvested set.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Sanskrit list for Terminalia bellirica: अक्षः (akshah); corroborated by wisdomlib 'Essentials of Ayurveda' note that 'in early times its seeds were used as dice in gambling'.

discovered.name: कर्षफल
discovered.reason: A further Hindi name from the same authority, alongside बहुवीर्य and भूतवास.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Hindi list for Terminalia bellirica: बहेड़ा, बहुवीर्य, भूतवास, कल्क, कर्षफल.

discovered.name: बीजपूर
discovered.reason: The Sanskrit name this page is titled after, attested for Citrus medica, in place of the wrong नागरङ्गफलम्.
discovered.source: Apte (via wisdomlib): 'Bījapūra (बीजपूर) — the citron tree. -ram, -rakam the fruit of citron'; wisdomlib also records बीजपूर as 'citron' in the 17th-century Bhojanakutūhala.

discovered.name: मातुलुङ्ग
discovered.reason: The other principal Sanskrit name for the citron, attested in both lexicon and kāvya.
discovered.source: Apte: 'Mātuluṅga — A kind of citron tree' (quoting Mālatīmādhava 6.19), '-gam the fruit of this tree, a citron'; 'Names of Plants in India' Sanskrit list for Citrus medica includes मातुलुङ्ग.

discovered.name: மாதுலங்கம்
discovered.reason: A Tamil name the authority actually gives for Citrus medica, unlike the harvested நாரத்தம்பழம்.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Tamil list for Citrus medica: கொம்மட்டிமாதுளை, மாதுலங்கம், பீதபூரம் (Flowers of India's Citron page adds பேரெலுமிச்சை).

discovered.name: गलगल
discovered.reason: The Hindi name for this species; the harvested set had no Hindi candidate for the page at all.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Hindi list for Citrus medica: गलगल (galgal), पूरक (purak), तुरन्ज (turanj), वेतस (vetas).

discovered.name: श्रीफलः
discovered.reason: The same name the harvest placed in the Hindi field is attested first and foremost as Sanskrit for this species, so it belongs in the Sanskrit list too.
discovered.source: Apte: 'Śrīphala (श्रीफल) — the Bilva tree'; Śabda-Sāgara: 'A fruit tree, (Ægle marmelos)'.

discovered.name: बिल्वफल
discovered.reason: The attested Sanskrit compound for the bael fruit, which is the drug this page covers.
discovered.source: wisdomlib: 'Bilvaphala (बिल्वफल) refers to the fruits of bilva (bael)', from the 17th-century Bhojanakutūhala (dravyaguṇāguṇa-kathana).

discovered.name: बेलपत्र
discovered.reason: The attested Hindi name for the bael leaf, which is exactly this page's drug and was missing from the harvested set.
discovered.source: DDSA A Practical Hindi-English Dictionary (via wisdomlib), s.v. बेल: '-[patra] leaves of wood-apple'; s.v. विल्व: '~[patra] leaves of the wood apple tree'.

discovered.name: बिम्बी
discovered.reason: The Sanskrit plant name proper for this species (the page's own title word), as against the fruit compound बिम्बफलम् that was harvested.
discovered.source: Rāja Nighaṇṭu (13th c.) verse 3.64-65 via wisdomlib: 'Bimbī (बिम्बी) is another name for Tiktatuṇḍī, a medicinal plant identified with Coccinia indica'; Monier-Williams: 'Bimbī — Momordica Monadelpha, [Suśruta]'.

discovered.name: तिक्ततुण्डी
discovered.reason: The head synonym under which the Rāja Nighaṇṭu files this plant; absent from the harvested set.
discovered.source: wisdomlib: 'Tiktatuṇḍī (तिक्ततुण्डी) is the Sanskrit name for a medicinal plant identified with Coccinia indica', Rāja Nighaṇṭu 3.64-65; Monier-Williams cites it to the lexicographers.

discovered.name: कुन्द्रू
discovered.reason: The correctly attested Hindi name, to replace the unattested कुंदुरी.
discovered.source: Wisdom Library 'Local Names of Plants and Drugs': 'Kundru [कुन्द्रू] in the Hindi language … identified with Coccinia grandis (L.) Voigt'; Flowers of India (Ivy Gourd): 'Hindi: कुन्द्रू Kundru'; Rāja Nighaṇṭu 3.64-65 glosses Tiktatuṇḍī as 'commonly known in Hindi as Kundarū'.

discovered.name: கோவை
discovered.reason: The variant Tamil form the compilations print alongside the Lexicon's கொவ்வை; useful as a search alias.
discovered.source: Flowers of India (Ivy Gourd): 'Tamil: கோவை Kovai'; Rāja Nighaṇṭu 3.64-65 (via wisdomlib) gives the Tamil as Kovaikaī.

discovered.name: कारवेल्लकः
discovered.reason: The form the authorities actually cite, worth carrying beside the harvested कारवेल्लम्.
discovered.source: Flowers of India (Bitter Gourd): 'Sanskrit: कारवेल्लकः kaarvellakah'; wisdomlib Ayurveda: 'Kāravellaka (कारवेल्लक) or Kareli — Momordica charantia', 17th-century Vaidyavallabha of Hastiruci.

discovered.name: सुषवी
discovered.reason: A classical Sanskrit synonym absent from the harvested set.
discovered.source: Flowers of India (Bitter Gourd) Sanskrit list: कारवेल्लकः, कटिल्लः, परारु, सुषवी, ऊर्ध्वासितः.

discovered.name: பாகற்காய்
discovered.reason: The fruit form in everyday Tamil market use, beside the plant name பாகல்.
discovered.source: Flowers of India (Bitter Gourd): 'Tamil: இராசவள்ளி iraca-valli, பாகற்காய் pAgakkai'.

discovered.name: कारवेल्लकः
discovered.reason: The form the authorities actually cite, worth carrying beside the harvested कारवेल्लम्.
discovered.source: Flowers of India (Bitter Gourd): 'Sanskrit: कारवेल्लकः kaarvellakah'; wisdomlib Ayurveda: Kāravellaka = Momordica charantia, 17th-century Vaidyavallabha.

discovered.name: कठिल्ल
discovered.reason: A second Hindi name recorded by the authority, beside करेला.
discovered.source: Flowers of India (Bitter Gourd): 'Hindi: करेला Karela, कठिल्ल kathilla, परारु poraru'.

discovered.name: जलनीम
discovered.reason: A species-specific Hindi name that avoids the brahmi/Centella ambiguity; missing from the harvested set.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Hindi list for Bacopa monnieri: बाम, ब्राह्मी, जलबूटी, जलनीम, नीरब्राह्मी, सफेद चमनी.

discovered.name: नीरब्राह्मी
discovered.reason: The water-qualified Hindi form, which distinguishes Bacopa from the Centella sense of brahmi.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Hindi list for Bacopa monnieri: नीरब्राह्मी; the same page gives Marathi जलब्राह्मी / नीर ब्राह्मी and Kannada ಜಲ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಿ / ನೀರು ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಿ.

discovered.name: तिक्तलोणिका
discovered.reason: The second Sanskrit name the authorities give for this species, absent from the harvested set.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Sanskrit entry for Bacopa monnieri: ब्राह्मी brahmi, तिक्तलोणिका tiktalonika; Flowers of India's Brahmi page gives the same pair.

discovered.name: பிரமி
discovered.reason: The short Tamil form, recorded beside நீர்ப்பிரமி.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Tamil list for Bacopa monnieri: நீர்ப்பிரமி, பிரமி, பிரமியம், தராய்.

discovered.name: श्रीखण्ड
discovered.reason: The genuine Sanskrit counterpart of the Kannada श्रीगंध that was wrongly harvested as Sanskrit.
discovered.source: Śabda-Sāgara (via wisdomlib): 'Śrīkhaṇḍa (श्रीखण्ड) — Sandal-wood'; Benfey: 'sandal-wood or the sandal-tree'; 'Names of Plants in India' Sanskrit list for Santalum album includes श्रीखण्ड.

discovered.name: मलयज
discovered.reason: A classical Sanskrit synonym naming the Malaya hills source of sandalwood; absent from the harvested set.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' extended Sanskrit list for Santalum album: मलयज malayaja (with गन्धसार, गन्धराज, पटीर, हरिगन्ध, चन्द्रद्युति, पीतसार).

discovered.name: गन्धसार
discovered.reason: Another attested Sanskrit synonym, useful for nighantu cross-referencing.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' extended Sanskrit list for Santalum album: गन्धसार gandhasara.

discovered.name: संदल
discovered.reason: The second Hindi name the authority records, from the Persian/Arabic sandal.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Hindi list for Santalum album: चन्दन chandan, संदल sandal.

discovered.name: चन्द्रशूर
discovered.reason: The Sanskrit name this page is titled after, attested for Lepidium sativum; the harvested set had no Sanskrit candidate.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Sanskrit entry for Lepidium sativum: चन्द्रशूर (chandrashura), रक्तराजी (raktaraji).

discovered.name: रक्तराजी
discovered.reason: The second Sanskrit name recorded for this species.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Sanskrit entry for Lepidium sativum: चन्द्रशूर, रक्तराजी.

discovered.name: चनसुर
discovered.reason: The Hindi name for this species; the harvested set had no Hindi candidate for the page.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Hindi entry for Lepidium sativum: चनसुर (chansur), हालिम (halim); Flowers of India (Garden Cress) gives the same.

discovered.name: हालिम
discovered.reason: The commoner trade name for the seed in Hindi, recorded by the same authority and echoed in Assamese, Bengali, Odia, Sindhi and Urdu.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' Hindi entry for Lepidium sativum: हालिम (halim).

discovered.name: ஆளி
discovered.reason: The short Tamil form the authorities print as the headword, beside ஆளிவிரை.
discovered.source: 'Names of Plants in India' and Flowers of India (Garden Cress), Tamil entry for Lepidium sativum: ஆளி (Ali).

discovered.name: अमरुल
discovered.reason: The everyday Hindi name for this species, which the harvested set lacked entirely.
discovered.source: Wisdom Library 'Local Names of Plants and Drugs': 'Amrul [अम्रुल] in the Hindi language is the name of a plant identified with Oxalis corniculata L.'; corroborated in the indiantreepix thread on Oxalis corniculata ('Both in Hindi and Bengali it is called Amrul').

discovered.name: अम्लिका
discovered.reason: An attested Sanskrit name for wood sorrel, absent from the harvested set, which had no Sanskrit candidate.
discovered.source: Śabda-Sāgara (via wisdomlib): 'Amlikā (अम्लिका) — Wood sorrel, (Oxalis corniculata)'; Apte: 'Amlikā — 3) Wood-sorrel; also पलाशीलता, श्वेताम्लिका and क्षुद्राम्लिका'. Note the same word also means the tamarind tree, so it needs a qualifier on the page.

discovered.name: ஆயா
discovered.reason: The correctly attested Tamil name for this species, to replace ஆவு மரம்.
discovered.source: DDSA: University of Madras Tamil Lexicon: 'Āyā (ஆயா) — Entire-leaved elm, medium tree, Holoptelea integrifolia'; Wisdom Library 'Local Names of Plants and Drugs': 'Aya [ஆயா] in the Tamil language … Holoptelea integrifolia (Roxb.) Planch.'; Flowers of India (Indian Elm): 'Tamil: ஆயா Aya'.

discovered.name: चिलबिल
discovered.reason: The principal attested Hindi name for this species, to replace चिरोल.
discovered.source: Flowers of India (Indian Elm) and the bodhi-nighantu compilation for Holoptelea integrifolia: Hindi चिलबिल (Chilbil), कान्जू (Kanju), पपड़ी (Papri).

discovered.name: पपड़ी
discovered.reason: A second attested Hindi name, from the tree's flaking corky bark.
discovered.source: Flowers of India (Indian Elm) / bodhi-nighantu Holoptelea integrifolia entry: Hindi पपड़ी (Papri).

discovered.name: चिरिबिल्वः
discovered.reason: The Sanskrit name this page is titled after, as the compilations actually spell it; the harvested set had no Sanskrit candidate.
discovered.source: Flowers of India (Indian Elm): 'Sanskrit: चिरिविल्वः Chirivilva'; bodhi-nighantu Holoptelea integrifolia entry: चिरिविल्वः, चिरबिल्व, पूतिक, उदकीर्य.

discovered.name: कृतमालः
discovered.source: Monier-Williams p.302, quoted in the Pandanus record for Cassia fistula: "kṛtamāla, m. ... the tree Cassia fistula Suśr."; also API Vol I, ĀRAGVADHA, Sanskrit: Kṛtamāla
discovered.reason: The second Sanskrit name Pandanus gives for the species, attested in Suśruta, and carried by the pharmacopoeia. A sound replacement for the rejected अरग्वदवृक्षः.

discovered.name: आरग्वधः
discovered.source: Monier-Williams p.149, quoted in the Pandanus record for Cassia fistula: "āragvadha, as, m. the tree Cathartocarpus (Cassia) Fistula, Bhpr.; Suśr."
discovered.reason: The correctly spelled form of the name the page is titled after, with ध and without the -वृक्षः suffix.

discovered.name: சரக்கொன்றை
discovered.source: API Vol I, ĀRAGVADHA, Tamil: Sarakonrai, Sarak konnai, Sharakkonrai; Tamil Lexicon p.1168 cross-refers கொன்றை to சரக்கொன்றை
discovered.reason: API's first-listed Tamil name and the Lexicon's own cross-reference target; the specific compound as against the generic கொன்றை.

discovered.name: अर्जुन
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Terminalia, Terminalia arjuna, HINDI: अर्जुन Arjun, Arjuna (in Devanagari); API Vol II, ARJUNA, Hindi: Arjuna; Pandanus, Hindi: arjun
discovered.reason: The one-word Hindi name that should replace the harvested 'अर्जुन वृक्ष'.

discovered.name: ककुभः
discovered.source: Monier-Williams p.241, quoted in the Pandanus record for Terminalia arjuna: "the tree Terminalia arjuna MBh. Suśr. &c."; API Vol II, ARJUNA, Sanskrit: Kakubha
discovered.reason: The principal classical synonym besides अर्जुन, attested in the Mahābhārata and Suśruta and listed first by API. Pandanus also records it as the Prakrit name.

discovered.name: நீர்மருது
discovered.source: Tamil Lexicon p.2306: "நீர்மருது nīr-marutu, n. Arjuna, 1. tr., Terminalia arjuna" — the only hit in a full-text Lexicon search for 'Terminalia arjuna'; also Pandanus, Tamil: nīrmarutu
discovered.reason: The Lexicon's own Tamil name for this species, and the correct replacement for the rejected வெண் மருது.

discovered.name: வெள்ளைமருது
discovered.source: Tamil Lexicon p.3803: "வெள்ளைமருது veḷḷai-marutu, n. பூமருது, 1. 2. Arjuna. See நீர்மருது"; Pandanus record for Terminalia arjuna, Tamil: veḷḷaimarutu
discovered.reason: The 'white marutu' name the Lexicon does allow for arjuna, as against வெண்மருது which it gives only for Terminalia paniculata.

discovered.name: மருதம்
discovered.source: API Vol II, ARJUNA (Terminalia arjuna), Tamil: Marudam; Tamil Lexicon p.3093 "marutu: 1. Arjuna"
discovered.reason: API's official Tamil name for the Arjuna monograph.

discovered.name: आक
discovered.source: API Vol I, ARKA (Root) and ARKA (Leaf), Calotropis procera, Hindi: Aak, Madar, Akavana; Pandanus record for Calotropis, Hindi: āk, madār
discovered.reason: The Hindi name for this species is absent from the harvested set entirely — the Arka pages carry no Hindi candidate at all.

discovered.name: मदार
discovered.source: API Vol I, ARKA (Root) and ARKA (Leaf), Hindi: Aak, Madar, Akavana, Urdu: Madar, Aak; Pandanus, Hindi: madār
discovered.reason: Second Hindi name, given by both API and Pandanus; also the source of the English 'madar'.

discovered.name: अर्कः
discovered.source: Monier-Williams p.89, quoted in the Pandanus record for Calotropis: "arka ... the plant Calotropis Gigantea ... ŚBr. &c."; API Vol I monograph title ARKA, botanical source Calotropis procera
discovered.reason: The Sanskrit name the page is titled after is missing from the candidate list. Note the lexicographic split the page may want to record: Monier-Williams and Pandanus attach arka to Calotropis gigantea, while API assigns the Arka monograph to C. procera — the same C. procera / C. gigantea tension as the Tamil name.

discovered.name: विजयसार
discovered.source: API Vol I, ASANA (Pterocarpus marsupium Roxb.), Hindi: Vijayasara, Bija; Pandanus record for Pterocarpus marsupium, Hindi: vijaysār
discovered.reason: API's first-listed Hindi name, and the correct replacement for the transliterated-binomial candidate.

discovered.name: बिजासाल
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Pterocarpus, Pterocarpus marsupium, HINDI: Banda, Bija, Bijasal, Bijasar, Biya; Pandanus, Hindi: bijasāl
discovered.reason: The commonest trade name for the heartwood in Hindi, given by both MMPND and Pandanus.

discovered.name: बीजकः
discovered.source: API Vol I, ASANA, Sanskrit: Bījaka, Pītasāra, Asanaka, Bījasāra; Pandanus record for Pterocarpus marsupium, Sanskrit: asana, bījaka
discovered.reason: API and Pandanus agree on this synonym. Worth a caution on the page: Monier-Williams p.732 glosses bījaka as Terminalia tomentosa, and p.118 glosses asana the same way, so both Sanskrit names for this monograph are shared with a Terminalia in the older lexicons.

discovered.name: अशोकः
discovered.source: Monier-Williams p.113, quoted in the Pandanus record for Saraca asoca: "aśoka ... m. the tree Jonesia Asoka Roxb."; API Vol I monograph title AŚOKA
discovered.reason: The plain Sanskrit name, which no candidate supplies — the three Sanskrit candidates on this page are two -वृक्ष compounds and the Ficus error.

discovered.name: कङ्केलिः
discovered.source: API Vol I, AŚOKA (Saraca asoca), Sanskrit: Kaṅkeli
discovered.reason: The only Sanskrit synonym API gives for the Aśoka monograph; absent from the harvested set.

discovered.name: अशोक
discovered.source: Platts p.58: "اشوك अशोक aśok ... The tree Jonesia aśoka" and p.54 असोक asok, same gloss; API Vol I, AŚOKA, Hindi: Ashoka
discovered.reason: The one-word Hindi name to replace 'अशोक वृक्ष'.

discovered.name: அசோகம்
discovered.source: Tamil Lexicon p.35: "அசோகம் acōkam ... 2. Ašōka tree, m. tr., Saraca indica"; API Vol I, AŚOKA, Tamil: Asogam, Asogu, Asokam; Pandanus, Tamil: acōkam
discovered.reason: API's first-listed Tamil name and the form Pandanus gives; a useful second Tamil entry alongside அசோகு.

discovered.name: अश्वगन्धा
discovered.source: Monier-Williams p.115, quoted in the Pandanus record for Withania somnifera: "aśvagandhā, f. the plant Physalis Flexuosa, Suśr."; API Vol I monograph title AŚVAGANDHĀ; MMPND Sorting Withania, SANSKRIT: Ashvagandha
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate at all, while the name harvested as Hindi is in fact this Sanskrit name. Carrying it in the Sanskrit field with the classical conjunct spelling (-गन्धा) fixes the mis-tagging rather than discarding the name.

discovered.name: वाजिगन्धा
discovered.source: API Vol I, AŚVAGANDHĀ (Withania somnifera Dunal), Sanskrit: Hayagandhā, Vājigandhā
discovered.reason: API's listed Sanskrit synonym; 'horse-smell' by a different word for horse, parallel in sense to अश्वगन्धा.

discovered.name: वराहकर्णी
discovered.source: Monier-Williams p.944, quoted in the Pandanus record for Withania somnifera: "vārāhakarṇī, f. Physalis Flexuosa"; Pandanus Sanskrit list: aśvagandhā, varāhakarṇī
discovered.reason: The second Sanskrit name Pandanus records for the species, attested in Monier-Williams.

discovered.name: पिप्पलः
discovered.source: Monier-Williams p.627, quoted in the Pandanus record for Ficus religiosa: "pippala, m. the sacred fig-tree, Ficus Religiosa (commonly called Peepal) MBh. Yājñ. Var."; API Vol I, AŚVATTHA, Sanskrit: Pippala
discovered.reason: The page carries no Sanskrit candidate. पिप्पलः and अश्वत्थः are the two Sanskrit names Pandanus gives for this species — and अश्वत्थः belongs here, not on the Arjuna and Ashoka pages where it was harvested.

discovered.name: अश्वत्थः
discovered.source: Monier-Williams p.115, quoted in the Pandanus record for Ficus religiosa: "aśvattha, as, m. ... the holy fig tree, Ficus Religiosa, AV.; ŚBr. &c."; API Vol I monograph title AŚVATTHA, botanical source Ficus religiosa Linn.
discovered.reason: This is where the name the batch misassigned three times actually belongs — and the Ashwattha page itself has no Sanskrit candidate.

discovered.name: அரசு
discovered.source: Tamil Lexicon p.118: "அரசு aracu: 01 1. Pipal, l. tr. Ficus religiosa"; API Vol I, AŚVATTHA, Tamil: Arasu; Pandanus, Tamil: aracu, acuvattam
discovered.reason: The base form from which அரசமரம் is built, attested with the binomial by the Lexicon, API and Pandanus.

discovered.name: वज्रवल्ली
discovered.source: API Vol III, ASTHIŚṚṄKHALĀ, Sanskrit: Vajravallī, Chatudhārā; Pandanus record for Cissus quadrangularis, Sanskrit: asthiśṛṅkhalā, vajravallī
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate. API and Pandanus both give this alongside the monograph name अस्थिशृङ्खला.

discovered.name: अतसी
discovered.source: Platts p.76 and p.352 both derive the Hindi names from "[S. अतसी]", printed in Devanagari in the dictionary; API Vol I monograph title ATASĪ, botanical source Linum usitatissimum Linn
discovered.reason: The Sanskrit name the page is titled after, absent from the candidate list, and printed in Devanagari by Platts itself rather than transliterated by me.

discovered.name: ஆளிவிதை
discovered.source: Tamil Lexicon p.255: "ஆளிவிதை āḷi-vitai, n. ஆளி² +. Linseed, flaxseed, Linus usitatissimum", with a Patārttaguṇa 780 citation; the Lexicon's ஆளிவிரை (p.255) is cross-referred to it, and MMPND Sorting Linum gives TAMIL: Aliviraaii
discovered.reason: The seed-name, which matters because the drug in this monograph is the seed; the Lexicon attests both ஆளிவிதை and ஆளிவிரை.

discovered.name: பெருந்துத்தி
discovered.source: Tamil Lexicon p.2876: "பெருந்துத்தி peru-n-tutti, n. 1. Common evening mallow, m. sh., Abutilon indicum" — the only hit in a full-text Lexicon search for 'Abutilon indicum'
discovered.reason: The Lexicon's own name for this exact species, and the precise replacement for the unattested துத்திக்கீரை. The Lexicon assigns bare துத்தி to Abutilon asiaticum, so the பெரு- qualifier is what pins the species.

discovered.name: துத்தி
discovered.source: API Vol I, ATIBALĀ (Abutilon indicum (Linn) Sw), Tamil: Tutti, Thuthi; MMPND Sorting Abutilon, Abutilon indicum, TAMIL: Paniyaratutti, துத்தி Tutti (in Tamil script)
discovered.reason: API's and MMPND's Tamil name for the species, given in Tamil script by MMPND. Worth carrying with the caveat that Tamil Lexicon p.1966 glosses bare துத்தி as Abutilon asiaticum in sense 1.

discovered.name: कंघी
discovered.source: API Vol I, ATIBALĀ, Hindi: Kanghi, Punjabi: Kangi, Kangibooti; MMPND Sorting Abutilon, Abutilon indicum, HINDI: कंघी Kanghi (in Devanagari)
discovered.reason: The Hindi name for this species, missing from the harvested set — the Atibala page has only a Tamil candidate.

discovered.name: अतिबला
discovered.source: API Vol I monograph title ATIBALĀ, botanical source Abutilon indicum (Linn) Sw; MMPND Sorting Abutilon, Abutilon indicum, SANSKRIT: Atibala
discovered.reason: The Sanskrit name the page is titled after, absent from the candidate list.

discovered.name: बब्बूलः
discovered.source: DDSA Practical Sanskrit-English Dictionary and Monier-Williams, per wisdomlib 'babbula': "Babbula (बब्बुल) or Babbūla (बब्बूल).—Acacia Arabica"; MMPND Sorting Acacia, A. nilotica subsp. indica, SANSKRIT: बब्बूलः Babbulaha; Pandanus, Sanskrit: barbura, babbūla
discovered.reason: The correctly formed name that the truncated candidate बब्बु was trying to be, attested in Devanagari by MMPND and in two dictionaries.

discovered.name: बर्बुरः
discovered.source: Pandanus record for Acacia nilotica (L.) Willd. ex Delile, Sanskrit: barbura, babbūla; MMPND Sorting Acacia, A. nilotica subsp. indica, SANSKRIT: Barburah; Monier-Williams attests varvūra = Acacia Arabica citing Amarasiṃha, Halāyudha, Hemacandra
discovered.reason: The b- spelling that Pandanus and MMPND give as the primary form, of which the candidate वर्वुरः is the v- variant.

discovered.name: बावरी
discovered.source: API Vol I, BABBŪLA (Acacia nilotica subsp. indica), Sanskrit: Bāvarī, Kinkirāta
discovered.reason: One of only two Sanskrit synonyms the pharmacopoeia lists for this monograph, and neither appears in the nine harvested Sanskrit candidates.

discovered.name: கருவேல்
discovered.source: Tamil Lexicon p.767: "கருவேல் karu-vēl, n. கரு-மை +. [M. karuvēlam.] Black babul, s. tr., Acacia arabica", with a Patārttaguṇa 462 citation; API Vol I, BABBŪLA, Tamil: Karuvelan, Karuvel
discovered.reason: The Tamil Lexicon's own headword for this species — the single hit in a full-text search for 'Acacia arabica' — and API's second Tamil name. Worth carrying alongside கருவேலம், which the Lexicon tags as the Malayalam cognate.

discovered.name: இலந்தை
discovered.source: Tamil Lexicon p.341: "இலந்தை¹ ilantai, n. [K. elaci, M. ilanda.] Jujube-tree, m. tr., Zizyphus jujuba", with a Tivākaram citation; API Vol III, KOLA (Fruit Pulp), Tamil: Ilandai; Pandanus record for Ziziphus mauritiana, Tamil: ilantai, ilantappaḻam
discovered.reason: The dictionary and pharmacopoeial spelling, against the candidate's எளந்தை which the Lexicon does not carry at all. Three independent sources agree on இலந்தை.

discovered.name: कोली
discovered.source: API Vol III, KOLA (Fruit Pulp), Sanskrit: Kolī, Badarī; Pandanus record for Ziziphus mauritiana, Sanskrit: kola, badara, kolī
discovered.reason: API's first-listed Sanskrit name for the jujube monograph, also in Pandanus; absent from the harvested set, which offers only the fruit-compound बदरीफलम्.

discovered.name: बदरः
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Ziziphus, Ziziphus mauritiana Lam., SANSKRIT: बदर Badara (in Devanagari); Pandanus, Sanskrit: kola, badara, kolī; Platts p.208 derives Hindi बेर from "[S. बदर]", printed in Devanagari
discovered.reason: The name the page is titled after, attested in Devanagari by MMPND and Platts and in transliteration by Pandanus — the species name as against बदरीफलम्, which names the fruit.

discovered.name: अवल्गुजः
discovered.source: API Vol I, BĀKUCĪ (Psoralea corylifolia Linn), Sanskrit: Avalguja, Somarājī
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate; these are the two synonyms API gives for the Bākucī monograph.

discovered.name: वाकुची
discovered.source: Pandanus record for Psoralea corylifolia L., Sanskrit: vākucī
discovered.reason: The Sanskrit form Pandanus gives, with v- and a long first vowel, from which the Hindi बकुची / बाकुची derive.

discovered.name: बकुलः
discovered.source: Pandanus record for Mimusops elengi L., Sanskrit: bakula; Platts p.160 derives the Hindi name from "[S. वकुल]", printed in Devanagari, and Tamil Lexicon p.3450 marks வகுளம் as a loan from Sanskrit vakuḷa
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate. Both the b- and v- spellings are attested — Pandanus gives bakula, Platts prints वकुल.

discovered.name: மகிழம்
discovered.source: Pandanus record for Mimusops elengi L., Tamil: alaku, ilañci, makiḻam; Tamil Lexicon p.3450 cross-refers வகுளம் to மகிழ்³, and p.3574 glosses வாகுலம் as 'Fruit of makiḻ tree; மகிழங் கனி'
discovered.reason: The native Tamil name for the tree, to which the Lexicon itself redirects the Sanskritic வகுளம். This is the form a Tamil speaker would use.

discovered.name: मौलसिरी
discovered.source: Pandanus record for Mimusops elengi L., Hindi: bakul, maulsirī; Platts p.160 gives "syn. maulsarī" in the बकुल entry
discovered.reason: The second Hindi name, attested by both sources; maulsari/maulsiri is in wider everyday use in north India than बकुल.

discovered.name: நிலத்துத்தி
discovered.source: Tamil Lexicon p.2274: "நிலத்துத்தி nila-t-tutti, n. நிலம் +. Downy heart-leaved morning mallow, s. sh., Sida cordifolia" — the single hit in a full-text Lexicon search for 'Sida cordifolia'; IISc India Flora Online herbsheet for Sida cordifolia, Tamil: Nilatutti
discovered.reason: The correct replacement for the rejected சித்தாமுட்டி: the only Tamil name the Lexicon gives for this species, independently corroborated by IISc's India Flora Online.

discovered.name: बला
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Sida, Sida cordifolia L., SANSKRIT: Bala, Balaa; IISc India Flora Online herbsheet for Sida cordifolia, Sanskrit: Bala
discovered.reason: The Sanskrit name the page is titled after; the page carries no Sanskrit candidate at all.

discovered.name: बरियारा
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Sida, Sida cordifolia L., HINDI: Bariara, Baryal; IISc India Flora Online herbsheet for Sida cordifolia, Hindi: Kungyi, Bariyara, Khareti
discovered.reason: The Hindi name, missing from the harvested set — the Bala page has only a Tamil candidate. Both sources give the same word.

discovered.name: சிறுபூளை
discovered.source: Tamil Lexicon p.1463: "சிறுபூளை ciṟu-pūḷai, n. Aerua lanata", with a Cilappatikāram 9.43 citation; API Vol V, PATTŪRA (Whole Plant, Aerva lanata), Tamil: Cherupoolai; Pandanus record for Aerva lanata, Tamil: ceṟupūḷai
discovered.reason: The replacement for the rejected பூளை: three independent sources give the சிறு- compound for Aerva lanata, and the Lexicon reserves bare பூளை for Aerva javanica.

discovered.name: भद्रा
discovered.source: API Vol V, PATTŪRA (Whole Plant), botanical source Aerva lanata, Sanskrit: Gorakṣagañja, Bhadrā; Pandanus record for Aerva lanata (L.) Juss. ex Schult., Sanskrit: bhadrā
discovered.reason: Confirms the page's own title against the right species — useful because API Vol II also has a monograph named BHADRA whose source is a coral tree (Sanskrit Pāribhadraka, Hindi Pangara, Tamil Kalyanamurongai), not Aerva. The feminine भद्रा is the Aerva lanata name.

discovered.name: गोरक्षगञ्जा
discovered.source: API Vol V, PATTŪRA (Whole Plant, Aerva lanata), Sanskrit: Gorakṣagañja, Bhadrā; Pandanus record for Aerva lanata, Hindi: gorakhgāñjā
discovered.reason: API's first-listed Sanskrit name for the species; the page has no Sanskrit candidate.

discovered.name: गोरखगांजा
discovered.source: API Vol V, PATTŪRA (Whole Plant, Aerva lanata), Hindi: Gorakhaganja, Gujarati: Gorakhganjo; Pandanus record for Aerva lanata, Hindi: chāyā, gorakhgāñjā
discovered.reason: The Hindi name for this species, missing from the harvested set — the Bhadra page has only a Tamil candidate.

discovered.name: अरिष्टः
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Azadirachta indica Sanskrit list: अरिष्ट arishta
discovered.reason: Second most common Sanskrit name for neem after निम्ब; also appears as a Hindi name (अरिष्ट) on the same list.

discovered.name: पिचुमन्दः
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Azadirachta indica Sanskrit list: पिचुमन्द picumanda
discovered.reason: Standard classical synonym used in nighantu literature for neem.

discovered.name: पारिभद्रः
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Azadirachta indica Sanskrit and Hindi lists: पारिभद्र paribhadra
discovered.reason: Worth flagging rather than adopting: पारिभद्र is attested for Azadirachta indica AND is the headword of the paribhadra page in this batch, where the same source attests पारिभद्रः for Erythrina variegata. A genuinely shared Sanskrit name; do not treat it as unique to either page.

discovered.name: நிம்பம்
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Azadirachta indica Tamil list: நிம்பம் nimpam
discovered.reason: Tamil reflex of निम्ब, useful alongside வேம்பு.

discovered.name: अङ्कोलः
discovered.source: efloraofindia / Names of Plants in India, Alangium salviifolium: Sanskrit अङ्कोल angkola, अङ्कोलक angkolaka
