discovered.reason: The principal Sanskrit name for this species, absent from the harvested set. Nikochaka, the page slug, is attested on the same list as a secondary Sanskrit synonym.

discovered.name: निकोचक
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Alangium salviifolium Hindi list: निकोचक nikochak
discovered.reason: The page slug itself is attested as a Hindi name, not only Sanskrit; also ढेरा and अंकूल.

discovered.name: அங்கோலம்
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Alangium salviifolium Tamil list: அங்கோலம் ankolam
discovered.reason: Second Tamil name, the reflex of Sanskrit अङ्कोल, widely shared across south Indian languages.

discovered.name: नीलिनी
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Indigofera tinctoria Sanskrit list: नीलिणी nilini
discovered.reason: Closest Sanskrit form to the page slug "nili"; the harvested set carried no Sanskrit candidate at all for this page.

discovered.name: नीलकः
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Indigofera tinctoria Sanskrit list: नीलक nilaka, with रञ्जनी ranjani, श्यामलिका shyamalika, रङ्गपुष्पी rangapushpi
discovered.reason: Attested Sanskrit synonyms for the indigo plant, retrieved directly.

discovered.name: நீலி
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Indigofera tinctoria Tamil list: நீலி nili
discovered.reason: The Tamil form matching the page slug, and the second attested Tamil name after அவுரி.

discovered.name: निर्गुण्डी
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Vitex negundo Hindi list: निर्गुण्ठी nirgunthi; Sanskrit list: निर्गुण्डि nirgundi, निर्गुण्टी nirgunti
discovered.reason: The real Hindi name matching the page headword, to replace the transliterated binomial. सम्भालू sambhalu and निसिन्धु nisindhu are the other common Hindi forms on the same list.

discovered.name: सिन्धुवारः
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Vitex negundo Sanskrit list: सिन्धुवार sindhuvara, सिन्धुक sindhuka, निर्गुण्डि nirgundi, श्वेतसुरसा-group names
discovered.reason: The page had no Sanskrit candidate; सिन्धुवार and निर्गुण्डि are the standard classical names for Vitex negundo.

discovered.name: நொச்சி
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Vitex negundo Tamil list: நொச்சி nocchi, கருநொச்சி karu-nocchi
discovered.reason: The primary Tamil name for Vitex negundo, more useful as a headword than the varietal வெண்ணொச்சி in the harvested set.

discovered.name: निर्गुण्डी
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Vitex negundo: Hindi निर्गुण्ठी, Sanskrit निर्गुण्डि
discovered.reason: Real Hindi name to replace the Devanagari-transliterated binomial on this page.

discovered.name: நொச்சி
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Vitex negundo Tamil list: நொச்சி nocchi
discovered.reason: Primary Tamil name for the species.

discovered.name: बरगद
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Ficus benghalensis Hindi list: बरगद bargad, बड़/बर bar, वट vat
discovered.reason: The actual Hindi name for the banyan, to replace the transliterated binomial. बरगद is the form a Hindi speaker would search.

discovered.name: न्यग्रोधः
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Ficus benghalensis Sanskrit list: न्यग्रोध nyagrodha, alongside वट, वटवृक्ष, भण्डीर, यक्षतरु, यक्षावास
discovered.reason: The page slug is itself an attested Sanskrit name for this species and was missing from the harvested candidates, which carried only वटः.

discovered.name: வசலைக்கீரை
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Spinacia oleracea: Tamil "Vachalaikkirai, Vasaiyilaikkirai"
discovered.reason: The Tamil names the source actually gives for true spinach, in place of the misattributed பசலை கீரை. Given only in roman script on the source, so treat the Tamil spelling as provisional and verify against a Tamil-script authority before publishing.

discovered.name: सागपालक
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Spinacia oleracea: Hindi "पालक Palak, सागपालक Sagpalak"
discovered.reason: Second attested Hindi form.

discovered.name: किंशुकः
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Butea monosperma Sanskrit list: किंशुक kimshuka, पलाश palasha; Flowers of India also gives किंशुक as Hindi
discovered.reason: The main classical Sanskrit synonym for Butea monosperma, missing from the harvested set, which offered only the non-lexical पलाशवृक्षः.

discovered.name: ब्रह्मवृक्षः
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Butea monosperma: Sanskrit "ब्रह्मवृक्ष Brahmavrksha, पलाश Palasha"; efloraofindia adds ब्रह्मपादप, मेघनाद
discovered.reason: Attested Sanskrit synonym read directly in two sources.

discovered.name: ढाक
discovered.source: efloraofindia and Flowers of India, Butea monosperma Hindi lists: ढाक dhak, टेसू tesu
discovered.reason: ढाक and टेसू are the everyday Hindi names, as common as पलाश in north India.

discovered.name: பலாசம்
discovered.source: efloraofindia and Flowers of India, Butea monosperma Tamil lists: பலாசம் palasam, கிஞ்சுகம் kincukam, முருக்கன்மரம் murukkan-maram
discovered.reason: Additional attested Tamil names. Caution: பலாசம் is also attested for Erythrina variegata (the paribhadra page in this batch), so it is not a unique identifier.

discovered.name: पनसम्
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Artocarpus heterophyllus: Sanskrit "पनसम् Panasam"; efloraofindia gives पनसः and पनसम्
discovered.reason: The attested Sanskrit name, to replace the unattested compound पनसफलम् in the harvested set.

discovered.name: पनस
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Artocarpus heterophyllus Hindi list: पनस panas, पूतफल puta-phal, सदाफल sadaphal
discovered.reason: The page slug is attested as a Hindi name as well as Sanskrit.

discovered.name: पारिभद्रः
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Erythrina variegata Sanskrit list: पारिभद्रः paribhadrah, with मन्दारः mandarah, महामेदः mahamedah, विद्रुमः vidrumah
discovered.reason: The page headword is attested Sanskrit for this species and the harvested set contained no Sanskrit candidate at all. Note the clash flagged above: the same source also lists पारिभद्र for Azadirachta indica.

discovered.name: मन्दारः
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Erythrina variegata Sanskrit list: मन्दारः mandarah, मन्दारकः, मन्दारवः
discovered.reason: The other principal classical Sanskrit name for the coral tree.

discovered.name: पांगरा
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Erythrina variegata: Hindi "पंगार Pangara"; efloraofindia Hindi list: पांगरा pangra, मन्दार mandar, महामेद mahamed, पारिभद्र paribhadra
discovered.reason: The page had no Hindi candidate; पांगरा/पंगार is the common Hindi and Marathi name.

discovered.name: முள்ளுமுருக்கு
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Erythrina variegata Tamil list: முள்ளுமுருக்கு mullu-murukku; Wiktionary derives it as முள்ளு + முருக்கு for Erythrina variegata
discovered.reason: The correctly spelled form of the harvested candidate.

discovered.name: கல்யாண முருங்கை
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Erythrina variegata: Tamil "கல்யாண முருஂகை Kalyana murungai"
discovered.reason: The Tamil name Flowers of India gives for this species; a second independent attestation distinct from the murukku form.

discovered.name: शेफालिका
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Nyctanthes arbor-tristis Sanskrit list: शीफालिका shiphalika; Wisdomlib lexicon: Śephālikā is a Sanskrit name of Nyctanthes arbor-tristis
discovered.reason: The correctly spelled Sanskrit/Hindi name, replacing the nuqta-bearing शेफ़ाली in the harvested set.

discovered.name: निशिपुष्पा
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Nyctanthes arbor-tristis Sanskrit list: निशिपुष्पा nishipushpa, शीतमञ्जरी shitamanjari, रजनीहासा rajanihasa, रक्तवृन्ता raktavrnta
discovered.reason: Attested classical Sanskrit synonyms read directly from the per-species list; none were in the harvested set, which offered only the phrase पारिजात वृक्षः.

discovered.name: शिउली
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Nyctanthes arbor-tristis Hindi list: शिउली shiuli, नेवारी newari, केसर kesar, रजनीहासा rajani-hasa
discovered.reason: Additional attested Hindi names, including the eastern form शिउली.

discovered.name: பவளமல்லிகை
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Nyctanthes arbor-tristis Tamil list: பவளமல்லிகை pavala-mallikai, with சேடல் cetal, பாரிசாதம் paricatam
discovered.reason: The fuller attested Tamil spelling of the coral-jasmine name.

discovered.name: पाटल
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Stereospermum chelonoides: Sanskrit "Kastapatala, पाटल Patala"
discovered.reason: Confirms the page headword as the attested Sanskrit name for this species; the harvested set had no Sanskrit candidate.

discovered.name: पतंग
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Caesalpinia sappan: Hindi "Patang, Bakam"; Sanskrit "Patranga, Patanga"
discovered.reason: The real Hindi name, to replace the Devanagari-transliterated binomial. Given in roman on the source, so verify the Devanagari spelling (पतंग / पतङ्ग) before publishing.

discovered.name: पत्रङ्गः
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Caesalpinia sappan: Sanskrit "Patrangah, Patangah"
discovered.reason: The page had no Sanskrit candidate; पत्रङ्ग and पतङ्ग are the attested classical names. Roman-only on the source, so confirm the Devanagari against API before publishing.

discovered.name: पीलु
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Salvadora persica Hindi list: जाल jaal, खरजाल kharjaal, मेस्वाक meswak, पीलु pilu
discovered.reason: The page headword is attested as a Hindi name and the harvested set carried no Hindi candidate at all. जाल is the other widespread Hindi name.

discovered.name: पीलुः
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Salvadora persica Sanskrit list: पीलु pilu, गुडफल gudaphala, शीतसह shitasaha, विरेचन virechana
discovered.reason: Attested Sanskrit name matching the page headword; no Sanskrit candidate was harvested for this page.

discovered.name: பீலு
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Salvadora persica Tamil list: பெருவிளா peru-vila, பீலு pilu, உகாய் ukay
discovered.reason: Second and third attested Tamil names beyond the single harvested candidate.

discovered.name: पिपली
discovered.source: efloraofindia and Flowers of India, Piper longum: Hindi "पिपली Pipli"
discovered.reason: The attested Hindi name, to replace the Sanskrit form पिप्पली that was harvested into the Hindi slot. Do not substitute पीपल, which denotes Ficus religiosa.

discovered.name: मागधी
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Piper longum: Sanskrit "पिप्पली Pippali, Magadhi"
discovered.reason: Classical Sanskrit synonym for long pepper, named for the Magadha provenance that API-derived sources also note. Given in roman on the source, so confirm the Devanagari (मागधी) against API before publishing.

discovered.name: महानिम्बः
discovered.source: MMPND (Univ. of Melbourne), Melia page, Sanskrit line "महानिंब Mahanimbah"; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India monograph title MAHANIMBA for Melia azedarach.
discovered.reason: The correct Sanskrit name, and the one the page slug already transliterates. Replaces the rejected coinage महानिम्बिसस्यम्.

discovered.name: रम्यकः
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MAHANIMBA (Stem Bark) monograph, Sanskrit synonyms "Ramyaka, Dreka".
discovered.reason: Official API Sanskrit synonym for Melia azedarach; absent from the harvested set.

discovered.name: மலை வேம்பு
discovered.source: MMPND Melia page, Tamil line "காட்டு வேம்பூ Kattu vembhu, மலை வேம்பு Malai vembu, Malaivenimpu"; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MAHANIMBA monograph, Tamil "Malaivembu".
discovered.reason: The actual Tamil name for Melia azedarach, in Tamil script from MMPND. Replaces the rejected Sangam-anthology heading.

discovered.name: बकैन
discovered.source: MMPND Melia page, Hindi line "बकैन Bakain"; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MAHANIMBA monograph, Hindi "Bakain, Drek".
discovered.reason: The form API actually romanises, printed in Devanagari by MMPND; a useful alias alongside बकायन.

discovered.name: मञ्जिष्ठा
discovered.source: MMPND Rubia page, Sanskrit line "Gandari, Manjishta, Manjishtha, Manjistha, Manjit, Munjistha"; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India monograph title MANJISTHA for Rubia cordifolia.
discovered.reason: The actual Sanskrit name, and the one the page slug transliterates. Replaces the rejected Devanagari-ised binomial.

discovered.name: मंजीठ
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MANJISTHA (Stem) monograph, Hindi "Manjitha, Manjit" (Urdu "Majeeth"); MMPND Rubia page, Hindi "Majith, Manjit".
discovered.reason: The real Hindi name for Rubia cordifolia, attested by two independent sources. Replaces the rejected Devanagari-ised binomial. मजीठ is an equally current spelling.

discovered.name: மஞ்சிட்டி
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Rubia cordifolia page, Tamil "மஞ்சிட்டி (mancitti)"; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MANJISTHA monograph, Tamil "Manjitte".
discovered.reason: The page has no Tamil candidate at all, yet both API and efloraofindia give one. Worth adding.

discovered.name: मञ्जिष्ठा
discovered.source: MMPND Rubia page, Sanskrit line "Gandari, Manjishta, Manjishtha, Manjistha, Munjistha"; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India monograph title MANJISTHA.
discovered.reason: Same correction as on the manjishtha page; these two slugs are duplicates of one species.

discovered.name: मंजीठ
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MANJISTHA monograph, Hindi "Manjitha, Manjit"; MMPND Rubia page, Hindi "Majith, Manjit".
discovered.reason: The real Hindi name for Rubia cordifolia.

discovered.name: மஞ்சிட்டி
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Rubia cordifolia page, Tamil "மஞ்சிட்டி (mancitti)"; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MANJISTHA monograph, Tamil "Manjitte".
discovered.reason: No Tamil candidate was harvested for this page; this is the attested one.

discovered.name: मातुलुङ्गः
discovered.source: MMPND Citrus medica page, Sanskrit line "... मातुलुङ्ग Matulunga, पूरक Puraka, रुचक Ruchak ..."; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, BIJAPURA (Fresh Fruit) monograph on Citrus medica, Sanskrit "Matulunga".
discovered.reason: The correct Sanskrit name for Citrus medica, and the one this page's slug transliterates. Replaces the rejected नागरङ्गफलम्, which is the orange.

discovered.name: बीजपूरः
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, monograph title BIJAPURA for Citrus medica; MMPND Citrus medica Sanskrit line "बीजाण्‍ड Beejand" (same bīja- stem).
discovered.reason: API's own monograph name for the Citrus medica fruit; the standard second Sanskrit synonym.

discovered.name: बिजौरा
discovered.source: MMPND Citrus medica page, Hindi line "बड़ा नीबु Bara nibu, बिजौरा Bijaura, Khatta, Karna, पूरक Puurak, तुरन्ज Turanj, वेतस Vetas"; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, BIJAPURA monograph, Hindi "Bijoura".
discovered.reason: The page has no Hindi candidate; both authorities give बिजौरा for Citrus medica.

discovered.name: கடரநாரத்தை
discovered.source: MMPND Citrus medica page, Tamil line "Campalam, Campiram, எலுமிச்சை Elumiccai, கடரநாரத்தை Kaṭāranārattai, கொம்மட்டிமாதுளை Kommatti-matulai"; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, BIJAPURA monograph, Tamil "Kadarangai, Turunji Pazham".
discovered.reason: The qualified compound is the Citrus medica name; bare நாரத்தம்பழம் is the bitter orange. This is the correct replacement.

discovered.name: பிசின்பட்டை
discovered.source: India Flora Online (IISc), Litsea glutinosa herbsheet, Tamil "Pisinpatty".
discovered.reason: The only Tamil name an independent authority gives for Litsea glutinosa (literally 'resin bark', matching its use as an incense binder). Replaces the unverified அரம்பா.

discovered.name: मैदा लकड़ी
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MEDASAKAH (Stem Bark) monograph on Litsea chinensis syn. L. glutinosa, Hindi "Maida Lakdee"; India Flora Online (IISc) Hindi "Maidah-lakadi, Maidah, Menda".
discovered.reason: The page harvested no Hindi name at all; this is the standard trade and Ayurvedic Hindi name, attested twice.

discovered.name: मेदसकः
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MEDASAKAH monograph, Sanskrit "Medasakah".
discovered.reason: The page harvested no Sanskrit name; API gives the one the slug transliterates.

discovered.name: திக்கமல்லி
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, NADIHINGU (Exudate) monograph on Gardenia gummifera, Tamil "Tikka malli"; flowersofindia Gummy Gardenia entry, Tamil "kambil, sirukkambil, tikkamalli".
discovered.reason: The real Tamil name, attested twice, replacing the Tamil-script Latin binomial that was harvested.

discovered.name: डिकामाली
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, NADIHINGU monograph, Hindi "Naadihingu, Dikaamaali".
discovered.reason: The page harvested no Hindi name; API gives two, of which डिकामाली is the trade name for the gum.

discovered.name: हिङ्गुनाडिका
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, NADIHINGU monograph, "SYNONYMS : Hingunadika".
discovered.reason: The page harvested no Sanskrit name; this is API's only Sanskrit synonym for the drug.

discovered.name: நாகப்பூ
discovered.source: MMPND Mesua page, Tamil line "... நாகப்பூ (Nāgappū, Nākappū) Nagappu, சிறுநாகப்பூ Ciṟunākappū, நாகேசுரம் Nakecuram, நாங்கு Nāṅku ..."; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, NAGAKESARA monograph, Tamil "Sirunagappu, Naugu, Nagachampakam".
discovered.reason: The Tamil name both authorities give for Mesua ferrea, in Tamil script. Replaces the wiki-only நாகமரம். Since the drug is the stamens, சிறுநாகப்பூ (the flower buds, per MMPND's gloss) is the more exact form.

discovered.name: नागपुष्पः
discovered.source: MMPND Mesua page, Sanskrit line "... नागपुष्प Nagapuspah ..."; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, NAGAKESARA monograph, Sanskrit "Kesara, Nagapuspa, Naga, Hema, Gajakesara".
discovered.reason: Attested Sanskrit synonym by both sources, not in the harvested set.

discovered.name: नागरमोथा
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MUSTA (Rhizome) monograph on Cyperus rotundus, Hindi "Motha, Nagarmotha"; India Flora Online (IISc), Cyperus rotundus sheet, Hindi "Nagarmotha, Motha".
discovered.reason: The form this page is actually named after, attested by both sources, yet absent from the harvested candidates.

discovered.name: मुस्तकम्
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MUSTA monograph, Sanskrit "Mustaka, Varida"; India Flora Online (IISc), Cyperus rotundus sheet, Sanskrit "Mustaka".
discovered.reason: The page harvested no Sanskrit name. मुस्ता / मुस्तकम् is the official API name for Cyperus rotundus and the one classical formulations cite, so its absence is the biggest gap on this page.

discovered.name: கோரைக்கிழங்கு
discovered.source: India Flora Online (IISc), Cyperus rotundus sheet, Tamil "korai, korai kilangu, muthakasu"; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MUSTA monograph, Tamil "Korai, Korai-Kizhangu".
discovered.reason: Names the rhizome specifically, which is the drug this monograph is about, where bare கோரை names the sedge.

discovered.name: मधूकः
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, monograph title MADHUKA for Madhuca indica (= M. longifolia var. latifolia per POWO).
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate at all, though it is named for the Sanskrit term.

discovered.name: गुडपुष्पम्
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MADHUKA (Flower) monograph, Sanskrit synonym "Gudapuspa".
discovered.reason: API's Sanskrit synonym for the flower drug specifically, which is exactly what this page is. The harvested set had no Sanskrit name.

discovered.name: ब्रह्म मंडुकी
discovered.source: MMPND Centella page, Hindi line "ब्रहमामानडुकी Brahma manduki, ब्रह्म मंडुकी Brahma maṇḍukī"; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MANDUKAPARNI monograph, Hindi "Brahma Manduki, Brahmi".
discovered.reason: The actual Hindi name for Centella asiatica from both authorities, in Devanagari. Supplies the genuinely Hindi entry the page lacks, since the harvested मण्डूकपर्णी is Sanskrit. Note API's other Hindi entry, ब्राह्मी, is ambiguous in Hindi usage with Bacopa monnieri and should carry a disambiguating note if used.

discovered.name: माण्डूकी
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MANDUKAPARNI monograph, Sanskrit "Manduki, Darduracchada".
discovered.reason: API's official Sanskrit synonyms for Centella asiatica; neither was harvested.

discovered.name: गुदरी साग
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MATSYAKSI (Whole Plant) monograph on Alternanthera sessilis, Hindi "Gudari Sag"; India Flora Online / efloraofindia listings for Alternanthera sessilis, Hindi "Gudrisag, गूधड़ीसाग, गरूण्डी".
discovered.reason: The page harvested no Hindi name; API gives one.

discovered.name: मत्स्यगन्धा
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MATSYAKSI monograph, Sanskrit "Matsyagandha, Bahli, Matsyaduni, Gandali, Gartkalambuka".
discovered.reason: The page harvested no Sanskrit name despite being titled Matsyakshi; these are API's official synonyms for Alternanthera sessilis.

discovered.name: मेथिनी
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, METHI (Seed) monograph, Sanskrit "Methini"; Rājanighaṇṭu 6.67-69 (via wisdomlib), second synonym "Methinī".
discovered.reason: API's official Sanskrit name for Trigonella foenum-graecum, attested twice, and absent from the harvested set.

discovered.name: मधुरिका
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MISREYA (Fruit) monograph on Foeniculum vulgare, Sanskrit "Misi, Madhurika"; MMPND Foeniculum page, Sanskrit "Madhurika, Shatapushpa".
discovered.reason: The page harvested no Sanskrit name though it is titled Mishreya. मिशि and मधुरिका are API's synonyms. I deliberately exclude MMPND's शतपुष्पा: that name conventionally denotes Anethum graveolens/sowa (dill), and listing it under fennel would reproduce a known conflation.

discovered.name: சோம்பு
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, MISREYA monograph, Tamil "Shombu"; India Flora Online (IISc), Foeniculum vulgare sheet, Tamil "Sopu, Kaattu seeragam"; MMPND Foeniculum page, Tamil "Perun siragum, Shombu, Sohikire".
discovered.reason: Three independent sources give this Tamil name for Foeniculum vulgare, more than for the harvested பெருஞ்சீரகம், and unlike it சோம்பு is not also used for anise. Should sit on the page alongside or ahead of the candidate.

discovered.name: काकमाची
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, monograph title KAKAMACI for Solanum nigrum, Sanskrit synonym "Dhvanksamaci".
discovered.reason: The page harvested no Sanskrit name; काकमाची is the official API name for Solanum nigrum and the standard classical term.

discovered.name: காசினிக்கீரை
discovered.source: Tamil greens and Siddha raw-herb sources (sriharshiniherbals, skorganicfarms, TrueLyf) consistently sell Cichorium intybus leaf as காசினிக்கீரை / காசினி கீரை. Flagged as a commercial, not botanical, source: no botanical compilation I checked gives any Tamil name for this species, so this needs a Siddha Materia Medica check before publishing.
discovered.reason: The real Tamil name for chicory, in place of the rejected சிக்கரி.

discovered.name: हिन्दुबा
discovered.source: Flowers of India / "Names of Plants in India", Chicory page: Hindi "कासनी (Kasni), Hinduba"; efloraofindia gives the same second Hindi name.
discovered.reason: Second attested Hindi name, from the authority directly.

discovered.name: தேத்தாங்கொட்டை
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Strychnos potatorum: Tamil "Thethaangkottai (தேத்தாங்கொட்டை)".
discovered.reason: The form actually used for the seed in Tamil and in Siddha practice; stronger candidate for the Tamil preferred slot than தேற்றா.

discovered.name: निर्मली
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Strychnos potatorum, gives "Hindi/Sanskrit: Nirmali" (romanised on the page; निर्मली is the standard Devanagari of that name).
discovered.reason: The common Hindi and Sanskrit name for the clearing nut, absent from the candidate list which had no Hindi at all.

discovered.name: महावल्कल
discovered.source: efloraofindia, Myrica esculenta: Sanskrit "katphala, mahavalkala" (romanised on the page).
discovered.reason: Second official Sanskrit synonym for the Katphala bark drug.

discovered.name: தாழை
discovered.source: Flowers of India / "Names of Plants in India", Kewda (Pandanus odorifer) page: Tamil "கேதகை (ketakai), தாழை (talai)".
discovered.reason: The everyday Tamil name for screwpine and the better preferred candidate than கைதை.

discovered.name: கேதகை
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Kewda page, Tamil கேதகை; MMPND "Sorting Pandanus names" lists kētakai from the Tamil Lexicon.
discovered.reason: Second attested Tamil name, cognate with the Sanskrit Ketaki.

discovered.name: केवड़ा
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Kewda page: Hindi "गगण धूल (gagan-dhul), केओड़ा (keora), केतकी (ketaki), केंवड़ा (kevara)".
discovered.reason: The candidate list had no Hindi for this page; केवड़ा is the name under which the flower distillate is sold across north India.

discovered.name: पांशुका
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Kewda page: Sanskrit "हनीलः (hanilha), केतकी (ketaki), पांशुका (panshuka)".
discovered.reason: Additional Sanskrit synonym alongside the page's own name Ketaki.

discovered.name: पिण्डखर्जूरम्

discovered.source: efloraofindia.com, Curculigo orchioides: Tamil 'நிலப்பனைக்கிழங்கு nilappanaikkilanku', 'நிலப்பனை nilappanai'
discovered.reason: The attested Tamil name, to replace the Wikipedia-only குறத்தி நிலப்பனை

discovered.name: काली मुसली
discovered.source: efloraofindia.com, Curculigo orchioides: Hindi 'काली मुसली kali musli', 'ताल मूली tal-muli'
discovered.reason: No Hindi candidate was harvested; kali musli is the standard Hindi and trade name

discovered.name: तालमूली
discovered.source: efloraofindia.com, Curculigo orchioides: Sanskrit 'तालमूली talamuli', 'मुसली musali'
discovered.reason: Sanskrit name behind the slug; no Sanskrit candidate was harvested

discovered.name: तामलकी
discovered.source: efloraofindia.com, Phyllanthus fraternus (Bhumyamalaki): Sanskrit 'तमालकी tamalaki', 'भूम्यामलकी bhumyamalaki'
discovered.reason: Sanskrit name behind the slug; no Sanskrit candidate was harvested

discovered.name: भूम्यामलकी
discovered.source: efloraofindia.com, Phyllanthus fraternus: Sanskrit 'भूम्यामलकी bhumyamalaki'
discovered.reason: The principal classical Sanskrit name for this drug

discovered.name: எள்ளு
discovered.source: efloraofindia.com, Sesamum indicum: Tamil 'எள்ளு ellu'
discovered.reason: Common spoken Tamil variant of எள்

discovered.name: திலம்
discovered.source: efloraofindia.com, Sesamum indicum: Tamil 'திலம் tilam'
discovered.reason: Tamil form of the Sanskrit term, used in Siddha texts

discovered.name: सफेद तिल
discovered.source: efloraofindia.com, Sesamum indicum: Hindi 'safed til'
discovered.reason: Hindi name distinguishing the white-seeded sesame of commerce

discovered.name: वृक्षाम्ला
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia species page for Garcinia indica, Sanskrit: वृक्षामला (vrikshamla); corroborated by the Dravyaguna Vigyan "Vrikshamla / Kokum" monograph on sdach.ac.in (Sanskrit name: Vrikshamla) and by the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I Vol V, which titles the monograph Vrikshamla for Garcinia indica.
discovered.reason: This is the actual Sanskrit name the harvest should have had in place of आमेतसवृक्षः. eFloraofIndia spells it वृक्षामला; the standard orthography with the conjunct is वृक्षाम्ला (from वृक्ष + अम्ल, "tree-sour"), which is what I give here. Caveat worth recording on the page: wisdomlib's Vrikshamla entry shows classical nighantu usage (Bhavaprakasha, Amarakosha, Caraka) is contested and sometimes points to Spondias pinnata, so this is the modern API identification, not an undisputed classical one.

discovered.name: अम्लबीजम्
discovered.source: Dravyaguna Vigyan "Vrikshamla / Kokum" monograph, sdach.ac.in, which lists Amlabija among the Sanskrit synonyms for Garcinia indica alongside Raktavrikshamla, Amlapura and Amlashaka.
discovered.reason: Secondary Sanskrit synonym attested in an Ayurvedic college Dravyaguna monograph for this species. Lower confidence than वृक्षाम्ला; include only if the page carries synonym lists.

discovered.name: मत्स्याक्षी
discovered.source: Rajanighantu (13th c.), via wisdomlib's Brahmi entry, which lists 23 synonyms of Brahmi including Matsyakshi, Sarasvati, Somalata, Medhya, Bharati and Parameshthini.
discovered.reason: Genuine classical Sanskrit synonym of the drug Brahmi. Flagging the risk honestly: the Rajanighantu Brahmi entry is itself the locus of the Bacopa / Centella conflation, so some of its 23 synonyms (notably मण्डूकी, मण्डूकमाता) lean to Centella asiatica. मत्स्याक्षी ("fish-eyed", from the leaf shape) is conventionally applied to Bacopa, but I would not publish it without an API cross-check.

discovered.name: सरस्वती
discovered.source: Rajanighantu (13th c.), via wisdomlib's Brahmi entry, where Sarasvati heads the list of 23 synonyms for Brahmi.
discovered.reason: Classical synonym attested for the drug Brahmi. Same caveat as मत्स्याक्षी: the Rajanighantu Brahmi entry covers both Bacopa and Centella traditions, so treat as a drug-level synonym rather than a species-exclusive name.

discovered.name: जव
discovered.source: ayushvedah.com Yava (Hordeum vulgare) monograph, vernacular names table, Hindi: "जव (jav), जौ (jau)".
discovered.reason: Attested secondary Hindi form for barley in the same per-species table that gives जौ. Also the Marathi and Punjabi form, so lower priority than जौ.

discovered.name: धान्यराजः
discovered.source: ayushvedah.com Yava (Hordeum vulgare) monograph, Sanskrit vernacular names: "aksata, akshata, dhanyaraja, divya".
discovered.reason: Sanskrit synonym ("king of grains") listed per species for Hordeum vulgare, not present in the harvested candidates. The same table also gives अक्षत and दिव्य.

discovered.name: अजवाइन
discovered.source: Hindi-language Trachyspermum ammi monograph on drvashishtsayuremedies (sites.google.com/site/drvashishtsayuremedies/ajwain-trachyspermum-ammi): "अजवायन को हिंदी में अजवाइन, ज़वेन कहा जाता है ... इसका वानस्पतिक नाम ट्रकीस्पर्मम् ऐम्मी (Trachyspermum ammi) है"; the Tata 1mg Hindi monograph uses the same spelling.
discovered.reason: This is the correctly spelled Hindi name and should replace the harvested अजवाईन. The variant अजवायन is equally attested in the same source and is the form used in Ayurvedic Hindi writing, so either is defensible; अजवाइन is the commoner search form.

discovered.name: दीप्यकः
discovered.source: Rajanighantu (13th c.) 6.38-40, via wisdomlib's Yavani entry, which opens the fourteen synonyms of Yavani with Dipyaka and Dipya.
discovered.reason: Leading classical Sanskrit synonym for Trachyspermum ammi, absent from the harvested set. The same verse also gives यवानिका, तीव्रगन्धा, उग्रगन्धा and शूलहन्त्री, all worth having for a synonym list.

discovered.name: यवानिका
discovered.source: Rajanighantu (13th c.) 6.38-40, via wisdomlib's Yavani entry, listing Yavanika among the fourteen synonyms of Yavani (Trachyspermum ammi).
discovered.reason: Classical nighantu synonym attested for this exact species; a direct derivative of the monograph name यवानी.

discovered.name: यूथिका
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia species page for Jasminum auriculatum, Sanskrit: यूथिका (Yuthika), also given as Juthika.
discovered.reason: Most valuable discovery in this batch: the page is slugged yuthika but the harvest supplied no Sanskrit candidate at all, so the page would have gone out with its own namesake Sanskrit name missing. Attested per species by a botanical source independent of Wikidata.

discovered.name: உச்சி மல்லிகை
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia species page for Jasminum auriculatum, Tamil: உச்சி மல்லிகை (Uccimalligai), also transliterated Usimalligai; the page distinguishes this from Jathi malli, which is Jasminum grandiflorum.
discovered.reason: The primary Tamil species name, and the one a Tamil speaker or nurseryman would use to name this jasmine specifically rather than jasmine in general. Should be the preferred Tamil form on the page.

discovered.name: முல்லை
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia species page for Jasminum auriculatum, which states that J. auriculatum "is referred to as Mullai in Tamil" while J. grandiflorum is Jathi Malli.
discovered.reason: The classical Tamil name for this species, attested bare, without the மலர் ("flower") suffix the harvest appended. Worth carrying as a secondary Tamil name, with the note that in modern colloquial use முல்லை is applied loosely across jasmines, so உச்சி மல்லிகை is the precise form.

discovered.name: त्रपुषम्
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Cucumis sativus page: 'Sanskrit: Trapushpa, कंटकीलता Kantakilata'; the eFloraofIndia Cucumis sativus notes give त्रपुसम् (trapusam) and त्रपुलम् (trapulam)
discovered.reason: The actual Ayurvedic Sanskrit lemma for this species, and the name the page slug is built from, yet it was absent from the harvested Sanskrit candidates. Should be the preferred Sanskrit name on this page.

discovered.name: कंटकीलता
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Cucumis sativus page: 'Sanskrit: कंटकीलता Kantakilata'
discovered.reason: Given in Devanagari directly by Flowers of India for C. sativus; a second Sanskrit synonym not in the harvested set.

discovered.name: ककड़ी
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Cucumis names, Cucumis sativus: Hindi 'Kheera (khira), Kakri, Kakdi, Tihu'
discovered.reason: A second widely used Hindi name for cucumber, listed by MMPND under C. sativus. Worth carrying because कक्कड़ी/ककड़ी is what the long Indian cucumber is sold as in much of north India.

discovered.name: त्रिवृत्
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Operculina turpethum page: 'Sanskrit: त्रिपुट Triputa, त्रिवृथ Trivrutha, निशोत्र Nishotra'
discovered.reason: The page had no Sanskrit candidate at all, yet Flowers of India gives three in Devanagari. Trivṛt is the official drug name and the page slug.

discovered.name: त्रिपुट
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Operculina turpethum page: 'Sanskrit: त्रिपुट Triputa'
discovered.reason: Second Sanskrit synonym given in Devanagari for this species; fills a page with zero harvested Sanskrit.

discovered.name: கும்பஞ்சான்
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Operculina turpethum page: 'Tamil: கும்பஞ்சான் Kumpncan, சரளம் Caralam, சிவதை Chivatai, பகன்றை Paganrai'
discovered.reason: Additional Tamil-script name attested for this species, read directly off the source.

discovered.name: त्वक्
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Cinnamomum names, Cinnamomum verum: 'Sanskrit: तज Taj, त्वच् Tvak, Darusita'
discovered.reason: The page carried no Sanskrit candidate, yet Tvak is the official API drug name for cinnamon bark and the page slug itself. MMPND gives it in Devanagari.

discovered.name: இலவங்கம்
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Cinnamomum names, Cinnamomum verum: 'Tamil: இலவங்கம் llavangam, கருவா Karuva, லவங்கபட்டை Lavangapattai'
discovered.reason: Second major Tamil name for C. verum, given in Tamil script by MMPND.

discovered.name: जन्तुफलः
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Ficus names, Ficus racemosa Sanskrit list: 'Hemadugdhaka, Jantuphala, Sadaphalah, Udumbar, Udumbara, Yajnanga'; the Udumbara dravyaguna monograph literature gives the same set plus kshiravriksha, kalaskandha, sheetavalka
discovered.reason: A genuine attested nighantu synonym for Ficus racemosa, offered in place of the constructed औदुम्बरवृक्षः that the harvest supplied.

discovered.name: सदाफलः
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Ficus names, Ficus racemosa Sanskrit list: 'Sadaphalah'
discovered.reason: Attested Sanskrit synonym for this species; the name refers to its year-round fruiting.

discovered.name: उपोदिका
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Basella names, Basella alba: 'Sanskrit: Upodika'; corroborated by the Basella alba Ayurvedic reviews which give Upodika, Potaki, Malva and Amritavallari
discovered.reason: The official Ayurvedic Sanskrit name for Basella alba and the page slug, yet it was missing from the harvested Sanskrit candidates, which supplied only the secondary पोतकी. This should be the preferred Sanskrit form.

discovered.name: उग्रगन्धा
discovered.source: Vacha (Acorus calamus) dravyaguna monographs at sdach.ac.in and the Acorus calamus ethnopharmacology review in Front. Pharmacol., which give the synonym set Ugragandha ('offensive nauseating smell'), Golomi/Lomashi/Jatila ('rhizome hairy like cow's hair'), Shadgrantha/Shataparvika ('rhizome with more than six nodes'), Hemavati
discovered.reason: A genuine, semantically motivated Sanskrit synonym for Acorus calamus, offered to replace the rejected वामनी. The etymological gloss in the source ties it to the plant's actual smell, which is the kind of corroboration a bare label cannot give.

discovered.name: षड्ग्रन्था
discovered.source: Vacha dravyaguna monographs (sdach.ac.in) and the Acorus calamus review in Front. Pharmacol.: 'Shataparvika/Shadagrantha: its rhizome has more than 6 nodes'
discovered.reason: Second attested Sanskrit synonym for A. calamus with a recorded morphological basis.

discovered.name: वचा
discovered.source: Flowers of India 'Sweet Flag' page: 'Sanskrit: वचा Vachaa, वाच Vacha, Bhadra'
discovered.reason: The canonical Sanskrit name for the species, given in Devanagari by Flowers of India. The harvested set oddly omitted it and supplied a cotton name instead.

discovered.name: மூங்கில்
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Bambusa names, Bambusa arundinacea (= B. bambos): 'Tamil: Mullumangila, Mulmunkil, Mungil'
discovered.reason: The actual Tamil name of the plant, as opposed to the harvested மூங்கிலிரிசி which names the seed. This page's only candidate had to be rejected, so it has no usable Tamil name without this.

discovered.name: பெருமூங்கில்
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Bambusa bambos ('Indian Thorny Bamboo') page: 'Tamil: குழாய்மூங்கில் kulay-munkil, பெருமூங்கில் peru-munkil'
discovered.reason: Tamil-script name given directly by Flowers of India for this species; 'great bamboo', fitting the giant thorny bamboo.

discovered.name: குழாய்மூங்கில்
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Bambusa bambos page: 'Tamil: குழாய்மூங்கில் kulay-munkil'
discovered.reason: Second Tamil-script name read directly off Flowers of India for B. bambos.

discovered.name: बांस
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Bambusa bambos page: 'Hindi: बांस baans, बम्बू bambu, बंस buns'
discovered.reason: The page had no Hindi candidate at all. बांस is the universal Hindi name and Flowers of India gives it in Devanagari for this species.

discovered.name: वंशः
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Bambusa bambos page: 'Sanskrit: आमुपः amupah, आर्द्रपत्रकः ardrapatrakah, कण्टकः kantakah, कण्टकिलः kantakilah, वम्भः vambhah, वंशः vamsh'
discovered.reason: The page had no Sanskrit candidate although वंशः is the page slug itself. Flowers of India supplies it and four more in Devanagari.

discovered.name: कण्टकिलः
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Bambusa bambos page: 'Sanskrit: कण्टकिलः kantakilah'
discovered.reason: Attested Sanskrit synonym in Devanagari, apt for the thorny species specifically rather than bamboo in general.

discovered.name: वनप्सा
discovered.source: Planet Ayurveda monograph 'Viola odorata Linn./Banafasha' and the Banafsha review literature, which give 'Sanskrit: Jvarapaha, Nilapushpa, Sukshmapatra, Vanapsa'
discovered.reason: The page had no Sanskrit candidate although Vanapsa is the page slug. Named Ayurvedic monograph sources attest it for Viola odorata.

discovered.name: नीलपुष्पा
discovered.source: Planet Ayurveda monograph for Viola odorata Linn.: 'Sanskrit: Jvarapaha, Nilapushpa, Sukshmapatra, Vanapsa'
discovered.reason: Second Sanskrit synonym attested for V. odorata by a named monograph; descriptive of the blue-violet flower.

discovered.name: रतालू
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Dioscorea names, Dioscorea bulbifera: 'Hindi: Gaithi, Hoei oepas, Ratalu, Karukanda, Karu kunda'
discovered.reason: The page had no Hindi candidate. MMPND attests Ratalu and Gaithi for D. bulbifera specifically; गेंठी and रतालू are the common north Indian names for this yam.

discovered.name: காய்வள்ளி
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Dioscorea names, Dioscorea bulbifera: 'Tamil: காய்வள்ளி Kaayvalli, காட்டுச்சீரகவள்ளி, காட்டுக்காய்வள்ளி Kaattukkaayvalli, Pannu kilangu'
discovered.reason: Given in Tamil script by MMPND for this species and much better attested than the harvested பண்ணுக்கிழங்கு, so it should be the preferred Tamil form.

discovered.name: காட்டுக்காய்வள்ளி
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Dioscorea names, Dioscorea bulbifera, Tamil list; also Dinesh Valke's Names of Plants in India photo record 'Kaattukkaayvalli (Tamil: காட்டுக்காய்வள்ளி)' for D. bulbifera
discovered.reason: Second Tamil-script name attested for D. bulbifera by two independent records.

discovered.name: वाराहीकन्दः
discovered.source: Dioscorea bulbifera Ayurvedic monographs (easyayurveda, ayushvedah drug record for barahi / Dioscorea bulbifera Linn.), which give Sanskrit Varahikanda, Aluka, Pindalu and the etymology 'Varahasya iyam priyatvat iti Varahi', dear to the boar, the tuber resembling a boar's face
discovered.reason: The page had no Sanskrit candidate although Varahikanda is the page slug. Named monograph sources attest it with its etymology for this species.

discovered.name: वासा
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Justicia names, Justicia adhatoda: 'Sanskrit: ... वासा Vasa, वासक Vasaka, Vasika'; wisdomlib's Vasaka entry gives वासक for Adhatoda vasica citing Rāj Nighaṇṭu
discovered.reason: The correctly spelled Sanskrit name, with long ā, for this species. All four harvested Sanskrit candidates were either a different plant or misspellings of this one, so the page needs it.

discovered.name: सिंहास्यः
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Justicia names, Justicia adhatoda Sanskrit list includes 'सिंहमुखी Simhamukhi, सिंही Simhi, सिंहिका Simhika, सिंहपर्णी Sinhaparni'; the Bhāvaprakāśa synonym set reported in the Adhatoda vasica reviews gives Simhasya, Simhika, Simhaparna, Vajidanta, Bhishangmata, Atarusha
discovered.reason: A genuine classical synonym group for Vāsā, given in Devanagari by MMPND, naming the lion-mouth shape of the corolla. Far more useful on the page than the harvested compounds.

discovered.name: कफहारी
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Justicia names, Justicia adhatoda: 'Sanskrit: कफाहारी Kaphahari'
discovered.reason: Attested Sanskrit synonym in Devanagari for this species, recording its expectorant use, which is the API indication for the drug.

discovered.name: अटरूषः
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Justicia names, Justicia adhatoda: 'Sanskrit: अटरुष Atrusha'; corroborated by the Bhāvaprakāśa synonym set in the Adhatoda reviews (Atarush, Atarushaka)
discovered.reason: Attested Sanskrit synonym in Devanagari, and the source of the Unani/Hindi 'Arusa' forms, which links the Sanskrit and Hindi name sets on the page.

discovered.name: अडुळसा
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Justicia names, Justicia adhatoda Hindi list: 'अडुळसा Adulsa, अडुसा Adusa, अर्शा Arusa'
discovered.reason: Additional Devanagari Hindi name read directly off MMPND for this species.

discovered.name: अडूसा
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Justicia names, Justicia adhatoda Hindi list: 'अडुसा Adusa, अडुळसा Adulsa, Adosa, Adulasa, Adus, अर्शा Arusa, Arusha'
discovered.reason: This page's only Hindi candidate had to be rejected, leaving it with no Hindi name. अडूसा is the attested everyday Hindi name for Justicia adhatoda and should be used.

discovered.name: वासकः
discovered.source: wisdomlib Vasaka entry: Devanagari वासक, identified as Adhatoda vasica = Justicia adhatoda (Acanthaceae), citing Rāj Nighaṇṭu and Mādhavacikitsā; MMPND also lists Sanskrit 'वासक Vasaka'
discovered.reason: This page had no Sanskrit candidate at all even though its slug is Vasaka. The correctly spelled Devanagari form, attested by a named nighantu.

discovered.name: बादाम
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Prunus dulcis ('Almond') page: 'Hindi: बादाम Badam, बदाम'
discovered.reason: The real Hindi name, in Devanagari, for the plant this page is about, replacing the descriptive phrase बादाम का पेड that the harvest supplied.

discovered.name: बाबरंग
discovered.source: Embelia ribes reviews in IJPSR ('Importance of Embelia ribes: An Update') and the Medicinal Plants compilation for E. ribes, giving Hindi 'Baberang, Karkannie, Vayvarang, Viranga'
discovered.reason: The commonest Hindi market name for the drug, attested for E. ribes by named review sources; absent from the harvested set.

discovered.name: विडङ्गः
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Embelia ribes ('Vidang') page: 'Sanskrit: आमोघः Amogha, मोघा Mogha, विडङ्गः Vidang'
discovered.reason: The page had no Sanskrit candidate. Flowers of India gives the proper Sanskrit spelling विडङ्गः in Devanagari, distinct from the Hindi विडंग the harvest supplied.

discovered.name: आमोघः
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Embelia ribes page: 'Sanskrit: आमोघः Amogha, मोघा Mogha'
discovered.reason: Second Sanskrit synonym given in Devanagari for E. ribes by Flowers of India.

discovered.name: भूमिकुष्माण्डः
discovered.source: Planet Ayurveda and IAFA monographs for Pueraria tuberosa DC.: 'Sanskrit: भूमिकुष्माण्ड Bhumikusmanda, गजवाजिप्रिया Gajavajipriya, कन्दपलाश Kandapalash, स्वादुकन्दा Svadukanda, विदारी Vidari, इक्षुगन्धा Ikshugandha'
discovered.reason: The page had no Sanskrit candidate. Bhūmikuṣmāṇḍa is the classical name, given with the explanation that the plant bears a large underground tuber.

discovered.name: विदारी
discovered.source: Planet Ayurveda monograph for Pueraria tuberosa DC.: 'Sanskrit: विदारी Vidari'
discovered.reason: The Sanskrit form behind the page slug 'vidari', attested in Devanagari for this species by a named monograph.

discovered.name: நிலப்பூசணி
discovered.source: Planet Ayurveda and IAFA monographs for Pueraria tuberosa DC., which give 'Tamil: Nilapoosani'
discovered.reason: The page had no Tamil candidate. Nilappūsaṇi, 'ground pumpkin', is the Tamil name these monographs give for P. tuberosa and parallels the Sanskrit Bhūmikuṣmāṇḍa and Telugu Nelagummuda, which cross-corroborates it. Flagging that the Tamil script spelling is my rendering of the sources' transliteration and should be checked against a Tamil-script authority.

discovered.name: विजयसार
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Pterocarpus marsupium ('Indian Kino Tree') page: 'Hindi: विजयसार Vijayasara, बीज पत्ता Beeja patta, Bijasal, Bila'
discovered.reason: The genuine Hindi name in Devanagari, matching the page slug, to replace the Devanagari-spelled Latin binomial the harvest supplied.

discovered.name: बीजसार
discovered.source: MMPND Sorting Pterocarpus names, P. marsupium Hindi list: 'Bija, Bijasal, Bijasar, Bijaisaar kaashtha, Vijaisar kaashthaa'; corroborated by the Pterocarpus marsupium pharmacology reviews ('Hindi: Bijasar')
discovered.reason: The commonest Hindi trade name for the heartwood drug, attested by two independent sources for this species.

discovered.name: असनः
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Pterocarpus marsupium page: 'Sanskrit: Asana, Beejaka, Petaca, Bandhukavriksha'; MMPND Sanskrit list: 'Asana, Bijaka, Bijavriksha, Priyaka, Pitasara, Mahasarja' and others
discovered.reason: The page had no Sanskrit candidate. Asana is the API/classical drug name for P. marsupium, attested by two independent sources.

discovered.name: बीजकः
discovered.source: Flowers of India, Pterocarpus marsupium page: 'Sanskrit: Beejaka'; MMPND P. marsupium Sanskrit list: 'Bijaka, Bijavriksha'
discovered.reason: Second classical Sanskrit synonym attested for this species by two sources; it is the root of the Hindi बीजसार/Bijasal name set.

discovered.name: पिपली
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Piper longum, Hindi: पिपली (Pipli)
discovered.reason: The actually attested Hindi form, as against the Sanskrit पिप्पली that was harvested into the Hindi field.

discovered.name: पिपरामूल
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, PIPPALIMULA (Stem) = Piper longum Linn., Hindi: 'Piparamula'
discovered.reason: This page is Pippali Moola, the root drug, and this is API's Hindi name for that drug specifically. API prints it romanised; the Devanagari spelling is given here. Highest-value Hindi name for this page.

discovered.name: मागधी
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, PIPPALI = Piper longum, Sanskrit synonyms 'Kana, Magadhi, Magadha, Krsna, Saundi'; PIPPALIMULA Sanskrit 'Magadhi, Granthika, Pippalika'
discovered.reason: API's first-listed Sanskrit synonym for both the fruit and the root of this species. Romanised in API; Devanagari given here.

discovered.name: चकवंड
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Senna tora, Hindi: चकूंदा, चकवंड, एड़गज, पद्माट, पंवार, प्रपुनाट, तर्किल
discovered.reason: Attested Hindi in Devanagari; the chakvad/chakunda group is the common Hindi name and should replace the unattested पोहाड़.

discovered.name: पंवार
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Senna tora, Hindi: पंवार. Corroborated by API PRAPUNNADA Hindi 'Pavand', Punjabi 'Panwal', Urdu 'Panwar'
discovered.reason: The form closest to what the harvested पोहाड़ was probably trying to be, and attested across four languages in API.

discovered.name: चक्रमर्दकः
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Senna tora, Sanskrit: चक्रमर्दकः, दद्रुघ्नः, एडगजः, पद्मटः, प्रपुनाट
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate at all; चक्रमर्द is the standard Ayurvedic name for this drug and दद्रुघ्नः/एडगजः are in API's Sanskrit field too.

discovered.name: சாரம்
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Buchanania lanzan, Tamil: சாரம் (charam), காட்டுமா (kattuma). Corroborated by API PRIYALA Tamil 'Saarapparuppu'
discovered.reason: The attested Tamil for this species, replacing the rejected புளிமா.

discovered.name: காட்டுமா
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Buchanania lanzan, Tamil: காட்டுமா
discovered.reason: Second attested Tamil name in native script for this species.

discovered.name: पियाल
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Buchanania lanzan, Sanskrit: अखट्ट, बहुकल्क, धनु, धनुष्पट, पियाल, प्रसवक, राजादन. Corroborated by API PRIYALA Sanskrit 'Priyala, Carah, Kharaskandhah'
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate; पियाल/प्रियाल is the classical name and matches the page slug.

discovered.name: सुपारी
discovered.source: Names of Plants in India, Areca catechu, Hindi list; API Part I, PUGA (Seed) = Areca catechu Linn., Hindi: 'Supari, Chaalia'
discovered.reason: The Hindi name a speaker actually uses and searches. None of the nine harvested candidates was this, so the page currently has no usable Hindi name even though five candidates confirmed.

discovered.name: पूगः
discovered.source: Names of Plants in India, Areca catechu, Sanskrit: पूगः, पूगफल, पूगी, अकोटः, वल्कतरुः, उद्वेग; API monograph title PUGA (Seed) = Areca catechu
discovered.reason: The standard Sanskrit lemma and the page name itself, as against the unattested compound पूगवृक्षः.

discovered.name: क्रमुकः
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, PUGA (Seed) = Areca catechu Linn., Sanskrit synonyms: 'Kramuka, Ghonta'
discovered.reason: API's official Sanskrit synonym for this monograph; romanised in API, Devanagari given here. Corroborated by kosha.sanskrit.today, which returns क्रमुकफल for 'areca nut palm'.

discovered.name: கமுகு
discovered.source: Names of Plants in India, Areca catechu, Tamil: அடைக்காய், சகுந்தம், சாமரபுட்பம், கமுகு, கந்தி, கூந்தற்கமுகு, பூகம், விம்பு. Corroborated by API PUGA Tamil 'Kamugu, Pakku, Pakhumaram'
discovered.reason: The page had no Tamil candidate at all. கமுகு is the Tamil name for the areca palm, attested by two sources.

discovered.name: அடைக்காய்
discovered.source: Names of Plants in India, Areca catechu, Tamil: அடைக்காய் (atai-k-kay)
discovered.reason: Attested Tamil name for the areca nut itself, which is this page's drug (the seed).

discovered.name: लाल चंदन
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, RAKTACANDANA (Heart Wood) = Pterocarpus santalinus Linn. f., Hindi: 'Raktachandanam, Lalchandana'; Punjabi 'Lal Chandan', Gujarati 'Ratanjali, Lalchandan'
discovered.reason: API's second Hindi name, romanised there; it is the form most Hindi speakers use and search, so it is a defensible alternative preferred Hindi name to the harvested रक्त चंदन.

discovered.name: क्षुद्रचन्दनम्
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, RAKTACANDANA = Pterocarpus santalinus, Sanskrit synonyms: 'Raktanga, Ksudracandana, Raktasara'
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate; this is one of API's official Sanskrit synonyms (romanised in API, Devanagari given here), alongside the monograph name रक्तचन्दन.

discovered.name: रसोनम्
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, LASUNA (Bulb) = Allium sativum Linn., Sanskrit synonyms: 'Rasona, Yavanesta'
discovered.reason: The page slug is rasona and API attests रसोन as a Sanskrit synonym for this species, so it belongs on the page explicitly rather than only in the slug. Romanised in API; Devanagari given here.

discovered.name: வெள்ளைப்பூண்டு
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, LASUNA (Bulb) = Allium sativum Linn., Tamil: 'Vellaipoondu'
discovered.reason: API's full Tamil name for the species, which disambiguates from the generic sense of bare பூண்டு ('any small plant') recorded in the Madras Lexicon.

discovered.name: रसोनम्
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, LASUNA (Bulb) = Allium sativum Linn., Sanskrit synonyms: 'Rasona, Yavanesta'
discovered.reason: Same as the rasona-garlic page: API attests रसोन for this species and it is the page slug.

discovered.name: வெள்ளைப்பூண்டு
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, LASUNA (Bulb) = Allium sativum, Tamil: 'Vellaipoondu'
discovered.reason: API's full Tamil name for the species.

discovered.name: உலக்கைப்பாலை
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Manilkara hexandra, Tamil: உலக்கைப்பாலை (ulakkai-p-palai)
discovered.reason: The attested Tamil name for this species in native script, replacing the rejected bare பாலை.

discovered.name: राजादन
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Manilkara hexandra, Sanskrit: क्षीरिणी, निम्बबिज, राजादन
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate. राजादन is the classical Sanskrit name for this species, which is also why the page's own name Rishabhaka deserves re-examination.

discovered.name: रायन
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Manilkara hexandra, Hindi: दृढ़, खिरनी, क्षीरी, रायन
discovered.reason: Second attested Hindi name in Devanagari for this species, widespread in Gujarat and Maharashtra as rayan.

discovered.name: दाडिमपुष्प
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, ROHITAKA (Stem Bark) = Tecomella undulata (Sm.) Seem., 'SYNONYMS : Dadima puspa, Dadimacchada'
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate; these are API's two official Sanskrit synonyms for this monograph. Romanised in API; Devanagari given here.

discovered.name: रुद्राक्ष
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, monograph title RUDRAKSA (Seed) = Elaeocarpus sphaericus Gaertn. K. Schum
discovered.reason: API names its monographs by the official Sanskrit drug name, so रुद्राक्ष is attested Sanskrit for this taxon. The page currently has no Sanskrit or Hindi candidate at all.

discovered.name: सैरीयकः
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Barleria strigosa, Sanskrit: आर्तगलः, बाण, दासी कुरण्टकः, नीलझिंटी, सहचरः, सैरीयकः and others. Corroborated by API NILAJHINTI (Root) = Barleria strigosa Willd., Sanskrit: 'Dasi, Bana, Krsna, Saireyakah, Nilasaireyakah'
discovered.reason: Confirms the page's own name against this species in two independent sources, and the page carries no Sanskrit candidate.

discovered.name: नीलझिंटी
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia, Barleria strigosa, Sanskrit: नीलझिंटी; API titles its Barleria strigosa monograph NILAJHINTI
discovered.reason: API's official Sanskrit drug name for this species, attested in Devanagari by eFloraofIndia.

discovered.name: कर्बुदार
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Barleria strigosa, Hindi: कर्बुदार (karbu-dar)
discovered.reason: The page has no Hindi candidate. API's Hindi for this species is additionally 'Nili, Katsaraiya'.

discovered.name: अश्वकर्ण
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia, Shorea robusta, Sanskrit: agnivallabha, ashvakarna, ashvakarnika
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate beyond its own name. Romanised in that source; Devanagari given here. API's Sanskrit synonym field for SALA gives only 'Sala'.

discovered.name: सखुआ
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, SALA (Heart Wood) = Shorea robusta Gaertn., Hindi: 'Saal, Sakhuaa, Saakhu'; eFloraofIndia notes the tree 'is known also as sakhua in northern India'
discovered.reason: The second Hindi name for this species across Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Jharkhand; romanised in both sources, Devanagari given here.

discovered.name: चितवन
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Alstonia scholaris, Hindi: बहुपुत्र, चतवन, चितवन, सप्तपर्णी, शैतान का झाड़, शारदी. Corroborated by API SAPTAPARNA Hindi 'Chhativan, Satawana'
discovered.reason: The genuinely Hindi name for this species, attested in Devanagari, to replace the Sanskrit सप्तपर्ण that was harvested into the Hindi field.

discovered.name: सप्तपर्णी
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Alstonia scholaris, Hindi: सप्तपर्णी
discovered.reason: If a saptaparṇa-type name is wanted in the Hindi field, this is the form the source actually labels Hindi.

discovered.name: सप्तच्छद
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Alstonia scholaris, Sanskrit: सप्तच्छद, सप्तपर्ण, बहुपर्ण, छत्त्रपर्ण, विषमच्छद and others. Corroborated by API SAPTAPARNA Sanskrit 'Saptacchada, Saptaparni, Saptahva'
discovered.reason: API's first Sanskrit synonym for this monograph, attested in Devanagari by eFloraofIndia. The page has no Sanskrit candidate, and सप्तपर्ण itself belongs in this field.

discovered.name: இருள்பாலை
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Alstonia scholaris, Tamil: ஏழிலைப்பாலை, இருள்பாலை
discovered.reason: Second attested Tamil name in native script for this species.

discovered.name: सारिवा
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, SVETA SARIVA (Root) = Hemidesmus indicus (Linn.) R. Br., Sanskrit synonyms: 'Ananta, Gopasuta, Sariva'
discovered.reason: API's attested Sanskrit for this species and the page's own name, to replace the rejected क्षीरिणीसस्यम्. Romanised in API; Devanagari given here.

discovered.name: अनन्ता
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, SVETA SARIVA = Hemidesmus indicus, Sanskrit: 'Ananta', with Hindi/Bengali/Marathi/Punjabi all giving anantamul
discovered.reason: API's first Sanskrit synonym for this monograph, and the root of the confirmed Hindi अनंतमूल.

discovered.name: வெள்ளைக்குங்கிலியம்
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Vateria indica, Tamil: துருளக்கம், வெள்ளைக்குங்கிலியம். Corroborated by API SARJA (Exudate) = Vateria indica Linn., Tamil: 'Kungiliyam, Vellai Kuntarakam, Vellai Kundarakam'
discovered.reason: The attested Tamil name in native script, replacing the rejected Malayalam பயினி. The வெள்ளை- qualifier is what distinguishes this resin from Shorea robusta's.

discovered.name: துருளக்கம்
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Vateria indica, Tamil: துருளக்கம் (turulakkam)
discovered.reason: Second attested Tamil name in native script, and unlike குங்கிலியம் it is not shared with Shorea robusta.

discovered.name: सर्जकः
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Vateria indica, Sanskrit: सर्जकः (sarjakah)
discovered.reason: Attested Sanskrit in Devanagari for this species, confirming the page's own name. API's Sanskrit synonyms for SARJA are additionally Devdhupa, Karsya, Sasyasumbara and Ajakarna.

discovered.name: सफेद डामर
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Vateria indica, Hindi: कहरुबा, सफेद डामर. Corroborated by API SARJA Hindi 'Sandras, Safed Damar'
discovered.reason: The page has no Hindi candidate; this is attested in Devanagari by one source and romanised in API, and 'white dammar' is how the resin is traded.

discovered.name: नाकुली
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Rauvolfia serpentina, Sanskrit: चन्द्रिका, नाकुली, पातालगरुड, सर्पगंधा. Corroborated by API SARPAGANDHA Sanskrit 'Nakuli, Candrika, Chandramarah'
discovered.reason: Attested in Devanagari by one source and romanised in API, for exactly this species. Replaces the malformed सर्पगन्धः together with सर्पगन्धा.

discovered.name: चन्द्रिका
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia, Rauvolfia serpentina, Sanskrit: चन्द्रिका; API SARPAGANDHA Sanskrit 'Candrika'
discovered.reason: Second Sanskrit name attested for this species by both sources.

discovered.name: छोटा चांद
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Rauvolfia serpentina, Hindi: चन्द्रभाग, छोटा चांद, नाकुली, सर्पगंधा. Corroborated by API SARPAGANDHA Hindi 'Chhotaa Chaand, Dhavalbaruaa'
discovered.reason: API's first Hindi name for this species, attested in Devanagari by eFloraofIndia. It is the older Hindi name and worth carrying alongside सर्पगंधा.

discovered.name: भरभांड
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia and Names of Plants in India, Argemone mexicana, Hindi: भरभांड (bharbhand)
discovered.reason: The primary spelling in the source for the name harvested as भड़भाड़; publish this form.

discovered.name: स्वर्णक्षीरी
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Argemone mexicana, Sanskrit: ब्रह्मदण्डी, हेमदुग्ध, हेमशिखा, कान्चक्षीरी, कटुपर्णी, पीतदुग्धा, सृगालकण्टक, स्वर्णक्षीरी
discovered.reason: The page has no Sanskrit candidate. स्वर्णक्षीरी is the usual Ayurvedic name for this drug (from its golden latex) and is attested in Devanagari.

discovered.name: ब्रह्मदण्डी
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Argemone mexicana, Sanskrit: ब्रह्मदण्डी (brahmadandi)
discovered.reason: Attested Sanskrit in Devanagari, and the source of the confirmed Tamil பிரம்மத் தண்டு, which makes the pair mutually corroborating.

discovered.name: குடியோட்டுப்பூண்டு
discovered.source: eFloraofIndia / Names of Plants in India, Argemone mexicana, Tamil: எலியோட்டி, குருக்கு, குடிக்குச்சகுனி, குடியோட்டுப்பூண்டு, பிரம்மத் தண்டு
discovered.reason: Attested Tamil name in native script, and the kudiyotti group appears to be the more current Tamil usage for this weed.

discovered.name: स्वर्णपत्री
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, monograph title SVARNAPATRI (Leaf) = Cassia angustifolia Vahl. Corroborated by IISc Flora of Peninsular India herbsheet for Senna alexandrina, Sanskrit: 'Svarnapatri, Sunamuki'
discovered.reason: API's official Sanskrit drug name for this species, corroborated by an academic flora. The page has no Sanskrit candidate at all. Romanised in both sources; Devanagari given here.

discovered.name: सनाय
discovered.source: IISc Flora of Peninsular India herbsheet, Senna alexandrina, Hindi: 'Sanay'. Corroborated by API SVARNAPATRI Hindi: 'Sanaya, Hindisana'
discovered.reason: The page has no Hindi candidate; sanay/sanaya is API's Hindi name for this species. Romanised in both sources; Devanagari given here.

discovered.name: நிலப்பொன்னை
discovered.source: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, SVARNAPATRI (Leaf) = Cassia angustifolia Vahl, Tamil: 'Nilapponnai, Avarai'. Corroborated by IISc Flora of Peninsular India, Senna alexandrina, Tamil: 'Ponnavari'
discovered.reason: API's first Tamil name for this species, and unlike நிலாவாரை it is not shared with Senna auriculata and Senna italica. Romanised in both sources; Tamil script given here.
